findings.title: The test-naming examples use a 'should …' prefix that Layer 2 and most current specs don't use
findings.current: testing.md:9-11 gives these as the 'Good' examples: "`should reject moves after game is finalized`" and "`should return the winner when both players have submitted`"
findings.truth: The Layer 2 example writes titles as present-tense behaviour phrases with no 'should', e.g. it('accepts supported moves') and it('rejects unsupported moves'). The org codebases mostly do the same. No ESLint test-title rule enforces either style, because eslint-config-flat ships no vitest or jest plugin.
findings.evidence: skills/xy-toolchain/testing.md:204-211 (it('accepts supported moves'), it('rejects unsupported moves')). I counted it()/test() titles in *.spec.ts(x) files, excluding node_modules, dist and .claude. Add one line: 'Match the repository's existing title style; a `should` prefix is optional — what matters is that the title states the expected behavior.' This keeps Layer 1 consistent with the Layer 2 example.

findings.title: No principle says tests must be independent, order-free and deterministic, which the standard runner setup assumes
findings.current: absent. testing.md covers naming, AAA, one concept, public interface, mocking and coverage. It mentions determinism only as a reason to mock the clock or randomness (testing.md:51).
findings.truth: Under the org preset, spec files run file-parallel by default. A spec under a plain spec/ folder runs in both the Node project and the real-browser project. Only explicitly serialized projects turn file parallelism off, and those are meant for e2e suites that share external state. So by default tests must not share mutable state, depend on run order or assume one runtime.
findings.evidence: toolchain/packages/vitest-config/src/defineXyVitestProjects.ts:47-50 ('spec/ — runs in BOTH realms'). toolchain/packages/vitest-config/src/defineXySerializedProject.ts:5-9,18 (serialized 'for e2e-style suites that share external state', fileParallelism: false only there). `node packages/toolchain/dist/bin/xy.mjs test --help` shows '-j, --jobs Max parallel jobs [default: 16]'. toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/test.ts:8-15 (xy test runs `vitest <path>` with the root projects config).
findings.recommendation: Add a short framework-agnostic section, 'Independent and Deterministic Tests'. Each test sets up and tears down its own state. Tests must pass in any order and when test files run concurrently. Never depend on wall-clock time, network or shared external state such as files, ports, chains or stores without controlling it. Keep slow or stateful end-to-end suites separate from fast unit tests. Add one sentence pointing to xy-toolchain → Testing with Vitest for runner specifics. Test files run in parallel by default. File placement picks the Node or browser realm when a browser project is configured. defineXySerializedProject declares serialized suites. Cite the Vitest fileParallelism default, not xy's global --jobs flag.

verify.code: adjusted: The core claim is real. Vitest 5.0.3 defaults fileParallelism to true (node_modules/vitest/dist/chunks/cac.DfDGTQ9W.js:937 says 'default: `true`', and index.DpLw24bj.js:14438 uses '?? true'). defineXyVitestConfig.ts:14-23 sets only watch:false and projects, so it never overrides this. Only defineXySerializedProject.ts:18 sets fileParallelism:false, and its doc comment (lines 5-9) says it is for e2e suites that share external state. Two pieces of evidence are wrong. First, '-j, --jobs' is a global xy option (packages/toolchain/src/xy/xyParseOptions.ts:88-93) that only prints a thread count. actions/test.ts:8-15 never passes it to vitest, so it says nothing about test parallelism. Second, 'spec/ runs in both realms' holds only when a browser project is configured. defineXyVitestProjects.ts:59 adds the browser project only if options.browser is set, and it is omitted by default. The skill does not currently state the principle (testing.md:51 mentions determinism only as a reason to mock). Low severity and the add action are right.
verify.skill: confirmed: No part of xy-development or xy-toolchain says tests must be independent, order-free or concurrency-safe. A grep for independen|isolat|any order|parallel|shared state|global state|determinis finds only testing.md:51 (mocking the clock or randomness), git.md:39 (each commit passes tests on its own) and unrelated toolchain lines. The source supports the claim. toolchain/packages/vitest-config/src/defineXyVitestProjects.ts:47-50 routes plain spec/ files to both realms when a browser project is enabled. defineXySerializedProject.ts:5-9,18 sets fileParallelism: false only for e2e suites 'that share external state'. The node and browser projects leave Vitest's default file parallelism on. One piece of evidence does not hold: `xy test --jobs` (default 16) is a global option, and packages/toolchain/src/actions/test.ts:8-15 never passes it to vitest. File parallelism comes from Vitest's own default, not from --jobs. The core finding and the recommendation are correct, framework-agnostic and in the right layer, and low severity fits.

findings.title: The documented default include glob for @ariestools/vitest-config is outdated as of v10.1.0
findings.current: skills/xy-toolchain/testing.md:73 says "Default include: `packages/*/src/**/spec/**/*.spec.ts`." The table at :77 gives the same.
findings.truth: The published v10.1.0 default is two globs: 'packages/*/src/**/spec/**/*.spec.{ts,tsx,mts,cts}' and 'packages/*/spec/**/*.spec.{ts,tsx,mts,cts}'. Both the node and browser projects also always exclude '**/node_modules/**' and '**/.claude/**'. So package-root spec/ folders and .tsx/.mts/.cts specs are now picked up without an include override.
findings.evidence: toolchain/packages/vitest-config/src/defaults.ts:1-4 (include) and :12 (XY_VITEST_SHARED_EXCLUDE = ['**/node_modules/**', '**/.claude/**']). Changed in commit e7ea93749 (2026-10-06, 'unify default testInclude globs across vitest-config and repo-init (item 13)'). `git tag --contains` gives v10.1.0. The published dist/node/index.mjs lines 3-4 contain the new globs.
findings.recommendation: Update xy-toolchain/testing.md:73 and the include row at :77. Since @ariestools/vitest-config 10.1.0 the default include is 'packages/*/src/**/spec/**/*.spec.{ts,tsx,mts,cts}' plus 'packages/*/spec/**/*.spec.{ts,tsx,mts,cts}'. Versions 10.0.x and earlier used only 'packages/*/src/**/spec/**/*.spec.ts', so repos on older versions need an include override for package-root spec/ or .tsx specs. Note that both realm projects always exclude '**/node_modules/**' and '**/.claude/**'. State that package-root spec/ folders are covered by default on 10.1.0+, which matches the 'Spec location' section.

findings.title: The xy-agent link in Related skills points at a skill that consumer repos do not have installed, and nothing says how to install it
findings.current: SKILL.md:33 "**[xy-agent](../xy-agent/SKILL.md)** — *recommended, not required.* ..." (workflow.md:47 has the same relative link). There is no install hint.
findings.truth: The toolchain manages only three ariestools-skills skills: `ARIESTOOLS_SKILLS = ['ariestools-sdk','xy-development','xy-toolchain']`. `xy skills lint --fix` installs each required skill one at a time with `skills add <source> --skill <name>`, so it never installs xy-agent. A repo also cannot opt in through `commands.skillsLint.additionalSkills: ['xy-agent']`, because `normalizeAdditionalSkills` throws "Unknown skills" for names outside the catalog. Two install paths do work: `xy skills defaults` (it runs `--all` against ariestools/ariestools-skills) and a package.json `xy.skills` entry that names an explicit source. As a result, `../xy-agent/SKILL.md` does not resolve in the consumer installs observed.
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/toolchain/src/actions/skills/defaults.ts:13-17 (ARIESTOOLS_SKILLS), :67-73 (defaults uses --all); lint.ts:91-95 (per-skill install); skillRules.ts:80-96 (unknown additionalSkills throw); packageSkills.ts:133-149 (out-of-catalog skill accepted with a declared source). Toolchain repo itself: `ls .agents/skills` → xy-development, xy-toolchain, xy-work (no xy-agent), and `diff -r` shows its xy-development matches the 0.1.5 source. Workspace survey: 30 repos under */* have xy-development v0.1.5 in .agents/skills and 0 have xy-agent (`ls -d */*/.agents/skills/xy-agent` → no matches). The toolchain work item .xy/work/items/XYW-20260901-263436.json already notes that xy-agent "also needs registering in src/actions/skills/defaults.ts (ARIESTOOLS_SKILLS) plus an optional-skills list".
findings.recommendation: At SKILL.md:33 (and the same way at workflow.md:47), add: "If `../xy-agent/` is not installed, add it with `pnpm xy skills add ariestools/ariestools-skills --skill xy-agent`, or declare it in package.json `xy.skills: [{ \"name\": \"xy-agent\", \"source\": \"ariestools/ariestools-skills\" }]`." Do not suggest `xy skills defaults`: it also installs the xyo-skills stack, which lint then flags as unnecessary on non-xl1 repos. Architecture follow-up in the toolchain: register xy-agent as an optional ariestools-skills skill (defaults.ts ARIESTOOLS_SKILLS or a separate optional list, plus skillRules.ts). Then `commands.skillsLint.additionalSkills: ['xy-agent']` is accepted, and skillSourceForName('xy-agent') resolves to ariestools-skills.

findings.title: The workflow.md entry leaves out the layered Definition of Done and the PRD acceptance-criteria authoring that downstream skills link to

findings.title: The release flow (`release/<version>` branches, manual tagging, "every commit on main is a release") matches no repo
findings.current: git.md:69 "`main` — production-ready code. Every commit on main is a release."; git.md:75 "`release/<version>` — release prep (version bumps, final fixes), branched from `develop`, merged to both `main` and `develop`"; git.md:85-86 "create a `release/` branch ... Merge the release branch into `main` (tag it) and back into `develop`"; git.md:76/87 hotfix branches.
findings.truth: No Gitflow repo has release/* or hotfix/* branches. Gitflow repos release through release-please: a `develop` → `main` PR with a `feat:`/`fix:` title merged as a merge commit, then release-please opens a release PR that bumps versions and tags, then an automated `main` → `develop` sync. Versions are never bumped by hand. The main-only @ariestools repos release with `pnpm xy deploy patch|minor|major`, then `pnpm xy publish`, then an annotated `vX.Y.Z` tag. Their main branch carries many commits that are not releases ("workitem", "updo", "lint" between "Deploy" commits), so "every commit on main is a release" is false in both models. The xy-toolchain skill currently documents neither `xy deploy` nor `xy publish`.
findings.evidence: `git branch -r | grep -E 'release/|hotfix/|release-please'` across ariestools-skills, xyo-skills, xyo-skills-internal, infrastructure, web-coin-react and app-portal found only `origin/release-please--branches--main--components--ariestools-skills`. ariestools-skills DEVELOPMENT.md:70-78 and release-please-config.json (`versioning: always-bump-patch`). ariestools-skills CLAUDE.md "Do not bump versions by hand". xyo-skills CLAUDE.md:76-83. toolchain CONTRIBUTING.md:36-47 (release checklist: xy deploy, then xy publish, then annotated tag). `git -C toolchain log`: 7eb43c3c2 "workitem", 3320116a4 "Deploy", 00e1d4d82 "updo", 6cdd67c35 "Deploy". `grep -rn -i 'xy deploy\|xy publish' skills/xy-toolchain` returned nothing.
findings.recommendation: Remove the `release/<version>` branch type and workflow steps 3-4. Reword git.md:69 to say main holds released or releasable code, and that releases are tagged by the release process, not on every commit. Add a 'Releases' note that says agents do not cut, publish or tag a release unless the owner explicitly asks, and never bump versions by hand. Describe the two models. (a) Gitflow/release-please repos: open a develop → main PR with a feat:/fix: title, merge it as a merge commit, merge the release-please PR, and let the automated main → develop sync run. (b) Main-only toolchain repos: follow the repo's release checklist (for example toolchain CONTRIBUTING.md: `xy deploy`, commit the bumps and tag `vX.Y.Z`, `xy publish`, push commits and tags), linking to xy-toolchain for command details. Keep hotfix only as 'branch from main, fix, merge back; the sync carries it to develop'. Architecture follow-up: xy-toolchain needs a deploy/publish section for this link to point at.

In toolchain and sdk-js, 'workitem'/'updo'/'lint' commits sit between 'Deploy' commits. So 'every commit on main is a release' is false in both models. findings.title: Merge-method rules are missing (squash throwaway branches; use merge commits between long-lived branches)
findings.current: absent. git.md never mentions how PRs are merged. git.md:52 says "`git rebase` ... — merge instead", with no guidance on squash merges.
findings.truth: Gitflow repos set the merge method by PR type: `feature/*` → develop is squashed, `develop` → main is a merge commit, release-please → main is squashed, and `main` → develop is a merge commit (automated). Branches between long-lived branches must never be squashed, because that leaves phantom commits in `git log main..develop`. Squash-merging a feature PR is the sanctioned way to collapse branch commits, so with squash the PR, not each commit on the branch, is the unit that lands on develop.
findings.evidence: ariestools-skills CLAUDE.md:47-50 (merge-method table). ariestools-skills DEVELOPMENT.md:89-96. xyo-skills CLAUDE.md:65-74 ("squash is fine when the source branch is throwaway ... Squash is harmful when both source and target are long-lived branches"), :80 ("Do not squash this PR if you ever merge it manually").
findings.recommendation: Add a 'Merging pull requests' subsection. Use the merge method the repo declares (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md or DEVELOPMENT.md). findings.title: The absolute "Never Rewrite History" ban contradicts the workspace commit-identity policy and the repo-scoped rule
findings.current: git.md:48 "Git history is append-only. We always add to it, never rewrite it." git.md:51-54 forbid `git commit --amend`, any `git rebase`, `git push --force`/`--force-with-lease` and `git reset --hard` with no exceptions; git.md:61 "Bad commit message? Let it stand".
findings.truth: The workspace CLAUDE.md requires rewriting an unpushed commit that carries the wrong author email (keeping its tree, parents, message and dates) and allows a force-push of an already-pushed one after asking the user. ariestools-skills scopes the ban to shared branches ("no force-push to main/develop"). An agent following git.md literally would refuse the identity fix and push a commit with the wrong author. xyo-skills keeps the absolute wording, so the repos disagree and the skill should state the scope.
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md:52-56 (Commit identity: "Rewrite an unpushed commit that carries the wrong email ... ask before force-pushing one that is already pushed"; do not override identity with --author / -c user.email / GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL). AGENTS.md:260-264 (same). ariestools-skills CLAUDE.md:41 ("Never rewrite git history on shared branches (no force-push to main/develop)"). xyo-skills CLAUDE.md:63 (absolute form).
findings.recommendation: Scope the rule. Never rewrite pushed or shared history (main, develop, or any branch someone else may have fetched), and never force-push main/develop. Local, unpushed commits may be corrected when the repository's or workspace's own instructions require it, for example fixing commit identity while preserving tree, parents, message and dates. Force-pushing an already-pushed feature branch needs explicit user approval. Add "Repository and workspace CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md take precedence over this section." Optionally add generic identity guidance: commit with the configured git identity, never override it with --author or GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL/GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL, and check `git log --format='%h %ae %ce' @{u}..HEAD` before pushing.

verify.code: confirmed: Workspace CLAUDE.md:52-56 and AGENTS.md:260-264 tell the agent to rewrite an unpushed commit with the wrong email while keeping its tree, parents, message and dates, and to ask before force-pushing an already-pushed one. They also forbid overriding identity with --author, -c user.email or GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL/GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL. ariestools-skills CLAUDE.md:41 limits the ban to shared branches. xyo-skills CLAUDE.md:63 keeps the absolute form. git.md:48-55 bans amend, rebase, force-push and reset --hard with no exceptions, and git.md:61 says 'Let it stand'. The contradiction is real. The workspace CLAUDE.md is normally loaded and wins in practice, so medium rather than high is reasonable.
verify.skill: confirmed: git.md:48 says history is "append-only", and git.md:50-55 forbids amend, any rebase, force or force-with-lease pushes, and reset --hard, with no scope. The workspace CLAUDE.md:56 and AGENTS.md:264 require rewriting an unpushed commit with the wrong email, keeping its tree, parents, message and dates, and they allow a force-push of a pushed one after asking. ariestools-skills CLAUDE.md:41 scopes the ban to shared branches, while xyo-skills CLAUDE.md:63 keeps the absolute form. The recommendation is sound. Keep the identity guidance generic and leave the workspace's specific email in CLAUDE.md. Note that `@{u}..HEAD` fails on a branch with no upstream; the workspace text uses `<upstream>`.

findings.title: Router never mentions the `xyex` channel, `xy --stability`, or docs/STABILITY.md

Those surfaces are compile.validator 'shared', compile.mode 'tsc', compile.compiler 'native', ESLint tier 4, `xy lint --mode shared-typecheck`, non-pnpm package managers, commands.planLint.rules, and commands.npmOrgLint. findings.evidence: toolchain packages/toolchain/package.json:48-49 (`"xy": "dist/bin/xy.mjs"`, `"xyex": "dist/bin/xyex.mjs"`). `node packages/toolchain/dist/bin/xy.mjs --help` lists `--stability  List command, package, and experimental config stability`. `xy.mjs --stability` output has an "Experimental config" section listing the 8 surfaces above. docs/STABILITY.md:9-14 (channel table and migration warning), :55-62, :110-116 (promotion rubric). CHANGELOG.md:40-41,48 (xyex, stability catalog, and `--stability` added in 9.2.0). docs/SKILLS-FOLLOWUP.md:5-7 asks for exactly this.

Mapping: @xylabs/indexed-db -> @ariestools/indexed-db (current home: @ariestools/storage-adapters/indexed-db). @xylabs/mongo -> @ariestools/mongo (current: @ariestools/storage-adapters/mongo). @xylabs/vitest-matchers -> @ariestools/vitest-matchers (current: @ariestools/testing/matchers). @xylabs/vitest-extended -> @ariestools/vitest-extended (current: @ariestools/testing/extended). The npm message for @xylabs/telemetry says to use @ariestools/sdk/telemetry, a path that is now @deprecated in favour of @ariestools/telemetry. The generic rule ("@xylabs/<pkg> with @ariestools/sdk/<pkg>") applies only to umbrella modules. findings.title: The fetch routing line, and fetch.md, omit bounded and cancellable response reads (maxResponseBytes, signal, timeout, readResponseText)
findings.current: SKILL.md:32: "Read when calling `fetchJson` / `FetchClient`, injecting a custom fetcher, or configuring Node HTTP caching with Undici (consumer-owned)." A grep of skills/ariestools-sdk/ for maxResponseBytes, readResponseText, timeout and signal finds nothing.
findings.truth: Since 8.2.0 (b86f3a024, 2026-08-27, "bounded cancellable response reads"), fetchJson, FetchClient and FetchJsonClient accept `maxResponseBytes` (validated positive safe integer), a caller `signal` that stays active through body consumption, and a client `timeout` composed with that signal. The module also exports `readResponseText` and `ReadResponseTextOptions`. 9.0.1 (158476cd7) adds a fallback to response.text() for bodies that are not streams when a signal or byte cap is set. These are the main safety controls for untrusted HTTP responses, and an agent routed by SKILL.md:32 would not know they exist.
findings.evidence: sdk-js packages/sdk/src/modules/fetch/index.ts:25-27 (readResponseText, FetchJsonOptions exports); fetch/types.ts:4-7 (maxResponseBytes); fetch/FetchClient.ts:14-15 (timeout), 158-183 (signal/timeout/maxResponseBytes handling); packages/sdk/README.md:133-205 ("Bounded response reads and cancellation"); `git show 3814c5f0b:packages/sdk/src/modules/fetch/index.ts` (8.2.0) already exports readResponseText; commit 158476cd7 (2026-09-18) message.
findings.recommendation: Change SKILL.md:32 to: "Read when calling `fetchJson` / `FetchClient`, bounding or cancelling response reads (`maxResponseBytes`, `signal`, client `timeout`, `readResponseText`), injecting a custom fetcher, or configuring Node HTTP caching with Undici (consumer-owned)." Add a matching "Bounded reads and cancellation" section to fetch.md, based on packages/sdk/README.md "Bounded response reads and cancellation".

verify.code: confirmed: In sdk-js packages/sdk/src/modules/fetch: index.ts:25-27 exports readResponseText, ReadResponseTextOptions and FetchJsonOptions. types.ts:4-7 adds maxResponseBytes, described as a positive safe-integer cap. FetchClient.ts:14-15 defines timeout 'composed with the caller signal through body consumption'. Lines 150-190 run validateMaxResponseBytes and requestSignal(signal, timeout) and pass {maxResponseBytes, signal} to the body read. fetchJson.ts:33-36 does the same, and FetchJsonClient extends FetchClient. Commit b86f3a024 (2026-08-27) is an ancestor of the 8.2.0 deploy 3814c5f0b, and that deploy's fetch/index.ts already exports readResponseText. Before b86f3a024, timeout replaced the caller signal rather than composing with it, so the composition is new in 8.2.0. 158476cd7 (the non-stream body fallback) is included in the 9.0.1 deploy 298fbb5bb. packages/sdk/README.md:133 has '## Bounded response reads and cancellation'. SKILL.md:32 and fetch.md mention none of these.
verify.skill: confirmed: SKILL.md:32 matches the quoted text. fetch.md has no mention of maxResponseBytes, signal, timeout or readResponseText; it covers only defaults, usage, fetcher injection and Undici. Source confirms the surface. sdk-js packages/sdk/src/modules/fetch/index.ts:25-27 exports readResponseText, ReadResponseTextOptions and FetchJsonOptions. types.ts:4-7 defines maxResponseBytes. FetchClient.ts:14-15 defines timeout, composed with the caller signal, and :158-183 handles signal, timeout and maxResponseBytes. README.md:133 has '## Bounded response reads and cancellation'. b86f3a024 (2026-08-27) shipped in 8.2.0, and 158476cd7 is in v9.0.1. These are the safety controls for untrusted responses, so leaving them out is a material omission rather than a break. Medium fits. The recommendation to update both the router line and fetch.md is correct.

findings.title: `pnpm install --resolution-only` is rejected by pnpm 12, the version every Aries Tools repo pins
findings.current: workflow.md:88 "After adding or changing dependencies, run `pnpm install --resolution-only` to force a fresh resolution check that surfaces all peer dependency warnings."
findings.truth: All Aries Tools repos pin pnpm 12.x through `packageManager`. pnpm 12.4.2 exits with "unexpected argument '--resolution-only'", and its `install --help` does not list the flag. pnpm 12 checks peers with a separate command, `pnpm peers` (also run as `pnpm peers check`), which "Checks for unmet or missing peer dependency issues" and supports `--json` and `--lockfile-only`.
findings.evidence: `pnpm --version` printed 12.4.2. `pnpm install --resolution-only --help` printed "error: unexpected argument '--resolution-only' found / tip: a similar argument exists: '--production'". The full `pnpm install --help` output has no resolution-only option. `pnpm --help` lists "peers: Checks for unmet or missing peer dependency issues", and `pnpm peers --help` says "The only subcommand is `check`, which is also what a bare `pnpm peers` runs". The `packageManager` fields are pnpm@12.4.2 in toolchain/package.json, sdk-js, actor-kit, browser-kit and cli-kit, and pnpm@12.9.1 in sdk-react.
findings.recommendation: Replace the last two sentences of workflow.md:88 with: "After adding or changing dependencies, run `pnpm peers` (pnpm 12+; same as `pnpm peers check`; add `--json` for automation or `--lockfile-only` to skip node_modules) to list unmet or missing peer dependencies." Drop the unverified claim that `pnpm install` suppresses warnings when the lockfile is up to date. Do not name a version range for `--resolution-only` either; it has not been verified. Say only that pnpm 12 does not accept it.

verify.code: adjusted: The core claim checks out. `pnpm --version` printed 12.4.2 in toolchain and 12.9.1 in sdk-react. In both, `pnpm install --resolution-only --help` errors with "unexpected argument '--resolution-only' found". `pnpm install --help` lists no resolution-only option. `pnpm --help` lists "peers  Checks for unmet or missing peer dependency issues", and `pnpm peers --help` documents `check` as the default subcommand, with `--json` and `--lockfile-only`. packageManager is pnpm@12.4.2 in toolchain, sdk-js, actor-kit, browser-kit and cli-kit, and pnpm@12.9.1 in sdk-react. High severity is right: workflow.md:88 tells the agent to run a command that fails. The recommendation's claim that the flag applies to "pnpm 7–10" could not be checked, so the wording should be softened.
verify.skill: confirmed: workflow.md:88 says to run `pnpm install --resolution-only`. On this machine `pnpm --version` printed 12.4.2. Running `pnpm install --resolution-only --help` in the toolchain repo printed "error: unexpected argument '--resolution-only' found / tip: a similar argument exists: '--production'", and `pnpm install --help` has no such option. `pnpm --help` line 44 lists "peers  Checks for unmet or missing peer dependency issues". `pnpm peers --help` documents `--json` and `--lockfile-only` and says a bare `pnpm peers` runs `check`. toolchain/package.json:49 pins pnpm@12.4.2. sdk-js, actor-kit, browser-kit and cli-kit also pin 12.4.2, and sdk-react pins 12.9.1. No other file in the pack mentions peer checking. The skill prescribes a command that fails in every current repo, so high severity is justified.

findings.title: Monorepo scoping example `pnpm --filter <package> build` fails in XY repos and contradicts the root-scoped `xy` convention
findings.current: workflow.md:27 "Use workspace-aware commands: `pnpm --filter <package> build`, not `cd packages/foo && pnpm build`"
findings.truth: XY workspace packages have no `build` script, so `pnpm --filter <pkg> build` has nothing to run. The convention is to run `xy` at the repository root and pass the package name as a positional argument (`pnpm xy build @ariestools/sdk`), because the CLI discovers workspaces, orders compilation and aggregates diagnostics. `--filter` still works for scripts a package really defines, for example the toolchain's own `pnpm --filter @ariestools/toolchain run package-compile`.
findings.evidence: Every sdk-js/packages/*/package.json has empty `scripts` except sdk (`sync-sdk-layout`, `test`), testing (`test`) and express (`coverage`). `node packages/toolchain/dist/bin/xy.mjs build --help` shows "pnpm xy build [package] … package  Specific package to build". CLAUDE.md:32 "Append a package name to scope: `pnpm xy build @ariestools/sdk`". xy-toolchain/toolchain.md:46 "Use `xy` at repository/workspace scope." toolchain/package.json scripts.bootstrap-toolchain = `pnpm --filter @ariestools/toolchain run package-compile`.
findings.recommendation: Reword workflow.md:27 as: "Run commands at the scope the repo's tooling expects. If a root CLI orchestrates the workspace, pass it the package name from the root (XY repos: `pnpm xy build <package-name>`; see xy-toolchain). Otherwise use `pnpm --filter <package> run <script>` for scripts the package actually defines. Never `cd` into a package to build."

verify.code: confirmed: No workspace package has a `build` script in toolchain, sdk-js, sdk-react, actor-kit, browser-kit or cli-kit. Package scripts are limited to package-compile, sync-sdk-layout, test/test:ci and coverage. `pnpm run --help` (12.4.2) documents `--if-present` as "Avoid exiting with a non-zero exit code when the script is undefined". Without it, `pnpm --filter <pkg> build` exits non-zero in these repos, so following workflow.md:27 literally produces a failing command. `xy build --help` shows "pnpm xy build [package] … package  Specific package to build", and CLAUDE.md:32 gives `pnpm xy build @ariestools/sdk`. The finding cites the "Use `xy` at repository/workspace scope" sentence as toolchain.md:46; it is actually at toolchain.md:51. The recommendation is sound.
verify.skill: adjusted: workflow.md:27 does give `pnpm --filter <package> build` as the workspace-aware form. In XY repos the workspace packages have no `build` script; all sdk-js packages/*/package.json scripts are `{}` except sdk (sync-sdk-layout, test), testing (test) and express (coverage). So the example has nothing to run there. The convention is root-scoped `pnpm xy build <package>`: `xy build --help` shows "pnpm xy build [package] … package  Specific package to build", and xy-toolchain/toolchain.md:51 says "Use `xy` at repository/workspace scope". The underlying principle (don't `cd` into a package) is correct and matches the xy convention. The line sits under step 2, which applies only when a script exists, and it is still correct for repos whose packages do define scripts. The failure is a non-destructive 'no script' error, not a wrong build. That makes it a stale or misleading example, medium rather than high.

findings.title: DoD gates name `pnpm build` / `pnpm lint` / `pnpm test` / `pnpm compile` and require "zero warnings", but give no XY mapping or way to prove zero warnings
findings.current: workflow.md:68 "The repo's build command (`pnpm build` or equivalent)". :73 "The repo's lint command (`pnpm lint` or equivalent) passes with zero errors and zero warnings". :81 "Run the repo's test command (`pnpm test` or equivalent)". :89 "A clean `pnpm compile` does not guarantee the app will run".

No `compile` script exists outside the toolchain repo itself; the command is `pnpm xy compile`. `xy lint` / `xy build` exit 0 when only warnings are present. Warnings fail the gate only with `--strict` or `XY_STRICT=1`. Many tier-2–4 rules, including the newly staged unicorn v77 rules, are warnings, so an exit code of 0 does not show "zero warnings".
findings.evidence: toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/lintNext.ts:226 `exitCode: totalErrors + (isStrictMode() ? totalWarnings : 0)`. actions/lint.ts:232 adds `--max-warnings 0` only in strict mode. lib/reporting/xyReporter.ts:46-48 `isStrictMode()` reads the --strict flag or `process.env.XY_STRICT === '1'`. `xy.mjs --help` says "--strict  Treat warnings as errors" and "pnpm xy check  Run git lint, packman lint, publint, repo lint, lint lint, and skills lint". Toolchain commit a499070cc "stage unicorn v77 rules across tiers 2-4". xy-toolchain/commands.md:29 "Do not infer that a zero exit code means zero warnings unless `--strict` was active"; commands.md:34-39 lifecycle-gates table; project-profiles.md:144-152 "Verify the selected profile". CI runs `pnpm xy build` then `pnpm xy test` (sdk-js verify.yml:46,52).
findings.recommendation: Keep layer 1 generic, but add one line under Definition of Done: "In repos using `@ariestools/toolchain`, the build/lint/dependency gates are `pnpm xy build --strict` (or `pnpm xy lint --strict` + `pnpm xy deplint --strict`), tests are `pnpm xy test` (`xy build` does not run tests), and repository policy is `pnpm xy check`. Change `pnpm compile` on line 89 to "a clean compile (`pnpm xy compile` or the repo's equivalent)". findings.title: Dependency-add guidance misses pnpm workspace-root targeting and the repos' `minimumReleaseAge` policy
findings.current: workflow.md:35 "when adding new dependencies, always use `pnpm add <package>` … to resolve the latest published version."
findings.truth: In a multi-package pnpm workspace, `pnpm add <dep>` at the root is refused unless `-w` / `--ignore-workspace-root-check` is passed. findings.title: Workspace-scoped test runs (`xy test @scope/package`, `xy retest @scope/package`, vitest 'in the correct package') skip the root @ariestools/vitest-config preset
findings.current: testing.md:171-177 "Use the toolchain for all tests, one workspace, or one file/folder path: ... pnpm xy test @scope/package"; testing.md:182-183 "pnpm xy retest @scope/package"; testing.md:186 "invoke the installed Vitest through the package manager in the correct package". The same file recommends one root preset config for monorepos (testing.md:25, 98).
findings.truth: When the target is a workspace, `xy test` and `xy retest` run `pnpm --filter <name> exec run-or-exec vitest .` (retest runs `--clearCache` first), so Vitest starts in the package directory. Vitest 5.0.3 looks for a config file only in cwd/--root and does not search upward. The root preset config is therefore never loaded. That means no `browser` project, no spec/node and spec/browser routing (spec/browser specs run in plain Node), no `watch: false`, no `**/.claude/**` exclude, and no root-level setup such as sdk-js's dotenv load; Vitest's default include applies instead. Current ariestools repos (sdk-js, sdk-react, actor-kit, browser-kit, cli-kit, toolchain) define no root `test` script and rely on `pnpm xy test`.

findings.title: Root compile config does not cascade into a package that has its own xy.config.ts
findings.current: "Root configuration cascades to packages under that root. Package-level configuration overrides or deep-merges the applicable root settings." (compilation.md:29)
findings.truth: Root-to-workspace merging only exists for `commands.*`, through loadWorkspaceCommandConfig/mergeCommandConfig. `package-compile` runs in the package directory (`pnpm --filter <pkg> exec run-or-exec package-compile`) and calls `loadConfig()`. That does a cosmiconfig search from cwd ('global' strategy, stopping at the .git root) and uses the first xy.config it finds. When a package has its own xy.config.ts, root `compile.*` settings such as `compiler`, `node`, `validate`, `mode` and `bundlePackages` are dropped, not deep-merged. Root compile settings reach only packages with no config of their own. One exception: the shared validator does fall back to the root `compile.validate`. The real repos show this. sdk-js and toolchain set `compile.compiler: 'native'` at the root and then repeat it in every package config.
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/toolchain/src/lib/loadConfig.ts:53-59 (cosmiconfig with stopDir), 62-92 (ensureRootConfigLoaded/loadConfig = search() from cwd, merged only with params), 210-241 (cascade only in loadWorkspaceCommandConfig for commands); src/pm/pnpmPackageManager.ts:185-188 (runInWorkspaceByName = pnpm --filter <pkg> exec run-or-exec); src/actions/package/compile/compile.ts:16-19 (packageCompile -> loadConfig(inConfig)); node_modules cosmiconfig@10.0.1 dist/index.js:104,120 (searchStrategy 'global' when stopDir set); src/actions/tsc-validate/tscValidate.ts:30 (shared path is the only compile cascade: `wsConfig.compile?.validate ?? rootValidate`); sdk-js/xy.config.ts:4 + sdk-js/packages/crypto/xy.config.ts:5 + sdk-js/packages/sdk/xy.config.ts:10; toolchain/xy.config.ts:7 + toolchain/packages/vitest-config/xy.config.ts:5 (compiler repeated per package). toolchain docs/xy-config.md:15 makes the same inaccurate claim.
findings.recommendation: Split the sentence. `commands.*` cascades: the root provides defaults, workspace configs deep-merge, rule tuples are replaced per id, arrays are unioned. `compile.*` does not: `package-compile` uses the nearest xy.config.ts, so a package config fully replaces the root compile block. Repeat any root compile settings you need (e.g. `compiler`, `validate`) in each package xy.config.ts. Root-only compile fields (`compile.validator`) are read from the repo-root config. Also file a toolchain docs fix for docs/xy-config.md:15.

The bin/package/compile.ts bin calls packageCompile → loadConfig(inConfig) (compile/compile.ts:19). loadConfig runs ensureRootConfigLoaded, which does getExplorer().search() from the process cwd (loadConfig.ts:61-93). The workspace step runs `pnpm --filter <pkg> exec run-or-exec package-compile` (pnpmPackageManager.ts:185-188; compile.ts:117-126), so that cwd is the package directory. cosmiconfig@10.0.1 sets searchStrategy 'global' when stopDir is given (dist/index.js:104). Its search walks up from cwd and returns the first non-empty config it finds (Explorer.js:44-75, ExplorerBase.js:101-116). A package that has its own xy.config.ts therefore never sees the root `compile` block. findings.title: Validation-then-emit ordering is wrong for workspace `xy compile`
findings.current: "By default, `xy compile` performs a no-emit TypeScript validation pass over the full package ... then emits package output through the selected compiler mode." (compilation.md:82)
findings.truth: Validate-then-emit is the order only for `package-compile` with no flags, which is what `xy compile <pkg>` runs. Monolith mode runs layout sync, then validation, then emit. A workspace-level `xy compile` (also build/recompile) runs two phases. First every package emits in topological order over dependencies and devDependencies with `package-compile --emit-only`, which does no type check, and a failure stops dependents. Then validation runs, either `package-compile --validate-only` per package or a single shared-host pass. So when validation fails in a workspace compile, dist has already been written. With `compile.validate: false` the workspace path skips the no-emit check entirely, while a single-package compile still runs the narrower per-source-folder check.
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/toolchain/src/actions/compile.ts:417-426 (Compile:Emit topological, `--emit-only`), 428-445 (Compile:Validate per-package `--validate-only` or shared), 556-570 (single package runs plain package-compile); src/actions/package/compile/packageCompileEsbuild.ts:401-414 (shouldRunFolderChecks = !fullValidation && !emitOnly), 471-478 (validate before emit inside one package); src/actions/package/compile/packageCompileMonolith.ts:135-171.
findings.recommendation: Reword the paragraph. `package-compile` (and `xy compile <pkg>`) first runs a full no-emit tsc validation of the package, including specs, stories and configs. It then emits: tsc declarations, then esbuild JS. Monolith runs layout sync, then validation, then emit. Workspace `xy compile` and `xy build` reverse the order: every package is emitted first, in topological order over dependencies and devDependencies, with `package-compile --emit-only`. That skips full-package validation, though the tsc declaration pass still fails on source type errors. The validation phase runs afterwards, as `--validate-only` per package or as the shared host. A workspace compile can therefore leave fresh dist output while spec, story or config validation fails, and an emit failure stops dependents. `xy recompile` validates then emits per package by default, and emits then validates only with `--validator shared`. With `compile.validate: false`, workspace compiles skip no-emit validation entirely, while `xy compile <pkg>` still runs per-source-folder checks.

verify.code: adjusted: The core issue holds. Workspace `xy compile` (and `xy build`, which calls compile()) emits first and validates second: compile.ts:417-426 runs a topological `package-compile --emit-only` over dependencies and devDependencies, and 428-445 then runs `--validate-only` or the shared host. Single-package `xy compile <pkg>` runs plain package-compile (556-570), which validates and then emits (packageCompileEsbuild.ts:471-478). Two details in the finding are wrong. (1) `--emit-only` does not mean 'no type check'. Declaration emit still runs tsc with emitDeclarationOnly and no noCheck over the src graph (createTypescriptConfig.ts:110-120, packageCompileEsbuild.ts:314-318, 354-378), so source type errors still fail the emit. Only the full-package validation (specs, stories, configs) and the folder checks are skipped. (2) `xy recompile` is not always two-phase. With the default per-package validator, recompileAll runs plain `package-compile` per workspace, validating then emitting in each package. Only with the shared validator does it use `--emit-only` followed by a shared validate (recompile.ts:59-72). The finding's monolith ordering (sync → validate → emit) and its compile.validate:false behaviour are correct (packageCompileEsbuild.ts:401-414).
verify.skill: confirmed: compilation.md:82 says `xy compile` validates first and then emits. That holds for package-compile without flags, which is what `xy compile <pkg>` runs (compile.ts:556-570). runCompileAll (actions/compile.ts:417-445) does the reverse. It first runs `package-compile --emit-only` topologically over dependencies and devDependencies, then runs the validate phase (`--validate-only` per package, or the shared host). resolveCompileMode (packageCompileEsbuild.ts:396-407) confirms that emit-only skips full validation and folder checks. Validation-only does nothing when compile.validate is false. One small imprecision in 'truth': emit-only still runs tsc for declaration emit, so it is not entirely free of type checking. The recommended wording does not depend on that point and is accurate. The skill's own troubleshooting (line 134) relies on this phase model, so medium is proportionate.

findings.title: Target object shape is misdescribed as an 'options object'
findings.current: "Enable a target with `true` or a non-empty options object." (compilation.md:36); "If no target is enabled, build `neutral`." (compilation.md:35)
findings.truth: A platform target object is keyed by source directory, e.g. `{ src: {} }` or `{ src: { entry: [...], ...esbuildOptions } }`. It is not a bag of options. Each key is treated as a srcDir, so `node: { minify: true }` enables node (and turns neutral off), finds no `minify/` directory and silently emits nothing. The legacy `esbuildOptions` key is stripped before classification, so `node: { esbuildOptions: {...} }` alone counts as disabled. Neutral is the default only when `neutral` is unset. With `neutral: false` and no other target, nothing builds. Shared esbuild overrides belong in `compile.esbuild.options`. `compile.tsup.options` is deprecated but still honored.

findings.title: Single-package pnpm repos with no exports or bin are auto-classified as workspace-root, not service or app. The skill never says to set the role
findings.current: project-profiles.md:63 says "Deplint auto-detects a **role**". :72 describes `workspace-root` as "Monorepo root / meta package". :108-115, the single-package section ("Treat the repository root as the package"), never mentions roles. :129 says "A private monorepo root is commonly `workspace-root`".
findings.truth: Deplint's detectRole checks for a workspace root before it checks for service or app. Any package directory with a `workspaces` field or a `pnpm-workspace.yaml` file, and with no library surface or bin, becomes `workspace-root`. Its defaults are runtimeEntry 'none', prodInstallMatters false and peerTarget 'none'. With runtimeEntry 'none' the source fallback is off, so every runtime import counts as non-runtime. The graph also counts as trusted, so `move-to-dev` is allowed. Every pnpm repo must keep a `pnpm-workspace.yaml`: packman lint (part of `xy check`) fails at error level without one, and its fix cannot create the file. The pnpm package manager also treats an empty `packages:` list as a single-package repo. The result: a single-package private service or app (start script `node dist/...`, no main/exports/bin) is classified `workspace-root`, and `xy fix` (which runs `deplint --fix`) demotes its runtime dependencies to devDependencies.
findings.evidence: toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/deplint/isTerminalPackage.ts:234-242 (isWorkspaceRootPackage: `workspaces` field or pnpm-workspace.yaml/yml exists), :282-285 (workspace-root branch runs first in detectRole), :142-148 (workspace-root facets). snapshot.ts:260-261 (runtimeEntry 'none' counts as trusted), :271 (useSourceFallback is runtimeEntry !== 'none'). getExternalImportsFromFiles.ts:126-128 (no source fallback, so the runtime import set is empty). actions/packman/lint.ts:147-152 ("No pnpm-workspace.yaml found" fails the check), :170-172 (the fix returns false when the file is missing), :321-333 (`packman.pnpm.minimumReleaseAge` defaultLevel 'error'). pm/pnpmPackageManager.ts:55-63 (single-package repos keep pnpm-workspace.yaml with empty packages). actions/fix.ts:21 (`xy fix` runs `deplint --fix`). Read-only check, running the classifier source with `node -e "import { classifyDeplintPackage } from '.../isTerminalPackage.ts' ..."`: xylabs/api-coin-xl1 (private, start `node dist/node/index.mjs`, no role configured) → `workspace-root {"prodInstallMatters":false,"runtimeEntry":"none"}`. xylabs/web-xylabs.com-react and XYOracleNetwork/app-portal.xyo.network-react (Vite apps) → `workspace-root`. XYOracleNetwork/api-automation-witness-nodejs/xy.config.ts:6 already works around this with `deplint: { role: 'service', runtimeRoots: ['src/index.ts'] }`.
findings.recommendation: Add a step to "Single-package repository": "If the root package has no `main`/`module`/`exports` and no `bin` (a typical single-package service, app or tooling repo), set `commands.deplint.role` explicitly in the root `xy.config.ts`, for example `{ role: 'service', runtimeRoots: ['src/index.ts'] }`. Deplint classifies any package directory that has `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (which packman lint requires) or a `workspaces` field, and no library or bin surface, as `workspace-root`, and that role demotes runtime dependencies aggressively." Reword :72 and :129: `workspace-root` detection depends on a workspace marker plus no library or bin surface, not on the repo being a monorepo. Separately, consider filing a toolchain issue: detectRole should not treat a root whose pnpm-workspace.yaml lists no packages as `workspace-root`.

In isTerminalPackage.ts, detectRole at :282-285 returns 'workspace-root' first whenever isWorkspaceRootPackage (:234-242: a `workspaces` field or pnpm-workspace.yaml/yml) holds and the package has no library surface and no bin. findings.title: Missing visibility axis and the error-level `dep.*.not-public` rules for public packages that depend on private or restricted workspace siblings
findings.current: :36 "Identify whether the package is independently publishable, deployable, or only a private workspace orchestrator." :125 "Keep workspace-internal runtime packages in `dependencies`; do not convert them mechanically to peers." The file never mentions `publishConfig.access` or the not-public rules.
findings.truth: Since toolchain v10.0.3 (commit 2f9db7e4e, included in 10.1.0), deplint has `dep.dependencies.not-public` and `dep.peerDependencies.not-public`. Both default to error and cannot be auto-fixed. A package is public when it is not `private` and is either unscoped or has `publishConfig.access: 'public'`; a scoped package without `access` counts as restricted. For a public package, `dependencies` and `peerDependencies` may not list: a private or restricted workspace sibling, a `file:`/`link:`/`portal:`/`catalog:`/`patch:`/git spec, or a name that is not on npmjs. Following :125 (keep a private sibling in `dependencies` of a published package) therefore fails `xy deplint` and `xy build`. The fixes are to publish the sibling or to use vendor mode, which keeps private packages in devDependencies.

findings.recommendation: Add a Visibility axis (private / restricted / public, based on `private` and `publishConfig.access`) to the table at :17-23. Extend monorepo item 5: "…in `dependencies`, but a public package may only depend on public siblings. Give each sibling `publishConfig.access: 'public'`, or bundle private implementations with vendor mode (private packages in devDependencies; see compilation.md#vendor-mode). `dep.dependencies.not-public` / `dep.peerDependencies.not-public` are errors and are not auto-fixable."

findings.title: Per-platform type handling is described too vaguely, and a Node package without compile.node fails declaration emit
findings.current: typescript.md:82 "Keep browser and neutral packages free of Node types unless the source genuinely requires them. The compiler resolves platform-specific types when producing browser, neutral, and node targets." The Node types section (typescript.md:64-80) tells agents to add `types: ["node"]` but never says the node target must be opted into.
findings.truth: For each target, `xy compile` writes its own check and declaration tsconfig at `build/tsconfig.package-{check|dts}-<platform>-<src>.json`, and that config extends the package tsconfig. The browser and neutral passes remove `node` from `types`. When `types` is unset, those two passes get `types: []`. Only the node pass keeps the declared types. The browser pass also forces `moduleResolution: 'Bundler'` and `customConditions: ['browser']`. The node pass uses `customConditions: ['node']`. Each pass sets `module` (ESNext for browser, NodeNext for node) only when the package's own tsconfig.json omits `module`. Neutral is the only target built unless another target is opted in. So a package with `types: ["node"]` and no `compile.node: true` builds only the neutral declaration pass, which has no Node types. That pass fails with "Compile:Declaration emit had N errors" even though raw `tsc` passes. A package tsconfig that sets `module: NodeNext` and also emits a browser target gets NodeNext with Bundler resolution, which TS rejects (TS5095).
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/toolchain/src/actions/package/compile/resolvePlatformTypes.ts:32-41 (`platform === 'node' ? [...userTypes] : userTypes.filter(type => type !== 'node')`, `undefined` → `[]` for non-node); spec/actions/resolvePlatformTypes.spec.ts:32-47; createTypescriptConfig.ts:45-61 (default module only when the package's own tsconfig omits it), 75-97 (Bundler + browser condition, node condition), 135-151 (generated file path under build/); packageCompileEsbuild.ts:304-310 (per-platform check), 360-370 (per-platform dts emit via tsc); resolveCompilePlatforms.ts:63-96 (neutral is built only when nothing else is enabled; enabling one target turns the others off); typescript 6.0.3 lib/typescript.js:129880-129882 (TS5095 for bundler with a non-ESM module).
findings.recommendation: Replace the typescript.md:82 paragraph with a short 'Per-target type passes' subsection. (1) xy compile writes build/tsconfig.package-{check|dts}-<platform>-<src>.json per target. Neutral and browser passes drop 'node' from types, and an unset types becomes []. Only the node pass keeps Node globals. (2) A package that declares types:["node"] and uses Node globals must enable compile.node: true in xy.config.ts. Otherwise only the neutral declaration pass runs and fails with 'Compile:Declaration emit had N errors' while raw tsc passes. Link compilation.md#target-selection and project-profiles.md. (3) Browser passes force moduleResolution Bundler and only default module to ESNext when the package tsconfig omits module. So a package that emits a browser target must not set module to NodeNext/Node16; leave module unset or use ESNext. (4) When declaration emit fails but raw tsc passes, inspect the generated build/tsconfig.package-dts-<platform>-*.json.

verify.code: adjusted: Core claim checked against source, and none of these files changed after v10.1.0 (git diff v10.1.0..HEAD touches only updo/parsedPackageJson). resolvePlatformTypes.ts:32-41 removes 'node' for browser and neutral and maps undefined to [] for them. createTypescriptConfig.ts:45-61 sets the default module only when the package's own tsconfig.json omits `module`, and 75-97 always forces Bundler plus customConditions ['browser'] on the browser pass and ['node'] on the node pass. Line 144 writes build/tsconfig.package-{dts|check}-<platform>-<src>.json, which extends the package tsconfig. resolveCompilePlatforms.ts:72-96 builds neutral only when no target is enabled. With the default compile.validate=true, the full validation pass uses the package tsconfig unchanged (packageCompileEsbuild.ts:405-409, 471-476) and the per-folder check is skipped, so a neutral-only Node package fails at 'Compile:Declaration emit had N errors' (line 316). In TS 6.0.3, typescript.js:129881 rejects Bundler with NodeNext (TS5095). Real Node packages pair the two settings (cli-kit-node and sdk-js express use `compile: { node: true }`). One problem is in recommendation point (3). The browser pass always forces moduleResolution Bundler, so setting moduleResolution in the package tsconfig is overridden and harmless. Only an explicit Node-style `module` (Node16/NodeNext) conflicts. Explicit `module: ESNext` + `moduleResolution: bundler` is fine and is used by the monolith packages in sdk-js and sdk-react. Severity medium and action update stand.
verify.skill: adjusted: Verified in source. resolvePlatformTypes.ts:32-41 strips 'node' from types for neutral and browser passes and maps an unset types to []. createTypescriptConfig.ts:45-61 sets the default module only when the package's own tsconfig omits it, and lines 75-97 force Bundler plus customConditions ['browser'] for browser and ['node'] for node. resolveCompilePlatforms.ts:72-96 builds neutral only when no other target is enabled. By default the full validation pass runs against the package tsconfig with node types (packageCompileEsbuild.ts:405-409, 472), and then the per-platform dts pass fails with 'Compile:Declaration emit had N errors' (lines 314-317, 360-370). In TS 6.0.3, lib/typescript.js:129880-129882 rejects bundler resolution with a NodeNext module. typescript.md:64-82 never connects types:["node"] to compile.node. Point (2) of the recommendation is already partly covered elsewhere: project-profiles.md:45 pairs a Node library with 'Base config plus explicit Node types | compile.node: true'. Point (3) is too broad. sdk-react/packages/sdk-react-core/tsconfig.json and sdk-js/packages/storage-adapters/tsconfig.json both set module ESNext with moduleResolution bundler and build browser output without problems. Only module NodeNext (or Node16) conflicts with the forced Bundler resolution. Setting moduleResolution in a package tsconfig is harmless for browser passes because the toolchain overrides it. Medium severity is proportionate, since the gap is real in typescript.md but compilation.md and project-profiles.md partly cover it.

findings.title: The `include: ["src"]` examples shrink xy compile's full-package validation and contradict the toolchain templates
findings.current: typescript.md:46-51, 55-60, 72-79 and 94-101 all show `"include": ["src"]`. Meanwhile typescript.md:117 says to "keep `tsconfig.json` broad for validation", and typescript.md:123 says "full-package validation includes non-emitted TypeScript files by design."
findings.truth: The validation pass is not independent of the package tsconfig. It takes the file list the package tsconfig.json produces (excluding nested `packages/`), forces noEmit, and writes `build/tsconfig.package-validate.json`. findings.title: No guidance on TypeScript 7: typescript must stay at major 6 or below, and the native compiler is an experimental side-by-side alias
findings.current: typescript.md:25 "Use TypeScript 5.9 or 6 with the current toolchain. Follow the consuming repository's exact range policy." Nothing about TypeScript 7, `typescript-native` or `compile.compiler`, and no skill file mentions them.
findings.truth: The peer range is `typescript: ^5.9 || ^6.0`. `xy updo` will not offer a bump past major 6, even with `--latest`, because TypeScript 7 is the Go compiler and exports none of the compiler API that ESLint, deplint, dead and api-exposure load from `typescript`. TS 7 can only be installed alongside, as `"typescript-native": "npm:typescript@~7.0.2"`, with `compile.compiler: 'native'`. That is enabled by the experimental `xyex enable ts-native`, and it does not work with `compile.validator: 'shared'`. deplint keeps the alias even though nothing imports it. The stability catalog says public examples must not require the native compiler. This shipped 2026-08-10 and is in 10.1.0.
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/toolchain/package.json:99-100 (dev `typescript ~6.0.3`, `typescript-native npm:typescript@~7.0.2`), 106-108 (peer `^5.9 || ^6.0`); src/lib/updo/majorCeiling.ts:16-28; src/actions/package/compile/XyConfig.ts:142-157, 171-177; src/actions/package/compile/resolveTscBin.ts:5-34; src/actions/deplint/rules.md:219; docs/STABILITY.md:59, 98-99; `node packages/toolchain/dist/bin/xy.mjs --stability --json` → experimentalConfig `compile.compiler.native`: "TypeScript 7 (Go) compiler. Enable with `xyex enable ts-native`. This repo may dogfood it; public examples must not require it."; `xyex enable --help` lists `ts-native`; git log c2b9db449 2026-08-10 "feat(toolchain): optional native TypeScript compiler".
findings.recommendation: Pin the TypeScript major in every install command: typescript.md:16/19/22 and toolchain.md:44 should use `typescript@^6` (or the repo's tilde policy, e.g. ~6.0.3) instead of bare `typescript`, because npm `latest` is now 7.x. Extend typescript.md:25: never upgrade the `typescript` dependency to 7. typescript@7 is the Go compiler and exports no compiler API, the toolchain peer is ^5.9 || ^6.0, and `xy updo` caps it at 6. The TS 7 compiler is an optional, experimental side-by-side install: `pnpm xyex enable ts-native` adds `"typescript-native": "npm:typescript@~7.0.2"` and sets `compile.compiler: 'native'`, which is incompatible with `compile.validator: 'shared'`, and shared examples must not require it. Add a matching `compile.compiler` / `nativePackage` bullet to compilation.md#type-validation.

verify.code: confirmed: Verified everything in released 10.1.0. Commit c2b9db449 (2026-08-10) is contained in v10.0.0 and later. toolchain package.json:99-100 has dev `typescript ~6.0.3` and `typescript-native npm:typescript@~7.0.2`, and :106-108 has peer `typescript ^5.9 || ^6.0`. majorCeiling.ts:16-28 caps updo at major 6 even with --latest, and its reason names ESLint, deplint, dead-code and api-exposure. The deplint rules.md devDependencies.unused row retains the alias. The `xy.mjs --stability --json` experimentalConfig entry compile.compiler.native says 'Enable with `xyex enable ts-native`... public examples must not require it.' `xyex enable --help` lists ts-native (`xy enable` also exists, marked 'experimental — prefer xyex'). STABILITY.md:59 and :99 agree. grep finds no skill that mentions native, ts-native or TypeScript 7.

findings.title: The `types` explanation assumes TS 5.9 auto-inclusion; on TS 6 `types` defaults to []
findings.current: typescript.md:66 "The base is not a license to expose Node globals everywhere." typescript.md:104 "Setting `compilerOptions.types` disables automatic `@types/*` inclusion."
findings.truth: TypeScript 6 is the toolchain's dev compiler and the one repo-init installs. On TS 6, automatic type directives are `options.types ?? []`, and `@types/*` packages are discovered only when `types` contains "*". So on TS 6 the base config exposes no Node, Vitest or other `@types` globals unless they are listed. Setting `types` disables auto-inclusion only on TS 5.9.

[]`), 21973-21975 (`usesWildcardTypes` = types includes "*"); toolchain packages/toolchain/package.json:99 (`typescript ~6.0.3`); templates/repo/cli/root/package.json.tmpl:48 (`typescript ~6.0.3`).
findings.recommendation: Reword typescript.md:104 only. On TypeScript 5.9, setting compilerOptions.types turns off automatic @types/* inclusion. On TypeScript 6, nothing is auto-included unless types lists it (or uses "*"). Either way, list Node, test-global or lib-neutral types explicitly. Leave line 66 as is; line 123 already covers missing Node globals. Optionally flag the same wording upstream in toolchain packages/lib-neutral/README.md and globals.d.ts:8-10.

Toolchain package.json pins dev typescript ~6.0.3, and templates/repo/cli/root/package.json.tmpl:48 installs `typescript ~6.0.3`. The base tsconfig (packages/tsconfig/tsconfig.json) sets no `types`. So on TS 6, nothing from @types is visible unless it is listed. The 'disables automatic @types/* inclusion' framing at typescript.md:104 (also lib-neutral/globals.d.ts:8) is accurate only for TS 5.9, which the peer range still allows. Low severity is right.

findings.title: Base-config list leaves out legacy `experimentalDecorators` and `importHelpers`, which affect decorators and tslib
findings.current: typescript.md:29-38 lists target/lib, module/moduleResolution, strict/noImplicitAny/noImplicitOverride, allowImportingTsExtensions/allowJs/resolveJsonModule, isolatedModules/erasableSyntaxOnly, declarations/maps, outDir and noEmit.
findings.truth: The base config also sets `experimentalDecorators: true`, `importHelpers: true`, `esModuleInterop`, `allowSyntheticDefaultImports`, `skipLibCheck: true` and `incremental: false`. Legacy decorators were restored on purpose on 2026-05-20, replacing TC39 decorators. Because of `importHelpers`, deplint treats `tslib` as an implicit devDependency in any package whose source uses decorators. `erasableSyntaxOnly` makes enums, value namespaces and parameter properties into errors; sdk-js `threads` overrides it to false.
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/tsconfig/tsconfig.json:3-28 (experimentalDecorators line 10, importHelpers line 12, skipLibCheck line 23); git show 417ebf827 (2026-05-20 "revert to legacy decorators", adds experimentalDecorators); packages/toolchain/src/actions/deplint/implicitDevDependencies.ts:32-44 (decorator detection), 104-110 (`tslib` needed when decorators are present or a dependency peers on tslib); sdk-js/packages/threads/tsconfig.json (`erasableSyntaxOnly: false`).
findings.recommendation: Add two bullets to the base-config list. First: `experimentalDecorators` — legacy TypeScript decorator semantics, not TC39. Second: `importHelpers` — code that needs emit helpers, such as decorators, requires `tslib` as a dependency, and TypeScript reports it when it is missing; deplint treats it as an implicit devDependency rather than flagging it unused. Add one line that `erasableSyntaxOnly` makes enums, value namespaces and parameter properties errors, and that overriding it (as sdk-js threads does) needs a package-level reason.

verify.code: adjusted: The facts mostly check out. packages/tsconfig/tsconfig.json sets experimentalDecorators (line 10), importHelpers (12), esModuleInterop (9), allowSyntheticDefaultImports (5), skipLibCheck (23) and incremental false (13). git show 417ebf827 (2026-05-20, 'revert to legacy decorators') added experimentalDecorators. sdk-js/packages/threads/tsconfig.json sets erasableSyntaxOnly false. The recommendation's claim that deplint 'enforces' tslib is wrong. getImplicitDevDependencies (implicitDevDependencies.ts:104-110) is called only from getUnusedDevDependencies.ts:56, so it only stops a declared tslib from being flagged unused. It never requires tslib or adds it. The requirement actually comes from the type checker. With importHelpers and legacy decorators, checkExternalEmitHelpers(firstDecorator, Decorate) (typescript.js:87387-87388, 93542-93546) raises TS2354 'This syntax requires an imported helper but module tslib cannot be found' during validation and declaration emit, even though esbuild does the JS emit.
verify.skill: adjusted: The base config does set experimentalDecorators (packages/tsconfig/tsconfig.json:10) and importHelpers (:12), along with esModuleInterop, allowSyntheticDefaultImports, skipLibCheck and incremental:false. Commit 417ebf827 (2026-05-20, 'revert to legacy decorators') confirms the legacy-decorator choice. sdk-js/packages/threads/tsconfig.json overrides erasableSyntaxOnly to false. findings.title: The experimental `xyex tsc-validate` type-check-only command is not mentioned anywhere
findings.current: absent. typescript.md:40 and 117 talk about separating validation from emission but name no type-check-only command. compilation.md:89-91 covers `compile.validator: 'shared'` and `--validator shared` only. A grep of skills/ finds no `tsc-validate`.
findings.truth: `xyex tsc-validate [package]` type-checks all workspaces in one process with a shared source-file cache. It respects `compile.validate: false` and skips packages without a tsconfig. It is the same engine as `compile.validator: 'shared'`, is catalogued as experimental, and does not work with the native compiler. The stable path is still `xy compile`, whose validation pass runs before emit.
findings.evidence: `node packages/toolchain/dist/bin/xyex.mjs tsc-validate --help` → "TSC Validate - Type-check all packages in one process with a shared source-file cache"; `xy --stability --json` → `{name: 'tsc-validate', stability: 'experimental'}`; toolchain packages/toolchain/src/actions/tsc-validate/tscValidate.ts:14-31, 42-60; docs/STABILITY.md:98.
findings.recommendation: In skills/xy-toolchain/compilation.md#type-validation, next to the `compile.validator: 'shared'` bullets (lines 89-91), add: `pnpm xyex tsc-validate [package]` runs the same shared-host engine as a type-check-only pass across workspaces. It is experimental, respects `compile.validate: false`, skips packages without a tsconfig, and is incompatible with `compile.compiler: 'native'`. Otherwise rely on `pnpm xy compile`'s validation pass. Optionally add a one-line pointer from typescript.md:117.

The stability catalog lists {name: tsc-validate, stability: experimental}, and its compile.validator.shared entry says 'Same engine as `xyex tsc-validate`. Incompatible with `compile.compiler: native`'. tscValidate.ts:26-31 mirrors compile.validate:false, and the no-tsconfig skip is handled at :62-70. STABILITY.md:98 matches. grep finds no tsc-validate anywhere under skills/. One nuance: in code, tsc-validate does not fail under native. Also note that a monolith package's tsconfig.json must be plain JSON (no comments), because package-sync-layout rewrites it with JSON.parse. In typescript.md:123, append: 'In monolith packages, tsconfig `paths` are generated — fix `compile.monolith` and run `package-sync-layout` (see compilation.md#monolith-mode) instead of editing them.'

Check mode reports 'out of date: tsconfig.json'. bin/package/sync-layout.ts:11-35 implements `package-sync-layout [--check]`, registered at package.json:46. sdk-js/packages/sdk/tsconfig.json has 88 generated paths. typescript.md:123 names 'path aliases' without saying they are generated. compilation.md:108 already says not to hand-edit 'generated monolith barrels, aliases, or shims' and has a '## Monolith mode' heading, so the gap is only a missing cross-reference from typescript.md troubleshooting. verify.skill: adjusted: Verified: monolithCompileLayout.ts:143-164 (buildTsconfigPaths) and :276-316 (syncMonolithLayout) regenerate tsconfig.json compilerOptions.paths and package.json imports. bin/package/sync-layout.ts:27-34 makes --check fail on drift. sdk-js/packages/sdk/tsconfig.json carries the generated #module paths. The skill does not omit this entirely, though. compilation.md:103-110 already shows `package-sync-layout` / `--check` and says 'Do not edit generated monolith barrels, aliases, or shims by hand'. findings.title: Relative imports must use .ts/.tsx extensions, not .js
findings.current: "Use `.js` extensions in relative import paths (TypeScript resolves `.ts` → `.js`)" (skills/xy-development/typescript.md:62)
findings.truth: The base tsconfig enables `allowImportingTsExtensions` with `noEmit`, and every @ariestools repo writes relative specifiers with `.ts`/`.tsx`. The lint barrel ban is spelled with `.ts` paths, so a `.js` specifier gets past it without any report.
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/tsconfig/tsconfig.json:4 `"allowImportingTsExtensions": true`, :17 `"noEmit": true`. I counted relative `from './…'` specifiers in packages/*/src: toolchain 1809 .ts / 0 .js; sdk-react 891 .ts + 374 .tsx / 0 .js; actor-kit 268/0; cli-kit 288/0; browser-kit 130/0; sdk-js 1052 .ts / 29 .js (leftovers in packages/sdk/src/spec/typeof/*.spec.ts, packages/express/src/middleware/standardResponses/standardResponses.ts:5-6, storage-adapters). eslint-config-flat src/rules/correctness.ts:5-14 and src/rules/index.ts:8-17 list the restricted paths as './index.ts', '../index.ts', and so on. I linted a scratch file with recommendedConfig({tier:3,isTypeChecked:true}) through the ESLint API: `import { helper } from './index.ts'` gives `error no-restricted-imports`, and `import { helper } from './index.js'` gives no no-restricted-imports report. The pack disagrees with itself: skills/xy-toolchain/typescript.md:34 lists `allowImportingTsExtensions`.
findings.recommendation: Replace line 62 with: "Use explicit `.ts` / `.tsx` extensions in relative import paths (`import { x } from './x.ts'`). The base `@ariestools/tsconfig` enables `allowImportingTsExtensions` and the toolchain compile handles them. Do not write `.js` specifiers for TypeScript sources. They break with house convention, and they slip past the lint rule that bans importing `index.ts` barrels." Also fix the same `.js` pattern in skills/xy-toolchain/testing.md:202 (`'../validateMove.js'`).

findings.title: The `any` escape hatch needs a rule-scoped eslint-disable, not a TODO comment
findings.current: "5. **Only then: `any`** — with a `// TODO: [reason alternatives don't work]` comment explaining the constraint." (skills/xy-development/typescript.md:17)
findings.truth: `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` is an error at every tier, so a TODO comment still fails lint. In the default type-checked mode, `any` that spreads also triggers the no-unsafe-* errors. The repos write `// eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any -- <reason>`. Blanket disables are banned (`unicorn/no-abusive-eslint-disable`), `@ts-ignore` is banned, and `@ts-expect-error` needs a description (`ban-ts-comment`).
findings.evidence: typescript-eslint 8.71.1 flat/recommended sets `no-explicit-any: 'error'`; it is spread at every tier in eslint-config-flat src/typescript/index.ts:186,196. Effective config from ESLint.calculateConfigForFile at tiers 2 and 3: no-explicit-any [2], no-unsafe-assignment [2], ban-ts-comment [2], unicorn/no-abusive-eslint-disable [2]. Type-checked is the default (src/tiers/recommendedConfig.ts:12-15). Scratch lint of `// TODO: reason alternatives don't work` followed by `const loose: any = helper` gives `10:16 error @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any`. ban-ts-comment defaults are `'ts-ignore': true, 'ts-expect-error': 'allow-with-description'` (node_modules/@typescript-eslint/eslint-plugin/dist/rules/ban-ts-comment.js:75-82). 29 source files in toolchain and sdk-js use `// eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any`; the toolchain adds `-- reason` descriptions (packages/eslint-config-flat/src/index.ts:44).
findings.recommendation: Rewrite step 5 as: "Only then: `any`, scoped as narrowly as possible with `// eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any -- <why the alternatives don't work>`. `no-explicit-any` is an error at every lint tier. Never use a blanket `eslint-disable` or `@ts-ignore`. If you must suppress a compiler error, use `@ts-expect-error <description>`." Also note under 'contained, never contagious' that `any` flowing into other values triggers the type-checked `no-unsafe-*` errors.

verify.code: confirmed: I computed the effective config with ESLint.calculateConfigForFile and recommendedConfig from the built eslint-config-flat 10.1.0. @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any is [2] at tiers 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4. ban-ts-comment is [2] at every tier. unicorn/no-abusive-eslint-disable is [2] from tier 2 up. no-unsafe-assignment is [2]. In a scratch lint at tier 3, `// TODO: reason alternatives don't work` followed by `const loose: any = helper` gave `error @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any`, so following step 5 fails `xy lint`. High is correct. ban-ts-comment defaults (typescript-eslint 8.71.1 dist/rules/ban-ts-comment.js:75-82) are 'ts-ignore': true and 'ts-expect-error': 'allow-with-description'. The evidence needs two corrections that do not change the verdict. First, rule-scoped next-line disables appear in 3 toolchain files and 6 sdk-js files, not 29. sdk-js also has 23 files with the file-scoped `/* eslint-disable @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any */`, mostly in packages/threads. Second, none of the existing no-explicit-any disables carries a `-- reason`. The cited eslint-config-flat src/index.ts:44 is a no-deprecated disable. Adding the description is still sound advice.

findings.title: Return-type guidance contradicts the workspace rule 'explicit return types on exported functions'
findings.current: "## Return Types: Prefer Inference … **Do not annotate return types** unless one of these applies: public API boundary / unexpectedly wide / type guard / recursive" (skills/xy-development/typescript.md:23-31)
findings.truth: The workspace style rules and the SDK repo rules require explicit return types on exported functions, and require async functions to declare `Promise<T>` (never `Promise<Promisable<T>>`). Lint does not enforce this (`explicit-module-boundary-types` is off), so the skill is the only place an agent outside this workspace would learn it, and right now it teaches the opposite default. In practice almost all exported functions are annotated.
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md:43 "Explicit return types on exported functions", :46 "When a function uses `await`, declare the return as `Promise<T>` — never `Promise<Promisable<T>>`"; AGENTS.md:251,254; sdk-js/AGENTS.md:58 "Explicit return types on exported functions". Lint: eslint-config-flat src/typescript/index.ts:101 and src/tiers/rule-catalog/managed-rules.ts:54 set `explicit-module-boundary-types` to off; explicit-function-return-type is not configured. A regex scan of `export function` declarations found return types on 712 of 742 in toolchain packages and 102 of 124 in sdk-js packages. `Promisable` is defined at sdk-js packages/sdk/src/modules/promise/types.ts:6.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the section: "Annotate return types on exported functions and methods (the module contract). Let inference handle local helpers, callbacks and arrow functions passed inline. When a function uses `await`, declare `Promise<T>`, never `Promise<Promisable<T>>`. Always annotate type guards (`x is T`) and recursive functions." Keep the covariance rationale only for non-exported code.

verify.code: adjusted: The conflict is real. CLAUDE.md:43 says "Explicit return types on exported functions" and :46 states the Promise<T>/Promisable rule. AGENTS.md:251 and :254 and sdk-js/AGENTS.md:58 say the same. The skill (typescript.md:23-31) defaults to 'Do not annotate'. An AST count of exported function declarations with bodies found return types on 716/746 in toolchain and 101/124 in sdk-js. Exported const arrows are typed less often (toolchain 199/272, sdk-js 71/134, sdk-react 27/56). The severity is too high, though. The rule is documented but not enforced by lint or tsc. Following the skill produces code that compiles and lints, and the skill already makes an exception for 'public API boundary'. That makes this medium (stale or contradictory guidance, not breaking). The recommendation is fine as written.

findings.title: Enums, parameter properties and runtime namespaces are compile errors (erasableSyntaxOnly), not just 'prefer unions'
findings.current: "**Prefer union types** over enums: `type Status = 'active' | 'inactive'` rather than `enum Status { Active, Inactive }`" (skills/xy-development/typescript.md:85). The Readonly section suggests "Class properties set in the constructor that shouldn't change" (:51) but says nothing about parameter properties.
findings.truth: The base `@ariestools/tsconfig` sets `erasableSyntaxOnly: true` and `noImplicitOverride: true`. As a result `enum`, constructor parameter properties (`constructor(private readonly x: T)`) and namespaces with runtime code fail to compile, and overriding members need the `override` keyword. Lint also flags enums and suggests string-literal unions or a `const` object. The SDK ships an `Enum()` helper for the const-object pattern.
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/tsconfig/tsconfig.json:8 `"erasableSyntaxOnly": true`, :19 `"noImplicitOverride": true`. I ran tsc 6.0.3 with that tsconfig on a scratch file: `export enum Status {…}`, `constructor(private readonly x: number) {}` and `export namespace NS { export const y = 1 }` each fail with `error TS1294: This syntax is not allowed when 'erasableSyntaxOnly' is enabled.` eslint-config-flat src/typescript/index.ts:161-167 configures no-restricted-syntax on TSEnumDeclaration with the message "Enums are disallowed. Consider using a union of string literals or a `const` object instead." `@typescript-eslint/no-namespace` is effective [2]. sdk-js packages/sdk/src/modules/enum/{Enum.ts,model.ts} exports `Enum`, `EnumKey`, `EnumValue` via `@ariestools/sdk/enum`.

Use a string-literal union, or an `as const` object (optionally `Enum({...} as const)` from `@ariestools/sdk/enum`) when you need runtime values." In the Readonly section add: "Declare `readonly` fields explicitly. Constructor parameter properties are not allowed (`erasableSyntaxOnly`). Mark overriding members with `override` (`noImplicitOverride`)."

The skill only says 'prefer union types' (line 85) and suggests constructor-set readonly properties (line 51) without mentioning that parameter properties are banned. Medium is appropriate.
