findings.title: 'Strictness Posture' says these conventions are what linters can't catch, but most of them are lint- or compiler-enforced
findings.current: "Most opinions are enforced via ESLint. The conventions below cover what linters can't catch — judgment calls that require understanding intent." (skills/xy-development/typescript.md:5)
findings.truth: Several conventions in this file are hard rules at the default tier 3 with type checking. Enforced by lint: interface over type (`consistent-type-definitions` error), optional chaining and nullish coalescing (`prefer-optional-chain` / `prefer-nullish-coalescing` error), no `any` (`no-explicit-any` error), no `require()` (`no-require-imports` error), no enums (`no-restricted-syntax`), import order (`simple-import-sort`). Enforced by the compiler: `strict`, `noImplicitAny`, `noImplicitOverride`, `erasableSyntaxOnly`. The file never mentions the tsconfig side.
findings.evidence: Effective rules from ESLint.calculateConfigForFile with recommendedConfig({tier:3,isTypeChecked:true}): consistent-type-definitions [2], prefer-optional-chain [2], prefer-nullish-coalescing [2], no-explicit-any [2], no-require-imports [2], no-restricted-syntax [1,{TSEnumDeclaration}], simple-import-sort/imports [1]. The defaults are tier 3 and type-checked (src/tiers/recommendedConfig.ts:12-15), and `xy lint init` generates `recommendedConfig({ tier: 3, isTypeChecked: true })` (packages/toolchain/src/actions/lint-init.ts, generateEslintConfig). tsconfig: packages/tsconfig/tsconfig.json:8,18,19,25.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite line 5: "We are strict. The compiler (`@ariestools/tsconfig`: strict, noImplicitAny, noImplicitOverride, erasableSyntaxOnly) and ESLint (`@ariestools/eslint-config-flat`, tier 3 type-checked by default) enforce most of what follows. Items marked *(enforced)* are tsc errors or lint errors/warnings; warnings fail `xy lint` only in strict mode. `pnpm xy fix` autofixes formatting, import order and type-import style. The rest are judgment calls." Tag each enforced bullet, and link ../xy-toolchain/eslint.md and ../xy-toolchain/typescript.md so Layer 2 owns the specifics.

verify.code: adjusted: The core claim holds. The effective tier-3 type-checked config has consistent-type-definitions [2], prefer-optional-chain [2], prefer-nullish-coalescing [2], no-explicit-any [2] and no-require-imports [2], with no-restricted-syntax (enum) at [1] and simple-import-sort/imports at [1]. The defaults are tier 3 and isTypeChecked true (recommendedConfig.ts:12-15), and lint-init.ts:102 generates `recommendedConfig({ tier: 3, isTypeChecked: true })`. The tsconfig sets strict, noImplicitAny, noImplicitOverride and erasableSyntaxOnly. Line 5's 'what linters can't catch' is therefore inaccurate. The recommended wording overstates enforcement, though. 'Items marked (enforced) fail `xy lint`/`tsc`' is false for warn-level rules (enum lint rule, import sort, consistent-type-imports, explicit-member-accessibility). `xy lint` adds `--max-warnings 0` only in strict mode (actions/lint.ts:232, isStrictMode = --strict state or XY_STRICT=1). `xy fix` runs `xy lint --fix` among other fixers (actions/fix.ts), so the autofix claim is fine.
verify.skill: confirmed: typescript.md:5 claims the conventions below 'cover what linters can't catch'. The effective tier-3 type-checked config shows many of them are enforced: consistent-type-definitions [2], prefer-optional-chain [2], prefer-nullish-coalescing [2], no-explicit-any [2], no-require-imports [2], and no-restricted-syntax on TSEnumDeclaration [1]. The tsconfig enforces strict, noImplicitAny, noImplicitOverride and erasableSyntaxOnly (tsconfig.json:8, 18, 19, 25). Linking ../xy-toolchain/eslint.md and typescript.md keeps the layering correct. Medium is acceptable.

findings.title: Null handling must cover strict-boolean-expressions (no implicit truthiness on nullable strings/numbers)
findings.current: "**Null handling**: prefer optional chaining (`?.`) and nullish coalescing (`??`) over manual null checks" (skills/xy-development/typescript.md:87). Nothing about truthiness checks.
findings.truth: At the default tier 3 with type checking, `@typescript-eslint/strict-boolean-expressions` is an error. With the default options, `if (name)` on `string | undefined` or `if (count)` on `number | undefined` is rejected, so agents must write explicit checks (`name !== undefined`, `name.length > 0`, `count !== undefined && count > 0`). `unicorn/no-typeof-undefined` is also an error, so compare with `=== undefined` directly. `null` itself is allowed (`unicorn/no-null` is off).
findings.evidence: eslint-config-flat src/tiers/rule-catalog/managed-rules.ts:57 sets `strict-boolean-expressions` to {0:'off', 3:'error'} and requires type checking; it is effective [2] at tier 3 and [0] at tier 2. Scratch lint at tier 3: `if (name)` with `name: string | undefined` gives `error @typescript-eslint/strict-boolean-expressions - Unexpected nullable string value in conditional`; `if (count)` with `count?: number` gives "Unexpected nullable number value in conditional"; `typeof loose === 'undefined'` gives `error unicorn/no-typeof-undefined`. managed-rules.ts:154 has `unicorn/no-null` off.
findings.recommendation: Expand the null-handling bullet into a short subsection: use `?.`/`??` *(enforced)*; write explicit comparisons in conditions for nullable strings, numbers and booleans (strict-boolean-expressions); compare with `=== undefined`/`=== null` rather than `typeof x === 'undefined'`; prefer `undefined` for absent values in new code, but `null` is not banned.

verify.code: confirmed: managed-rules.ts:57 sets strict-boolean-expressions to {0:'off',3:'error'} and marks it type-check-only. It is effective [2] at tiers 3 and 4 and [0] at tiers 0-2. A scratch lint at tier 3 gave: `if (name)` with `string | undefined` → 'error @typescript-eslint/strict-boolean-expressions - Unexpected nullable string value in conditional'; `if (count)` with `count?: number` → 'Unexpected nullable number value in conditional'; `typeof loose === 'undefined'` → 'error unicorn/no-typeof-undefined'. unicorn/no-null is effective [0] (managed-rules.ts:154). The skill's line 87 does not mention truthiness checks.
verify.skill: confirmed: The skill's null-handling bullet (typescript.md:87) does not cover truthiness. Effective config has @typescript-eslint/strict-boolean-expressions [2] at tier 3 and [0] at tier 2, unicorn/no-typeof-undefined [2] and unicorn/no-null [0]. My scratch lint at tier 3 reported `if (name)` on string|undefined as 'Unexpected nullable string value in conditional', `if (count)` on number|undefined as 'Unexpected nullable number value', and `typeof x === 'undefined'` as unicorn/no-typeof-undefined. These are idiomatic patterns agents write by default and they fail lint at the default tier. Medium is appropriate.

findings.title: Import-ordering bullet should defer to simple-import-sort groups and its autofix
findings.current: "**Import ordering:** External packages first, then internal modules, separated by a blank line" (skills/xy-development/typescript.md:80-81)
findings.truth: `simple-import-sort` v14 sets the order (warn at tiers 2 and 3, autofixable). Its default groups are side-effect imports, then `node:` built-ins, then packages, then absolute imports, then relative imports, each separated by a blank line. Agents should run the fixer instead of ordering by hand.

Scratch lint reported `warn simple-import-sort/imports - Run autofix to sort these imports!`.
findings.recommendation: Replace with: "Import order is enforced and autofixed by simple-import-sort: side-effect imports, then `node:` built-ins, then packages, then relative imports, with a blank line between groups. Run `pnpm xy fix` (or `pnpm xy lint --fix`) rather than ordering by hand."

findings.title: A local no-restricted-imports block, including the one lint init generates, silently replaces the shared tier-0 barrel/src import bans
findings.current: eslint.md:22 "derives root-barrel import restrictions from installed SDK barrels"; eslint.md:130 "Place justified local overrides after the recommended config. Run `xy lint lint` to distinguish intentional additions from redundant shared rules and overrides requiring review."
findings.truth: The shared config sets `no-restricted-imports` at error level. Its options ban `./index.ts` … `../../../../../../../index.ts` barrel paths and the `**/src/**` import patterns. If you accept a barrel prompt, `xy lint init` adds an unscoped `{ rules: { 'no-restricted-imports': ['warn', { paths: [...barrels] }] } }` block after the recommended config. In flat config a later rule entry with options replaces the earlier options completely. The result is that the barrel-index.ts and src/ bans disappear and the rule drops to warn. `xy lint lint` deliberately exempts this block from `lintlint.rule-override` (isLintInitBarrelRestriction), so nothing reports it. This works against the workspace policy "no importing from barrel index.ts files".
findings.evidence: toolchain/packages/eslint-config-flat/src/rules/correctness.ts:5-14,24-27 (restrictedImportPaths, error); src/rules/index.ts:19-26,40-56 (src patterns); src/tiers/rule-catalog/managed-rules.ts:46 (tier 0 error). toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/lint-init.ts:132-138 (unscoped 'warn' block appended after recommendedConfig). lintlint.ts:183-191 (exemption). Empirical: calculateConfigForFile('src/index.ts') with recommendedConfig({tier:3}) gives [2,{paths:['./index.ts',...],patterns:[{group:['**/src/**',...]}]}]. Adding the generator-style block gives [1,{paths:[{name:'@xylabs/hex',...}]}]. Real consumers affected: XYOracleNetwork/xl1-faucet-twitter/eslint.config.ts:145-150, XYOracleNetwork/webble/eslint.config.ts:67-70.
findings.recommendation: Add a caution to 'Overrides and troubleshooting' and next to the lint init description in eslint.md:22. Say that any local `no-restricted-imports` entry with options replaces the shared tier-0 options and does not merge with them, and that this includes the block `xy lint init` writes when a barrel prompt is accepted. Scoping the block with `files` does not prevent this. Agents should merge the shared options back in (the exported `correctnessRulesConfig.rules['no-restricted-imports']` paths, plus the `srcImportsConfig` src/ patterns for **/src files) and keep the level at `error`. Also say that `xy lint lint` deliberately does not report the lint-init barrel block. Separately, file a toolchain issue so that lint-init (lint-init.ts:132-138) merges the shared restrictions and emits `error`.

verify.code: adjusted: I confirmed the core issue. eslint-config-flat/src/rules/correctness.ts:5-14,25-28 sets no-restricted-imports to error with the index.ts paths. src/rules/index.ts:44-56 adds the `**/src/**` patterns for files under src. lint-init.ts:132-138 appends an unscoped `'warn'` block with only the barrel paths. lintlint.ts:186-190,213-214 exempts that block from rule-override. None of these files changed after the 10.1.0 deploy (3320116a4). I reproduced the effect with ESLint calculateConfigForFile against dist: the base config gives src/index.ts `[2,{paths:[./index.ts…],patterns:[{group:['**/src/**',…]}]}]`, and with the generator-style block it becomes `[1,{paths:[{name:'@xylabs/hex',…}]}]`. The consumer configs in xl1-faucet-twitter (lines 145-150) and webble (lines 67-70) match this pattern. One part of the recommendation is wrong. Scoping the barrel block with `files` does not stop the replacement; it only limits which files lose the bans. webble's block is scoped to `**/*.{ts,tsx,mts,cts}` and still replaces the shared options for every TS file. Also, the shared path and pattern lists are module-private and not exported, so re-including them means copying them by hand. `@typescript-eslint/no-restricted-imports` is not set by the shared tier-3 config (checked), so it can carry the barrel paths without touching the core rule's options.
verify.skill: adjusted: The finding holds up. correctness.ts:25-28 sets the tier-0 'no-restricted-imports' error with the index.ts paths, and rules/index.ts:46-56 adds the src/ patterns for **/src files. lint-init.ts:132-138 appends an unscoped 'warn' block whose paths list only the barrels, and lintlint.ts:191-197 (isLintInitBarrelRestriction) exempts that block from rule-override. I reproduced the effect with ESLint 10.12 calculateConfigForFile on dist recommendedConfig({tier:3}). Without the block, src/index.ts resolves to [2,{paths:[./index.ts…],patterns:[**/src/**…]}]. With it, the rule resolves to [1,{paths:[{name:'@xylabs/hex'…}]}] for src/index.ts, foo.ts and README.md. The real configs are affected: xl1-faucet-twitter/eslint.config.ts:145-150 (unscoped, warn) and webble/eslint.config.ts:67-70. I lowered severity to medium for three reasons. Nothing fails; lint just gets quietly laxer. It only happens when someone accepts one of the @xylabs/@xyo-network barrel prompts, not in @ariestools-only repos. And the skill text is not itself wrong: it needs a caveat for a toolchain defect. The recommendation also needs a fix. Scoping the barrel block with `files` does not help: webble scopes to **/*.{ts,tsx,mts,cts} and still replaces the shared options for those files. Flat config replaces rule options per matching file, so the only fix is to re-include the shared options.

findings.title: lint init description is inaccurate: it is interactive, the barrel list is fixed, and it may install barrel packages
findings.current: eslint.md:16-22 "Prefer the generator: pnpm xy lint init … It detects React, installs the applicable config package and ESLint, generates `eslint.config.ts`, includes repository `.gitignore` behavior when the file exists, and derives root-barrel import restrictions from installed SDK barrels. Review the generated diff before accepting an overwrite."
findings.truth: `xy lint init` has no flags and no non-interactive mode. It reads stdin via readline for these prompts: first a 'Replace it with eslint.config.ts? (y/N)' confirmation, asked before anything is generated, so there is no diff to review at that point. Then one y/N prompt per hard-coded barrel: @xylabs/sdk-js, @xyo-network/sdk-js, @xyo-network/xl1-sdk and @xyo-network/chain-sdk, plus @xylabs/sdk-react, @xyo-network/react-chain and @xyo-network/react-sdk for React repos. @ariestools/sdk is not among them. If an accepted barrel is not installed, init adds it to devDependencies at `latest` and runs `pnpm install`. The disallowed list comes from deep analysis of what the barrel re-exports, and it steers sub-package imports toward the barrel. Init also deletes a legacy eslint.config.mjs. It adds devDeps `@ariestools/eslint-config(-react)-flat@^<toolchain>` and `eslint@^10.0.0`, then runs install.
findings.evidence: toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/lint-init.ts:21-29 (askConfirmation/readline), 56-68 (BARREL_DESCRIPTORS), 76-82 (eslint '^10.0.0'), 201-215 (ensureBarrelInstalled adds 'latest' + install), 243-253 (overwrite prompt before generation), 262-268 (per-barrel prompts), 280 (removeLegacyConfig); src/xy/lint/lint/initCommand.ts:6-13 (no options).

Say that accepting a barrel may add and install it at `latest`. Say the legacy eslint.config.mjs is removed. Tell agents to review with `git diff` afterwards, and in a non-interactive agent shell to ask the user to run it or hand-write the config from the documented template.

The overwrite prompt runs before any generation (243-253), and the per-barrel y/N prompts follow (262-268). ensureBarrelInstalled adds a missing barrel at 'latest' and runs install (201-215). removeLegacyConfig unlinks eslint.config.mjs (178-185, 280). The required devDeps are the config package at `^<toolchain>` and `eslint: '^10.0.0'` (76-82), followed by an install via shouldRunInstall. initCommand.ts:6-13 defines no options, and `xy lint init --help` shows only global flags. The skill's 'Review the generated diff before accepting an overwrite' cannot be done, because the prompt comes before anything is generated. None of these files changed after the 10.1.0 deploy.

findings.title: Peer requirements missing: eslint ^10.3 and eslint-import-resolver-typescript ^4.4
findings.current: eslint.md:14 "The current packages target ESLint 10 and use flat config."
findings.truth: Both config packages (v10.1.0 on npm) declare peerDependencies `eslint: ^10.3` and `eslint-import-resolver-typescript: ^4.4`. importConfig sets `import-x/resolver: { typescript: {...} }`, so the resolver must be installed in the consuming repo. `xy lint init` does not add the resolver, and it adds `eslint: ^10.0.0`, which is below the peer floor. Consumer repos install the resolver explicitly (~4.4.5).

findings.title: Lint execution modes and performance controls are missing, though SKILL.md sends 'lint performance' questions here
findings.current: absent (SKILL.md:38 routes "diagnosing lint performance" to eslint.md; the Commands table eslint.md:115-124 has no --mode/--profile/--jobs)
findings.truth: `xy lint --mode` takes package-workers (the default: persistent worker pool), shared-typecheck (experimental: shared TypeScript ingestion, semantic phase runs without the ESLint cache) and workspace-eslint (direct workspace ESLint CLI; a package target delegates to that package's lint script). The hidden `--next`/`--prev` flags are deprecated aliases. `-p/--profile` prints per-package config/lint/spawn timings, and `-j/--jobs` caps parallelism. `XY_LINT_WORKER_MAX_RSS_MB` (default 2048) sets the RSS budget at which a worker is recycled. Workers are recycled to prevent out-of-memory failures on large monorepos.
findings.evidence: `node packages/toolchain/dist/bin/xy.mjs lint --help` (shows --mode choices, --profile, --jobs); toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/lintMode.ts:1-9; src/xy/lint/lint/runCommand.ts:43-60; `xy.mjs --stability --json` experimentalConfig {id:'lint.mode.shared-typecheck'}; src/xy/stability.ts:158-160; docs/STABILITY.md:61; packages/toolchain/README.md:240-266; src/actions/lintNextWorker.ts:381-382; commit bc8e52802 (2026-09-25).
findings.recommendation: Add a short 'Performance' subsection to eslint.md. Cover `xy lint --mode package-workers|shared-typecheck|workspace-eslint`: package-workers is the default and shared-typecheck is experimental per `xy --stability`. Cover `XY_LINT_WORKER_MAX_RSS_MB` (default 2048) for memory-bound runners, and say to use `--mode` instead of the deprecated `--next`/`--prev`. Point to the global `--jobs` and `--profile` controls in commands.md rather than re-documenting them.

findings.title: All-workspace xy lint runs incrementally by default and can lint nothing; the troubleshooting section does not say so
findings.current: eslint.md:132 "If no files are linted, verify workspace discovery, source globs, meta-package handling, and `--skip-empty`."
findings.truth: runCommand passes `incremental: argv.incremental !== false`, so incremental mode is on unless disabled. When no package is given and neither --fix nor --analyze is set, `xy lint` lints only the workspaces changed since the last clean snapshot. If none changed it prints 'No changed packages to lint.' and exits 0. `--no-incremental`, or `--fresh` (which clears the snapshot), forces a full run. Other relevant flags: `--meta full|skip` (default full), `--no-skip-empty`, and `-c/--no-cache`.
findings.evidence: toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/xy/lint/lint/runCommand.ts:27-32,77-88,124; src/actions/lint.ts:94-98,154-156; src/actions/relint.ts:53-57 (clearIncrementalSnapshot); packages/toolchain/README.md:262-263 ('Repository-level incremental linting'). toolchain.md:108 mentions incremental only for compile/build.
findings.recommendation: In eslint.md's Commands/troubleshooting, say that all-workspace `xy lint` (with no package, no --fix and no --analyze) is incremental against the last clean run and may print 'No changed packages to lint.' Say that `--no-incremental` forces a full run. List `--meta full|skip` (default full), `--no-skip-empty` and `--no-cache`. Also broaden commands.md:27 and toolchain.md:108 so `--no-incremental` and incremental defaults cover lint, not only compile/build.

verify.code: confirmed: In runCommand.ts:124, `incremental: argv.incremental !== false`. lint.ts:94-98 enables incremental lint when no package is given and neither fix nor analyze is set. lint.ts:198-205 skips this in workspace-eslint mode. When nothing is affected, lint.ts:154-164 prints 'No changed packages to lint.' and returns 0. relint.ts:53-57 clears the snapshot, and incremental.ts:513 then forces a full plan ('no previous snapshot'). The defaults in `--help` are --meta full, --skip-empty true and --cache true. In the skills, toolchain.md:108 describes incremental behaviour only for compile/build, and commands.md:27 frames `--no-incremental` as compile/build-only. One nuance: the snapshot is written only after a clean run (lint.ts:173-182), so the no-op is safe but surprising. Medium is appropriate.
verify.skill: adjusted: The behavior is real. runCommand.ts:124 passes `incremental: argv.incremental !== false`. lint.ts:94-98 uses incremental mode when no package is given and neither --fix nor --analyze is set, and lint.ts:154-165 prints 'No changed packages to lint.' and returns 0. The skill is silent on this. commands.md:27 and toolchain.md:108 describe incremental behavior and `--no-incremental` only for compile/build. Severity is overstated, though. The snapshot is written only after a clean result (lint.ts:173-181). Changes to the root eslint/tsconfig/xy config (incremental.ts:170-178) and to the lockfile (incremental.ts:445-446, 513-521) force a full run. findings.title: Hand-written template differs from the generator output it calls canonical (Markdown ignored, Storybook always added)
findings.current: eslint.md:28-36 "Use the generator's output as canonical" followed by `{ ignores: ['build', '**/build/**', 'dist', '**/dist/**', 'node_modules/**'] }`; eslint.md:70 "Add `configReactStorybook` explicitly only when Storybook files need that layer"
findings.truth: The generator emits `{ ignores: ['.yarn/**', 'build', '**/build/**', '**/dist/**', 'dist', 'node_modules/**', '**/node_modules/**', '**/*.md', '.claude/worktrees/*'] }`. The `**/*.md` entry means generated configs (and consumer repos such as sdk-js and cli-kit) never run the tier-0 Markdown rules, while the skill's template would. For React, the generator always spreads `...configReactStorybook`.
findings.evidence: toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/lint-init.ts:129-130; ariestools/sdk-js/eslint.config.ts:14 and ariestools/cli-kit/eslint.config.ts:14 (same ignores incl. '**/*.md').
findings.recommendation: Either copy the generator's ignores into the template, or keep the minimal one and state that generated configs ignore `**/*.md`, so Markdown rules apply only if that entry is removed. Say that `lint init` always adds `configReactStorybook` for React repos and that agents may remove it when there are no stories.

verify.code: confirmed: lint-init.ts:129 emits the ignores `['.yarn/**','build','**/build/**','**/dist/**','dist','node_modules/**','**/node_modules/**','**/*.md','.claude/worktrees/*']`, and line 130 always spreads `...configReactStorybook` for React. sdk-js/eslint.config.ts:14 and cli-kit/eslint.config.ts:14 also carry `'**/*.md'`. findings.title: xy lint lint coverage is thin: rule ids, --rules, config levels, legacy @xylabs migration, tier-2 comparison baseline
findings.current: eslint.md:122-123 "`xy lint lint` | Check the local config against toolchain conventions" / "`xy lint lint --fix` | Normalize supported config-package, rule, and `.gitignore` issues"
findings.truth: The rules are lintlint.config-package (fixable), lintlint.gitignore (fixable), lintlint.redundant-rule (fixable) and lintlint.rule-override (report only), all at warn level. `xy lint lint --rules` lists them, and `commands.lintLint.rules` in xy.config changes their levels. config-package detects `@xylabs/eslint-config(-react)-flat`, and `--fix` rewrites the import and the devDependency to `@ariestools/*` before running install. `xy check` runs lint lint. Redundant and override detection compares against the shared package's deprecated `config` export, which is tier 2 type-checked, plus Storybook for React. It does not use the repo's chosen tier, so local settings for tier-3/4-only rules show up as additions rather than overrides.
findings.evidence: `node packages/toolchain/dist/bin/xy.mjs lint lint --rules` (4-rule table); toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/lintlint.ts:127-130 (config ?? default), 274-301 (fixConfigMismatch), 328-405 (LINTLINT_RULES); src/actions/barrel/restrictionHelpers.ts:28-33; src/actions/package/compile/XyConfig.ts:632; docs/xy-config.md:45; eslint-config-flat/src/tiers/index.ts:85.
findings.recommendation: List the four rule ids (lintlint.config-package, lintlint.gitignore, lintlint.redundant-rule, lintlint.rule-override), `xy lint lint --rules`, and `commands.lintLint.rules` for setting their levels. Say that `xy check` and `xy check --fix` run it. Note that `xy lint lint --fix` is the migration path off the retired `@xylabs/eslint-config(-react)-flat` packages: it rewrites the import and the devDependency and then installs. Add a caveat that redundant/override analysis compares against the deprecated tier-2 type-checked `config` export, not the repo's chosen tier. In a tier-3 or tier-4 repo, a deliberate override that equals the tier-2 value (for example `@typescript-eslint/strict-boolean-expressions: 'off'`) is classed as redundant, and `--fix` removes it. Settings that equal the tier-3 value are reported as overrides. Agents should review `lintlint.redundant-rule` findings before accepting `--fix`.

verify.code: adjusted: Mostly confirmed. `xy lint lint --rules` lists the 4 rules (config-package fixable, gitignore fixable, redundant-rule fixable, rule-override not fixable), all at warn. restrictionHelpers.ts:28-33 detects @xylabs config packages. fixConfigMismatch (lintlint.ts:263-289) rewrites the import and the devDependency, then runs install. checkCommand.ts:67 runs lintlint, including under --fix. `commands.lintLint` exists in committed XyConfig.ts and docs/xy-config.md:45. The baseline is the deprecated `config` export (lintlint.ts:127-130), which is tier 2 type-checked (eslint-config-flat tiers/index.ts:85; React adds Storybook). The finding's stated consequence is wrong, though. A merge of dist rules shows 0 rule names that exist only at tier 3, so 'tier-3/4-only rules show up as additions' does not happen. Instead, 62 rules have different values at tier 2 and tier 3. A local setting equal to the tier-2 value counts as redundant: for example, `'@typescript-eslint/strict-boolean-expressions': 'off'` in a tier-3 repo, where tier 2 is 'off' and tier 3 is 'error' (isRulesMatching at lintlint.ts:85-87). `xy lint lint --fix` and `xy check --fix` would then delete that deliberate override and re-enable the rule as an error. A local setting equal to the tier-3 value is reported as an override. The skill tells agents to rely on `xy lint lint --fix` (eslint.md:64-68,123,130), so this is more than polish.
verify.skill: confirmed: `xy.mjs lint lint --rules` prints four warn-level rules: lintlint.config-package (fix), lintlint.gitignore (fix), lintlint.redundant-rule (fix) and lintlint.rule-override (no fix). restrictionHelpers.ts:28-33 detects @xylabs/eslint-config(-react)-flat. lintlint.ts:270-290 rewrites the import and devDependency to @ariestools/* and then runs install. lintlint.ts:127-130 compares against the shared `config` export, which tiers/index.ts:85 defines as the deprecated tier-2 type-checked config. docs/xy-config.md:45 lists commands.lintLint. The skill covers `--rules` and `commands.<cmd>.rules` only generically (commands.md:23, 292-322). findings.title: --fresh silently drops --fix, --type-checked, --analyze, --skip-empty and --meta
findings.current: eslint.md:119 "`xy lint --fresh` | Clear lint caches and run from a fresh snapshot"; eslint.md:126 "Use `--fresh` when config changes …"
findings.truth: With --fresh, runCommand calls relint({ gitignore, jobs, mode, pkg, verbose }) and nothing else. relint then runs lint with cache:false and fix undefined, so `xy lint --fresh --fix` does not fix anything, and --type-checked, --analyze, --skip-empty and --meta are ignored. This is a toolchain defect, but agents should not combine these flags.
findings.evidence: toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/xy/lint/lint/runCommand.ts:108-116; src/actions/relint.ts:45-57.
findings.recommendation: Add a note that `--fresh` should be run on its own, followed by a separate `xy lint --fix` or `--type-checked …` run if needed. Optionally file a toolchain issue.

verify.code: confirmed: runCommand.ts:108-116 calls relint with only gitignore, jobs, mode, pkg and verbose when --fresh is set. relint.ts:45-57 calls lint with cache:false and fix undefined, plus no analyze, typeChecked, skipEmpty, meta or profile. So `xy lint --fresh --fix` does not fix, and --type-checked, --analyze, --no-skip-empty, --meta and --profile are ignored. Unchanged since the 10.1.0 deploy. This is a toolchain defect, and a skill note is a low-severity mitigation.
verify.skill: confirmed: runCommand.ts:108-116 passes only gitignore, jobs, mode, pkg and verbose to relint, and relint.ts:45-57 calls lint with `cache:false` and an undefined fix. In workspace-eslint mode, relintAllPackages({fix}) also receives an undefined fix. As a result `--fix`, `--type-checked`, `--analyze`, `--skip-empty`, `--meta` and `--profile` are silently dropped when combined with `--fresh`. findings.title: Install command fails at a pnpm monorepo root because it has no -w flag
findings.current: toolchain.md:43-45 gives `pnpm add -D @ariestools/toolchain @ariestools/tsconfig typescript`, and toolchain.md:51 says `xy` runs at repository/workspace scope.
findings.truth: The toolchain is installed at the repo root because `xy` must run from there. In a multi-package pnpm workspace, `pnpm add` refuses to add to the root unless you pass `-w` / `--workspace-root` (or `--ignore-workspace-root-check`). The scaffolded monorepo also puts @ariestools/toolchain in the root devDependencies. So the command as written fails in the default (monorepo) topology.
findings.evidence: Command `pnpm --version` printed 12.4.2. Command `pnpm add --help` lists `--ignore-workspace-root-check  Permit adding dependencies to a multi-package workspace root without -w` and `-w, --workspace-root`. toolchain/packages/toolchain/README.md:54 says to run `xy` from the repository root. toolchain/packages/toolchain/templates/repo/cli/root/package.json.tmpl:39-50 puts @ariestools/toolchain in the root devDependencies.
findings.recommendation: Show two forms: `pnpm add -D -w @ariestools/toolchain @ariestools/tsconfig typescript eslint` for a monorepo root, and the same command without `-w` for a single-package repo. Add one sentence saying toolchain/config/eslint/typescript/vitest devDependencies belong on the root package.

verify.code: confirmed: Checked against the source. toolchain.md:44 is `pnpm add -D @ariestools/toolchain @ariestools/tsconfig typescript` with no -w. pnpm 12.4.2's `pnpm add --help` lists `--ignore-workspace-root-check  Permit adding dependencies to a multi-package workspace root without -w` and `-w, --workspace-root`, so the bare form is refused at a monorepo root. toolchain/packages/toolchain/README.md:54 says to run `xy` from the repository root. templates/repo/cli/root/package.json.tmpl:39-51 puts @ariestools/toolchain, the config packages, eslint, typescript and vitest in the root devDependencies, and resolvePlan.ts:227 defaults to a monorepo. The command therefore fails in the default topology. pnpm's error names -w, but the vocabulary defines a failing command as high.

findings.title: pnpm-workspace.yaml and its release-age/verify settings are required in every pnpm repo; the skill says 'when needed'
findings.current: toolchain.md:37 says "For pnpm workspaces, keep `pnpm-workspace.yaml` at the repository root." toolchain.md:114 says "Pin pnpm in `packageManager` and create the correct workspace file when needed."
findings.truth: `xy check` runs `xy packman lint`, which is stable. For any pnpm repo, single-package or monorepo, it raises errors (exit code is non-zero) unless pnpm-workspace.yaml contains three settings: `minimumReleaseAge` of at least 1440 minutes, a `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` covering the scopes actually used (@ariestools/*, @xylabs/*, @xyo-network/*), and `verifyDepsBeforeRun`. If the file is missing, the check reports "No pnpm-workspace.yaml found", and `--fix` cannot create it. Separately, `xy repo lint` raises an error if a pnpm monorepo declares `workspaces` in package.json (`repo.workspaces-field-placement`).
findings.evidence: Command `xy.mjs packman lint --rules` shows packman.pnpm.minimumReleaseAge, packman.pnpm.minimumReleaseAgeExclude and packman.pnpm.verifyDepsBeforeRun, all at level error. toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/packman/lint.ts:147-169 (needs the yaml file, reads minimumReleaseAge from it), :172-174 (fix returns false when the file is missing), :39 (DEFAULT_VERIFY_DEPS_BEFORE_RUN='warn'). toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/lib/pnpmConfig/readMinReleaseAge.ts:12 (floor 1440). toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/releaseAgeExcludeScopes.ts:6. toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/xy/common/checkCommand.ts:13,55-56 (check runs packman lint). toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/package-lint.ts:176-197 (pnpm: no package.json `workspaces`). toolchain/docs/STABILITY.md:84 (packman lint is stable and part of xy check). The toolchain's own pnpm-workspace.yaml:7-10 is a working example.

findings.title: Root scripts example uses `vitest run` and leaves out how `xy` defers to same-named root scripts
findings.current: toolchain.md:96-106 shows root scripts build/compile/lint/`lint:fix: xy lint --fix`/`"test": "vitest run"`. This conflicts with toolchain.md:23 ("Do not substitute a raw ... Vitest invocation for a repository wrapper"). Root-script deferral is not mentioned anywhere in the file.
findings.truth: When you run `xy <command>` with no subcommand and the root package.json has a script of the same name, xy hands off to that script (`pnpm run <command>`). XY_LOCAL_SCRIPT=1 stops this from recursing, and `--no-defer` or `XY_NO_DEFER=1` turns it off. With the skill's example, `pnpm xy test` silently runs `vitest run` and skips `xy test`'s target handling. The package README hello-world and the `xy repo init` template both use `build/compile/lint/fix/test/check` mapped to `xy <cmd>`, including `"test": "xy test"` and `"check": "xy check"`.
findings.evidence: toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/xy/xyParseOptions.ts:60-67. toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/lib/tryRunLocalScript.ts:13-52 (root scripts only, XY_LOCAL_SCRIPT guard, delegates via `run <name>`). Output of `xy.mjs --help` shows `--no-defer  Do not defer to local package.json script of the same name`. toolchain/packages/toolchain/README.md:22-32. toolchain/packages/toolchain/templates/repo/cli/root/package.json.tmpl:28-35.
findings.recommendation:
Change the example to `"test": "xy test"` and add `"fix": "xy fix"` and `"check": "xy check"` (`lint:fix` may stay). Add a paragraph explaining deferral:
- When `xy <cmd>` is run with no positional arguments and the root package.json has a script with the same name, xy runs that script instead (`<pm> run <cmd>`, with flags forwarded). For example, a root `"build": "tsc -b"` would make `pnpm xy build` run tsc.
- `"build": "xy build"` is safe because of the XY_LOCAL_SCRIPT recursion guard.
- A positional target such as `xy test packages/foo` is never deferred.
- `--no-defer` or `XY_NO_DEFER=1` forces the built-in command.

verify.code: adjusted: The core issue is real, but the stated failure scenario is overstated. xyParseOptions.ts:60-67 defers to a same-named root script, and tryRunLocalScript.ts:13-52 shows the XY_LOCAL_SCRIPT=1 recursion guard and delegation via `<pm> run <name>`, with extra args forwarded. `--no-defer` and XY_NO_DEFER=1 disable it. The README hello-world (README.md:22-32) and the template (package.json.tmpl:28-35) use `"test": "xy test"` plus fix/check. The example at toolchain.md:103 contradicts the skill's own rule at :23. However, the middleware returns early when `argv._.length > 1` (xyParseOptions.ts:63), so `xy test <target>` is never deferred and target handling is not skipped. Deferral prints 'Delegating "test" to local script', so it is not silent. Bare `xy test` runs `vitest .` (actions/test.ts:13-14), which is close to `vitest run`. The real harm is the undocumented deferral behavior and the self-contradicting example. Medium still fits.

findings.title: 'Require Node.js 22' step does not match the enforced engines/volta placement policy
findings.current: toolchain.md:115 says "Require Node.js 22 or newer unless the consuming product imposes a newer version."
findings.truth:
Where the Node requirement goes depends on the package:
- The root package must not declare `engines`. `repo.engines-non-terminal` is an error with the message "use volta instead".
- Private (terminal) workspace packages must not declare `engines`.
- Non-private workspace packages must declare `engines`.
- Publishable packages with Node exports need `engines.node` inside ">=22" (node.engines-node-range).
- Browser/neutral-only packages must not declare `engines.node` (node.engines-node-portable).
- The root `volta.node` should track the latest Node (node.volta-node-latest). The toolchain root itself uses volta node "26".
- The engines and volta values must include the latest Node version (repo.engines-lts, error).

An agent that adds `engines.node >=22` at the root, or to a neutral library, trips these rules.
findings.evidence: Output of `xy.mjs repo lint --rules`: repo.engines-non-terminal (error), repo.engines-lts (error), repo.volta-only-root (error). toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/package-lint-engines.ts:71-87. toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/node-lint.ts:18 (REQUIRED_NODE_RANGE='>=22'), :110-166. Output of `xy.mjs node lint --rules`. toolchain/package.json:50-52 (volta node 26, no engines).
findings.recommendation:
Replace step 2 with placement rules.

In a monorepo (repo lint applies only there):
- Pin Node at the root through `volta.node`, tracking the latest Node. Do not give the root an `engines` field (repo.engines-non-terminal, error).
- Every non-private workspace package declares `engines`. The convention is `engines.node: ">=22"` or newer, and the range must include the latest Node (repo.engines-lts).
- Private workspace packages declare no `engines`, and only the root declares `volta`.

In a single-package repo, the root is the published package and declares `engines.node`.

Point to `pnpm xy repo lint --fix`. Mention `xy node lint` as an advisory, warn-level check that also verifies Node-exporting packages stay within >=22.

verify.code:
adjusted: The core issue is real: toolchain.md:115 gives no placement guidance, and repo lint enforces placement. Several details are off, though:
- Scope: repo lint only runs for monorepos (package-lint.ts:534-537 'Not a monorepo — skipping repo lint checks'). The 'no root engines' rule (package-lint-engines.ts:71-75) does not apply to single-package repos.
- Levels: all node.* rules are warn-level (`xy node lint --rules`), and node lint is not part of `xy check` (checkCommand.ts runs git/packman/publint/repo/lint/skills only). repo.engines-lts errors only on engines ranges; a lagging volta pin is a warning (package-lint-engines.ts:195-216).
- Recommendation conflict: 'leave engines.node off browser/neutral-only packages' clashes with repo.engines-non-terminal (error), which requires every non-private workspace package to declare engines (package-lint-engines.ts:85-86). It also clashes with practice: every toolchain package, including neutral lib-neutral and the tsconfig packages, declares engines.node '>=22', and every sdk-js package declares '>=26'.
The rest is confirmed: root engines is an error in monorepos, volta-only-root is an error, REQUIRED_NODE_RANGE is '>=22' (node-lint.ts:18), and the toolchain root uses volta node '26' with no engines.

The CLI has `-e/--exclude` and `--include` (by check name), `--fresh` (clear the incremental snapshot), and `--pack` (default true; packs before linting).

findings.title: Missing `nodeTrack` config for `repo.engines-lts` / `node.volta-node-latest` (LTS-pinned repos fail `xy check`)
findings.current: absent. commands.md:160-161 mention only engines and "Root Volta pin and package `engines.node` portability". No skill mentions nodeTrack.

Both default to 'current'. Repos pinned to LTS must set both to 'lts'.
findings.evidence: toolchain/docs/xy-config.md:46-55 (`commands.repoLint.nodeTrack` ('current' default, or 'lts') … `commands.nodeLint.nodeTrack`). toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/package/compile/XyConfig.ts:597,606. package-lint.ts:404-408 (repo.engines-lts uses nodeTrack). `xy.mjs repo lint --rules`: `error repo.engines-lts`. findings.recommendation: Under Repository policy, add a note: 'Repos that track the Node LTS line set `commands: { repoLint: { nodeTrack: 'lts' }, nodeLint: { nodeTrack: 'lts' } }`. With the default (`current`), `repo.engines-lts` (run by `xy check`) warns when the root volta pin is older than the latest Current Node, which fails under `--strict`. It errors when an `engines` range excludes the latest Current. `xy node lint --fix` rewrites `volta.node` to the latest Current, so set nodeTrack before running it in an LTS repo.'

verify.code: adjusted: The config is real and absent from the skills. XyConfig.ts:590-607 defines NodeReleaseTrack 'current'|'lts' on RepoLintConfig and NodeLintConfig (default current). xy-config.md documents both. Commit a2b5c6ea3 (2026-09-16) is in v10.1.0, and grep of skills/ finds no nodeTrack. The failure mode is overstated, though. package-lint-engines.ts:176-220 checks against nodeCurrent 26.8.2 (lib/latestVersions.ts:6): an engines range that does not satisfy that version is an error, but a volta pin older than it is only a warning. node.volta-node-latest is warn level, and node lint is not part of `xy check` (checkCommand.ts:48-70). So an LTS repo fails `xy check` only when its engines range is capped below the current Node (e.g. `^24`), or under --strict. A repo with `engines.node: '>=24'` and volta 24.x only warns.
verify.skill: adjusted: The gap is real: `grep nodeTrack skills/` finds nothing, and XyConfig.ts:592-608 and xy-config.md document `commands.repoLint.nodeTrack` and `commands.nodeLint.nodeTrack` (default 'current'). Many workspace repos pin volta.node to 24.x (LTS), e.g. xyo-skills, this repo, clients and modular-one, so it matters. But the mechanism is overstated. In package-lint-engines.ts:176-216 (checkVersionsIncludeLts), an older volta pin is pushed to `warnings`, and lintResultDiagnostics in package-lint.ts:286-304 emits it at 'warn'. Only an engines range that excludes the latest Current (26.8.2) is an error. So an LTS repo with `engines.node: ">=24"` gets a warning in `xy check`, which fails only under --strict. The bigger hazard is node-lint.ts:81-99: `xy node lint --fix` overwrites root volta.node with the latest Current (26.8.2) unless nodeTrack is 'lts'. node lint is not part of xy check. Severity stays medium because of that silent wrong-config rewrite.

findings.title: Auth-wrapping fetcher example spreads a Headers instance and silently drops every SDK header, including Content-Encoding: gzip
findings.current: fetch.md:39-40: `const fetcher: FetchFunction = (input, init) =>\n  globalThis.fetch(input, { ...init, headers: { ...init?.headers, authorization: token } })`
findings.truth: fetchJson and FetchClient always pass a `Headers` instance to the fetcher: fetchJson.ts:40 and FetchClient.ts:174 use `buildHeaders()`, which returns `new Headers()` (fetchJson.ts:9-20, FetchClient.ts:60-71), and fetchCompress.ts:58-63 builds `new Headers(init.headers)` when it compresses. A Headers object has no own enumerable properties, so `{ ...init?.headers }` is `{}`. The wrapped request then loses Accept, Content-Type: application/json and, for gzip-compressed bodies (default for bodies over 1024 chars), Content-Encoding: gzip. The server receives gzip bytes with no encoding header.
findings.evidence: `node -e` on Node v26.9.0: spreading `new Headers({Accept,'Content-Type','Content-Encoding':'gzip'})` into `{...h, authorization:'tok'}` printed `{"authorization":"tok"}`. Rebuilding with `new Headers(init.headers); headers.set('authorization', ...)` kept all four headers. Source: sdk-js packages/sdk/src/modules/fetch/fetchJson.ts:9-20,38-41; FetchClient.ts:60-71,171-182; fetchCompress.ts:49,55-68. Test fetchJson.spec.ts:105 casts `call[1]?.headers as Headers`.
findings.recommendation: Replace the example with a version that keeps the existing headers: `const fetcher: FetchFunction = (input, init) => { const headers = new Headers(init?.headers); headers.set('authorization', token); return globalThis.fetch(input, { ...init, headers }) }`. Add one sentence: init.headers reaching a fetcher is a `Headers` instance, so never object-spread it. For auth that does not need transport control, prefer client-level `headers` config.

verify.code: confirmed: Checked against source and at runtime. FetchClient.ts:60-71,174 and fetchJson.ts:9-20,40 always pass a `new Headers()` to the fetcher, and fetchCompress.ts:58-63 rebuilds `new Headers(init.headers)` and adds Content-Encoding: gzip when the body is over compressMinLength (default 1024, fetchCompress.ts:49). Test 1: I ran the built SDK (packages/sdk/dist/neutral/fetch.mjs, sdk-js main = v9.0.1 Deploy 298fbb5bb) with the exact fetcher from fetch.md:39-40 and `client.post('/item', {big:'x'.repeat(2000)})`. The fetcher received a Headers instance (`isHeaders: true`) and an ArrayBuffer (gzip) body. The resulting Request carried only `authorization`, so Accept, Content-Type: application/json and Content-Encoding: gzip were all dropped. Test 2: a plain `node -e` spread of a Headers object gave `{"authorization":"tok"}`, and a Request built from it fell back to content-type text/plain. Following the skill sends gzip bytes with no encoding header, so severity high holds. The recommended fix (rebuild with `new Headers(init?.headers)` and `.set`) keeps all four headers, which I also checked.
verify.skill: confirmed: fetch.md:39-40 matches the quote exactly. fetchJson (fetchJson.ts:40) and FetchClient.request (FetchClient.ts:174) always pass buildHeaders(), which returns `new Headers()` (fetchJson.ts:9-20, FetchClient.ts:60-71). fetchCompress passes that object through (fetchCompress.ts:68), or swaps in a new `new Headers(init.headers)` when it gzips (fetchCompress.ts:58-63). On Node v26.9.0, `JSON.stringify({...new Headers({Accept,'Content-Type','Content-Encoding':'gzip'}), authorization:'tok'})` printed `{"authorization":"tok"}`. So a fetcher written from the skill sends gzip bytes with no Content-Encoding header and drops Content-Type and Accept. That is a broken request, so high severity is right. No other skill file covers this (grep for Headers or fetcher found nothing outside fetch.md). The recommended fix (`new Headers(init?.headers)` + `set`) keeps all headers, as verified.

findings.title: HTTP-status semantics missing: fetchJson never throws on non-2xx, while FetchClient throws FetchClientError per validateStatus
findings.current: fetch.md:30 lists only `FetchError`, `isFetchError`, `toFetchError`, `classifyFetchError`. fetch.md:117 warns only about retries and caching. The file never says which entry points throw on HTTP error statuses.
findings.truth: fetchJson and the fetchJson* helpers resolve on 4xx/5xx with `status` set. `data` is the best-effort parsed body, or null when it is malformed. They throw FetchError only for transport, parse-on-success and policy failures. FetchClient, FetchJsonClient and fetchJsonClient throw `FetchClientError` (a FetchError subclass with type 'http-status', `.response` and `.config`) when `validateStatus` rejects the status. The default accepts 200-299. A custom function overrides it, and `validateStatus: null` never throws. FetchClientError is exported but not mentioned.
findings.evidence: sdk-js packages/sdk/src/modules/fetch/fetchJson.ts:43-45 (non-ok -> tryParseJson, no throw); parseJson.ts:60-82; FetchClient.ts:16-21,34-58,197-211; index.ts:2 exports FetchClientError. Tests: fetchJson.spec.ts:81-86 ('does not throw for a non-JSON error body (returns null)', status 500); FetchClient.spec.ts:264-307 (FetchClientError, validateStatus null and custom).
findings.recommendation: Add a short 'Errors and HTTP status' subsection. Use fetchJson* when you want to branch on `status` yourself and check `status`/`response.ok`; it never throws for HTTP status. Use FetchClient/fetchJsonClient for Axios-style throw-on-non-2xx, catching `FetchClientError` (or `isFetchError(e) && e.type === 'http-status'`). Document `validateStatus` (function or null). Add `FetchClientError` to the list at line 30, and extend line 117 to: do not assume fetchJson throws on non-2xx.

findings.title: Bounded, cancellable response reads (maxResponseBytes, timeout, signal, readResponseText) shipped in v8.2.0 but are absent
findings.current: absent. The file predates the feature: its only commit is 8a7d4f0 (2026-07-31).
findings.truth: Since sdk-js b86f3a024 (2026-08-27, first in v8.2.0, present in v9.0.1), fetchJson, FetchClient and FetchJsonClient accept `maxResponseBytes`. It must be a positive safe integer and is validated before any I/O (RangeError otherwise). It counts decoded stream bytes incrementally and applies to non-2xx bodies too. FetchClient also takes `timeout` (ms; 0 disables), which composes with the caller `signal` (first abort wins). The signal stays active through body consumption. Failures are FetchError with type 'response-too-large', 'aborted' or 'timeout'. When a cap or signal is set, non-2xx read errors propagate instead of becoming `data: null`, and `validateStatus: null` does not disable this. `readResponseText(response, { maxResponseBytes, signal })` is exported for text bodies, with `ReadResponseTextOptions` available from `@ariestools/sdk/fetch/model`. The README also notes the SDK adds no SSRF, redirect or credentials policy, so callers should set `redirect: 'error'` and `credentials: 'omit'` when required.

findings.title: Injected-fetcher contract missing: non-WHATWG bodies (node-fetch, cross-fetch, RN polyfills) fall back to buffered text() (v9.0.1 fix)
findings.current: fetch.md:32-45 ('Injecting a fetcher') only shows how to pass a FetchFunction. It says nothing about what the returned Response must support.
findings.truth: sdk-js 158476cd7 (2026-09-18, merged 2026-09-24 as 'claude/fetch-non-stream-bodies', shipped in v9.0.1) changed readResponseText. When a cap or signal is set, a response whose body lacks getReader() is now read with response.text() instead of throwing. That covers the Node Readable from node-fetch/cross-fetch, the undefined body of whatwg-fetch/React Native polyfills, and Response-like test doubles. With this fallback, abort rejects promptly but cannot cancel the body, and maxResponseBytes is checked only after the whole body is buffered, against the UTF-8 byte length. Injected fetchers must also honor the provided signal while acquiring the response.
findings.evidence: sdk-js packages/sdk/src/modules/fetch/readResponseText.ts:129-146 (isReadableStream / readBufferedText), 156-161 (doc comment), 173-180; README.md:169-170 ('Injected fetchers must honor the provided signal...'), 201-206. Commit 158476cd7 message; `git merge-base --is-ancestor 158476cd7 v9.0.1` succeeded.
findings.recommendation: In 'Injecting a fetcher' (fetch.md:32-45), add one line: a FetchFunction must forward the given `init`, in particular `init.signal`, so timeouts and aborts cancel the request, and must preserve `init.headers` (see finding 0). In the bounded-reads section proposed in finding 3, add two sentences from README.md:201-206: a Response whose body is not a WHATWG ReadableStream (node-fetch or cross-fetch Readable, whatwg-fetch/React Native polyfills, Response-like test doubles) is read with response.text(). In that case abort only stops waiting, and maxResponseBytes is checked only after the whole body is buffered, so it no longer bounds memory. Optionally note that this fallback requires @ariestools/sdk >= 9.0.1.

verify.code: adjusted: The facts check out. readResponseText.ts:129-146 and 168-180 fall back to response.text() for non-WHATWG bodies, but only when maxResponseBytes or signal is set; line 171 uses plain response.text() when neither is set. Commit 158476cd7 (2026-09-18) was merged at 69534d452 (2026-09-24), and `git merge-base --is-ancestor 158476cd7 v9.0.1` succeeds. README.md:169-170 says injected fetchers must honor the signal. The recommendation's version note is too broad, though. 'Needs >= 9.0.1; earlier versions threw' holds only for policy-bound reads: maxResponseBytes, a signal, or a FetchClient `timeout`, which creates a signal (FetchClient.ts:169). Those reads threw only in 8.2.0-8.3.x, since the policy path was introduced in 8.2.0 (b86f3a024). Plain fetches through node-fetch etc. worked on every version. The skill's existing examples (globalThis.fetch, undici fetch) already return WHATWG streams and forward `init.signal` through `...init`. Medium is still defensible because the memory cap silently stops bounding memory with such fetchers.
verify.skill: adjusted: The facts check out. readResponseText.ts:129-146 and 156-161 add the non-WHATWG fallback to response.text(). 158476cd7 (2026-09-18) is an ancestor of v9.0.1 and not of v8.3.0. Its commit message confirms that earlier versions threw 'body.getReader is not a function', and v8.3.0's readResponseText.ts:148 called body.getReader() unconditionally. README.md:169-170 says injected fetchers must honor the signal. Medium overstates the impact, though. The fallback is a robustness fix that makes non-native fetchers work. It only matters with a cap or signal and a non-WHATWG body, which is rare on the SDK's Node >=26 baseline with native fetch. Both fetcher examples in the skill already forward `init`, signal included (fetch.md:40,76). The most important point, that a fetcher must forward `init`, overlaps with finding 0. This is a contract detail, not a missing feature surface, so low fits better. The details belong in the bounded-reads section from finding 3.

findings.title: Request-side behavior undocumented: default gzip of bodies over 1024 chars, data/body serialization, baseURL resolution, shallow-merged client defaults
findings.current: fetch.md:7 names `fetchCompress` without explaining it. fetch.md:24-25 shows only `baseURL`, and fetch.md:28 lists the method helpers without saying how they treat request bodies.
findings.truth: (1) By default, compression is on for every helper: any request body whose string form exceeds `compressMinLength` (default 1024) is gzip-compressed and sent with `Content-Encoding: gzip`, so the server must accept gzip request bodies. Raise `compressMinLength` to opt out. (2) fetchJson's `body` is a native BodyInit sent as-is (pass a JSON string). fetchJsonPost/Put/Patch(url, data, options) and client.post/put/patch(url, data) JSON.stringify `data`. (3) FetchClient resolves `url` against `baseURL` with WHATWG `new URL(path, base)`, so `/item` against `https://api.example.com/v1` yields `https://api.example.com/item`; this differs from Axios-style joining. (4) Instance defaults are shallow-merged beneath per-request config, so a per-request `headers` or `params` replaces the client's rather than merging. Other config: `params`, `timeout`, `validateStatus`, `fetcher`, plus native RequestInit fields.
findings.evidence: sdk-js packages/sdk/src/modules/fetch/fetchCompress.ts:15-26,47-68 (default 1024 at :49); FetchJsonClient.ts:8-13; methods.ts:13-37; FetchClient.ts:9-32,73-83,97,152,178-180; FetchClient.spec.ts:193-199 (instance params {a} + request params {b} -> '?b=2'). `node -p "new URL('/item','https://api.example.com/v1').href"` -> https://api.example.com/item.
findings.recommendation: Add a compact 'Request options' table: baseURL (WHATWG resolution; use a trailing slash and a relative path to keep a base path), params, headers, timeout, validateStatus, compressMinLength (default 1024; gzip on by default), fetcher, maxResponseBytes. Add a note that per-request config shallow-replaces client defaults, including headers and params. Add one line that fetchJson takes a string `body` while the method helpers and client methods take `data`.

verify.code: confirmed: All four sub-claims check out. (1) fetchCompress.ts:49 sets compressMinLength = 1024 by default, and :55-63 gzip any body whose string length exceeds it and set Content-Encoding: gzip. Every helper goes through fetchCompress (fetchJson.ts:38, FetchClient.ts:182). Running the built SDK, a 2000-char post body reached the fetcher as an ArrayBuffer. (2) fetchJson passes `body` through as-is, methods.ts:16,25,34 JSON.stringify `data`, and FetchClient.ts:178-180 stringifies `data`. (3) FetchClient.ts:76 uses `new URL(path, base)`; `node -p` resolves '/item' against 'https://api.example.com/v1' to https://api.example.com/item, and 'item' against '.../v1/' to .../v1/item. This differs from Axios joining, which matters because FetchJsonClient.ts:6 bills itself as an axiosJson drop-in. (4) FetchClient.ts:152 merges with `{ ...this.defaults, ...config }`, and FetchClient.spec.ts:193-199 shows per-request params replacing instance params. One nit: the fetchCompress.ts:41 doc comment says 'when compressMinLength is set' and :16 says 'byte count', but the code compares string length and compresses by default. The skill should describe the code.
verify.skill: confirmed: All four sub-claims check out against source. (1) fetchCompress.ts:49 sets the compressMinLength default to 1024 and gzips by default with Content-Encoding (lines 55-63). The FetchJsonClient.ts:10 doc comment agrees. (2) methods.ts:13-37 and FetchClient.ts:178-180 JSON.stringify `data`, while fetchJson passes `body` through. (3) FetchClient.ts:76 uses `new URL(path, base)`; `node -p "new URL('/item','https://api.example.com/v1').href"` printed https://api.example.com/item. That differs from Axios, and FetchJsonClient is billed as an axiosJson drop-in (FetchJsonClient.ts:6). (4) FetchClient.ts:97,152 does `{...this.defaults, ...config}`, and FetchClient.spec.ts:193-199 shows request params replacing the instance params. None of this appears anywhere in the skill. fetch.md:7 only names fetchCompress, and the skill's baseURL example has no path, so it does not show the pitfall. The default gzip and the baseURL behavior are real interoperability gotchas, so medium is proportionate.

findings.title: Undici guidance drops the README's 'compatible Undici release' qualifier for the global-dispatcher path
findings.current: fetch.md:49: 'If you need caching in Node, the **consumer** installs Undici and supplies a fetcher or global dispatcher.'
findings.truth: The SDK README says the Node app should install 'a compatible Undici release'. For `setGlobalDispatcher` to drive Node's built-in globalThis.fetch, the installed major should match Node's bundled undici. The SDK requires Node >= 26, which bundles undici 8.x. The API used in the snippets (Agent().compose, interceptors.cache, cacheStores.MemoryCacheStore {maxSize,maxCount,maxEntrySize}, type 'shared'|'private') is valid in both undici 7.29.1 and 8.10.2, so the snippets themselves are correct.
findings.evidence: sdk-js packages/sdk/README.md:33-36; packages/sdk/package.json engines `{ node: '>=26' }`; `node -p process.versions.undici` on Node v26.9.0 -> 8.10.2; `npm view undici dist-tags` latest 8.11.2, seven 7.30.0. The types in node_modules/.pnpm/undici@{7.29.1,8.10.2}/node_modules/undici/types/cache-interceptor.d.ts:13,40,118-162 and interceptors.d.ts:80 match the skill's usage.
findings.recommendation: Restore the README qualifier at fetch.md:49: the consumer installs 'a compatible Undici release', meaning one whose Dispatcher API matches the undici bundled in the running Node (check `process.versions.undici`; undici 7.29+ and 8.x both share the global dispatcher registration Node 26 reads). Do not mandate an exact major. Under 'Process-wide default', add README.md:111-113: install the global dispatcher once at bootstrap, before normal requests, and include any required proxy, TLS, retry or tracing behavior in that dispatcher, because it replaces the previous one.

verify.code: adjusted: The skill does drop the README's 'compatible Undici release' qualifier (README.md:33-36 vs fetch.md:49), and it omits README.md:111-113 (install once, before normal requests; include proxy/TLS/retry/tracing). The finding's key 'truth' claim is wrong, though. It says the installed major must match Node's bundled undici, 'undici 8 for Node 26'. Both undici 7.29.1 and 8.10.2 lib/global.js setGlobalDispatcher write Symbol.for('undici.globalDispatcher.2') (v7 lines 5,19-31; v8 lines 5,24-48), and Node 26's bundled undici 8 reads that symbol. I tested on Node v26.9.0: setGlobalDispatcher with a cache-intercepted Agent from undici 7.29.1 drove the built-in globalThis.fetch, giving 2 fetches and 1 server hit, exactly like 8.10.2. So undici 7 works on Node 26. The snippets need the cache-interceptor API (interceptors.cache, cacheStores), which is present in both 7.29.1 and 8.10.2. Low severity polish only.
verify.skill: adjusted: fetch.md:49 does drop the README's 'compatible Undici release' qualifier (README.md:33-36), and it omits README.md:111-113: install the dispatcher once, before normal requests, and include any proxy, TLS, retry or tracing behavior in it. The finding's stronger claim is not supported. It says the installed major must match Node's bundled undici and recommends 'undici 8 for Node 26'. In sdk-js node_modules, lib/global.js:5 in both undici@7.29.1 and undici@8.10.2 registers `Symbol.for('undici.globalDispatcher.2')`. Node v26.9.0 bundles undici 8.10.2 (process.versions.undici), whose global.js:57-58 reads that same symbol. So a recent undici 7.x setGlobalDispatcher also drives Node 26's built-in fetch. The real issue is compatibility of the Dispatcher API version, not an exact major match.

findings.title: zod is not really optional: the root barrel and the /hex, /object and /zod subpaths load zod at runtime
findings.current: overview.md:40 "`zod` | **Optional peer** — install only if you use zod helpers (`@ariestools/sdk/zod`, hex zod helpers, etc.)"; overview.md:44-45 "# Only if you use zod helpers from the SDK / pnpm add zod"; overview.md:22-25 shows the root-barrel import `import { assertEx, delay, exists, fetchJson } from '@ariestools/sdk'` as the default with no zod caveat.
findings.truth: zod is declared as an optional peer (`^4.6`), but the root barrel (node, browser and neutral builds), `@ariestools/sdk/hex`, `@ariestools/sdk/object` and `@ariestools/sdk/zod` all import `zod/mini` or `zod/v4/core` at the top level. Without zod, `import ... from '@ariestools/sdk'` fails with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND, even for assertEx or fetchJson. Zod-free subpaths such as /assert, /delay, /exists and /fetch load fine. The version must be zod v4 (`^4.6`), because the code uses the `zod/mini` and `zod/v4/core` entry points. Downstream, `@ariestools/pixel` imports `@ariestools/sdk/object` at runtime but does not declare zod. `@ariestools/express` declares `zod ^4.6` as a required (non-optional) peer. The upstream umbrella README:234 makes the same wrong 'optional' claim.
findings.evidence: sdk-js/packages/sdk/package.json:403-411 (peerDependencies zod ^4.6, peerDependenciesMeta zod optional); package.json:401 devDep zod ~4.6.5. Runtime imports: packages/sdk/src/modules/hex/hex/hex.ts:1 `import * as z from 'zod/mini'` (used by `export const HexZod = z.pipe(...)` at :11), hex/address/address.ts:1, hex/hash/hash.ts:1, hex/zod.ts:1, hex/ethAddress.ts:1, object/JsonObject.ts:1, zod/zodAsFactory.ts:1 (`zod/v4/core`). Root barrel src/index.ts:21,23,36 re-exports #hex, #object, #zod. Built output (dist built 2026-09-24 = published 9.0.1): `grep -n '^import' dist/neutral/index.mjs` shows `import * as z from "zod/mini"` at :988 and `zod/v4/core` at :3266, and the same holds for dist/node/index.mjs and dist/browser/index.mjs. Simulation with a resolve hook that makes 'zod*' unresolvable (node 26.9.0): FAIL dist/node/index.mjs, dist/browser/index.mjs, dist/neutral/index.mjs, hex.mjs, object.mjs and zod.mjs (ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND 'zod/mini'); OK for assert.mjs, fetch.mjs, delay.mjs and exists.mjs. pixel/src/XyUserEventHandler.ts:1 `import { type EmptyObject, toSafeJsonObject } from '@ariestools/sdk/object'` → pixel/dist/browser/index.mjs:514; pixel/package.json has no zod. express/package.json peers {winston-transport ^4.9, zod ^4.6}, with no peerDependenciesMeta.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite overview.md:40 as: "`zod` (^4.6, v4 only) — declared optional, but **required at runtime** for the root barrel `@ariestools/sdk` and the `/hex`, `/object` and `/zod` subpaths (and transitively for `@ariestools/pixel`; `@ariestools/express` lists it as a required peer). Skip it only if you import zod-free subpaths exclusively (e.g. `/assert`, `/delay`, `/exists`, `/fetch`)." Change the default install at overview.md:18-20 and 43-45 to `pnpm add @ariestools/sdk zod@^4.6`. Under the root-barrel example (overview.md:22-29), note that the root barrel loads both `zod` and `@opentelemetry/api`. In the same change, fix conventions.md:58 to: "Install `zod` whenever you use the root barrel or /hex, /object, /zod. `@opentelemetry/api` is a required peer." Fix modules.md:41, :43 and :56 to say /hex, /object and /zod need zod at runtime, not 'optional zod'. Optionally file an sdk-js issue for packages/sdk/README.md:234 and pixel's undeclared zod.

findings.title: zod is a hard runtime import of /hex, /object and the root barrel, not an optional extra

findings.truth: Core hex code imports `zod/mini` at module load, so zod is needed for any hex import, not only the zod helpers. The `object` module does the same through JsonObject. The root barrel re-exports both. Without `zod` installed, `@ariestools/sdk/hex`, `@ariestools/sdk/object`, `@ariestools/sdk/zod` and `@ariestools/sdk` all fail to load. Because zod is declared as an optional peer, pnpm does not install it automatically. The imports are `zod/mini` and `zod/v4/core`, so zod 4 (^4.6) is required. The root barrel also loads `@ariestools/telemetry`, which needs the required peer `@opentelemetry/api`.

findings.title: The retry example hides that retry ignores thrown errors and does not retry by default
findings.current: modules.md:72-80 ("Delay and retry"): `await retry(async () => doWork(), { /* options per package API */ })`. The table row at modules.md:47 says only "Retry helpers".
findings.truth: `retry(func, config?)` has no try/catch, so a thrown error propagates on the first attempt and is never retried. It retries only while `complete(result)` is false; the default check is `result !== undefined`. Defaults are `retries = 0` (no retries), `interval = 100` ms and `backoff = 2`. When everything is exhausted it returns `undefined` rather than throwing. As written, the `doWork()` example (void result) is never "complete": with `retries: N` it runs N+1 times even on success and returns undefined.
findings.evidence: sdk-js/packages/sdk/src/modules/retry/retry.ts:5-18 (RetryConfig: backoff, interval, retries; RetryConfigWithComplete: complete), :26-41 (`const result = await func()` with no try/catch at :30; defaults at :28; `return undefined` when retries <= 0). src/spec/retry/retry.spec.ts covers only undefined/complete cases, with no throw case.
findings.recommendation: Replace the placeholder with a concrete example: `const value = await retry(() => fetchMaybe(), { retries: 3, interval: 100, backoff: 2, complete: v => v !== undefined })`. Add a note that retry re-runs on an incomplete/undefined result, not on exceptions, so the function should catch and return undefined to trigger a retry. Also note that the default is 0 retries and that exhaustion returns `undefined`.

verify.code: confirmed: retry.ts:26-41 calls `const result = await func()` without a try/catch, so a thrown error propagates on the first attempt. The defaults at :28 are complete = value !== undefined, retries = 0, interval = 100 and backoff = 2. Line :35 returns undefined once retries run out. A void `doWork()` therefore never counts as complete: it runs retries+1 times and returns undefined. The placeholder `{ /* options per package API */ }` at modules.md:79 hides all of this.

The default `timeout` is 30 000 ms, and on expiry it only calls `onCancel` and the timeout handler; the underlying work keeps running. `ForgetPromise.activeForgets` and `ForgetPromise.awaitInactive(interval, timeout)` let tests and shutdown paths drain pending forgets. Global defaults can be set via `globalThis.xy.forget.config`.
findings.evidence: sdk-js/packages/sdk/src/modules/forget/ForgetConfig.ts:5-24 (fields) and :27 (`defaultForgetConfig = { timeout: 30_000 }`); forget/forget.ts:6-10 ("Timeouts notify via `onCancel` but do not stop the underlying work"); forget/ForgetPromise.ts:26,33,45 (activeForgets, active, awaitInactive); forget/ForgetPromiseNode.ts:28-30 (globalThis.xy?.forget?.config merge).
findings.recommendation: Add `import { forget, ForgetPromise } from '@ariestools/sdk/forget'; forget(sendMetrics(), { name: 'metrics', onComplete: ([, error]) => { if (error) logger.warn(error) } })`. Note four points: (1) rejections are logged automatically and surface through `onComplete`'s `[result, error]` tuple, while `onException` fires only for errors thrown while the forget is set up; (2) `timeout` (default 30 s) only calls `onCancel` and does not cancel the work; (3) run `await ForgetPromise.awaitInactive()` before process exit and in test teardown; (4) defaults can be set globally via `globalThis.xy.forget.config`.

verify.code: adjusted: The gap is real: modules.md:82-84 is prose only. ForgetConfig.ts:5-19 has name, onCancel, onComplete, onException and timeout. defaultForgetConfig = { timeout: 30_000 } is at :22, not :27. ForgetPromise has activeForgets, active and awaitInactive(interval = 100, timeout?). The timeout only notifies (forget.ts:10; ForgetPromise.forget never aborts the promise). globalThis.xy.forget.config is merged in both ForgetPromise.forget and ForgetPromiseNode.forget. The recommended example is wrong, though. In ForgetPromise.forget, a rejected promise is caught inside promiseWrapper, logged with logger.error, and passed to onComplete([undefined, error]). onException fires only for synchronous exceptions in the setup try block. So `onException: e => logger.warn(e)` would never see sendMetrics() failures.

A timeout only notifies (ForgetPromise.ts:104-113). activeForgets and awaitInactive are at :26 and :45. The recommended example is wrong, though. findings.title: storage-adapters: the root barrel needs both optional peers (idb and mongodb), and the install line installs neither
findings.current: packages.md:36-41 table lists "`@ariestools/storage-adapters` | Root barrel" first, then `/indexed-db`, `/mongo`, and "`*/model` | Types-only subpaths". packages.md:43-45 `pnpm add @ariestools/storage-adapters`.
findings.truth: The root entry statically imports both `idb` and `mongodb`. Both are optional peers (`idb ^8.0`, `mongodb ^7.6`), and pnpm's auto-install-peers does not install optional peers. So `pnpm add @ariestools/storage-adapters` followed by importing the root (or `/indexed-db` or `/mongo`) fails with module-not-found until the matching backend is installed. The root barrel also pulls `mongodb` into browser graphs. The exported subpaths are exactly `.`, `./indexed-db`, `./indexed-db/model`, `./mongo`, `./mongo/model`; there is no root `./model`. Main exports: `IndexedDbKeyValueStore` (implements `KeyValueStore` from `@ariestools/sdk/storage`), `withDb`, `withStore`, `withReadOnlyStore`, `withReadWriteStore`, `BaseMongoSdk`, `MongoClientWrapper`, `BaseMongoSdkConfig`.
findings.evidence: sdk-js/packages/storage-adapters/dist/neutral/index.mjs:5 `import { openDB } from "idb"` and :271 `import { MongoClient } from "mongodb"`. sdk-js/packages/storage-adapters/src/index.ts re-exports both `#indexed-db` and `#mongo`. sdk-js/packages/storage-adapters/package.json:89-99 (peerDependencies idb/mongodb, both `optional: true`). `npm view @ariestools/storage-adapters@9.0.1 exports` lists no `./model`. Exports: src/modules/indexed-db/IndexedDbKeyValueStore.ts:12, withDb.ts:20, src/modules/mongo/Base.ts:23, Wrapper.ts:14, Config.ts:26.
findings.recommendation: Replace the root-barrel row with a warning: it imports both backends, so import a backend subpath instead. List the exact subpaths (`indexed-db`, `indexed-db/model`, `mongo`, `mongo/model`) instead of `*/model`. Change the install line to `pnpm add @ariestools/storage-adapters idb` (browser/IndexedDB) or `pnpm add @ariestools/storage-adapters mongodb` (Node/Mongo). Name the main classes and helpers listed above.

findings.title: express: the install guidance gets peers and deps backwards and leaves out the required zod peer and the Node-only export

findings.truth: `@ariestools/sdk` is a regular dependency, not a peer. The declared peers are `zod ^4.6` (required: `requestHandlerValidator` imports `zod/mini`) and `winston-transport ^4.9`. findings.title: testing: `/extended` is described wrongly, two type subpaths are missing, and the Vitest 5 coupling is not mentioned
findings.current: packages.md:63-67 table: "`@ariestools/testing` | Root", "`@ariestools/testing/matchers` | Custom matchers", "`@ariestools/testing/extended` | Extended utilities"; packages.md:73 "Wire matchers in Vitest setup files per the consuming repo."
findings.truth: `/extended` is a side-effect entry, not a set of utilities. It calls `expect.extend(matchers)` and augments Vitest 5's `Assertion<R, T>` / `AsymmetricMatchersContaining` types with `CustomMatchers`, which add jest-extended-style matchers such as `toBeArray`, `toBeArrayOfSize`, `toBeTrue`, `toContainKey`, `toInclude` and `toBeValidDate`. It is listed in `sideEffects`. The intended usage is `import '@ariestools/testing/extended'` in a spec or setup file. `/matchers` exports the raw `matchers` object. The root re-exports both, so importing it also registers the matchers. Two types-only subpaths are missing from the table: `./model` and `./matchers/model` (`ExpectationResult`). `vitest ~5.0.1` is a hard `dependency` (moved back from peer in commit 4448bc03b). Consumers on another Vitest major get a second Vitest copy, and `expect.extend` then targets the wrong `expect`.
findings.evidence: sdk-js/packages/testing/src/modules/extended/index.ts:5 `expect.extend(matchers)`, :12 `declare module 'vitest'`, interface CustomMatchers (toBeArray … toIncludeAllMembers). sdk-js/packages/testing/package.json:30-34 sideEffects, :41-64 exports (`.`, `./matchers`, `./matchers/model`, `./extended`, `./model`), :76-77 `"dependencies": { "vitest": "~5.0.1" }`. sdk-js/packages/testing/src/index.ts re-exports `#extended` and `#matchers`; dist/neutral/index.mjs:372 `expect.extend(matchers)`. In-repo usage: sdk-js/packages/express/src/spec/node/*.spec.ts:1 `import '@ariestools/testing/extended'`. `npm view @ariestools/testing@9.0.1 dependencies` → `{ vitest: '~5.0.1' }`.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the table. `/extended` is the side-effect import that registers the custom matchers and their Vitest types; add it to `setupFiles` or import it at the top of a spec. `/matchers` is the raw `matchers` object for a manual `expect.extend`. Add the `./model` and `./matchers/model` type subpaths. Note that the root import also registers the matchers. State that 9.x requires Vitest 5 (matching `@ariestools/vitest-config`'s `vitest ^5.0` peer).

findings.title: crypto-auth: main API (SeedPhraseVault, injected store and crypto, PBKDF2 versioning) is not documented
findings.current: packages.md:85 "Self-contained password and seed-phrase encryption/decryption (vault-style crypto)."
findings.truth: API: `SeedPhraseVault(store: SeedPhraseStore, walletKind?, crypto: VaultCrypto = defaultVaultCrypto)`, `SeedPhraseDecryptError`, `PasswordKey`, `Pbkdf2AesGcmVaultCrypto`, `deriveKeyFromPassword`, `deriveKeyAndValues`, `verifyPassword`, `needsRehash`, `encryptSeedPhrase`/`decryptSeedPhrase`, and `bytesToBase64`/`base64ToBytes`. Default PBKDF2 is 600,000 iterations (legacy 100,000). Records are self-describing and upgrade their KDF safely. Storage is injected by the app.
findings.evidence: sdk-js/packages/crypto-auth/src/SeedPhraseVault.ts:17,31,38-42; src/password.ts:16,28,38,53,67; src/models/KeyMetadata.ts:12 `LEGACY_PBKDF2_ITERATIONS = 100_000`, :20 `DEFAULT_PBKDF2_ITERATIONS = 600_000`; src/Pbkdf2AesGcmVaultCrypto.ts:22,76; src/models/SeedPhraseStore.ts:8.
findings.recommendation: Add 2–3 lines under the crypto-auth section of packages.md. The app injects a `SeedPhraseStore` into `SeedPhraseVault` and can pass a custom `VaultCrypto` (default is `Pbkdf2AesGcmVaultCrypto`). To create a vault use `deriveKeyAndValues`; to open one use `deriveKeyFromValues`, which reads the salt and iterations from the stored record. Never use `deriveKeyFromPassword` with its default to open an existing vault. New keys use 600k PBKDF2 iterations; records with no stored count are read at the legacy 100k. After a successful unlock, upgrade old records with `needsRehash` / `SeedPhraseVault.recordNeedsRehash`.

findings.title: Router ignores the toolchain's own docs contract (xy plan lint / repo-docs.md) and sends agents to guidance that breaks it
findings.current: SKILL.md:14 "Read the repository's own `AGENTS.md` first... never overrides what a specific repository says"; SKILL.md:24 routes to structure.md for "the `papers/` vs `specs/` vs `docs/` split, lifecycle subfolders"; SKILL.md:28 routes to agents-md.md for "`@AGENTS.md` imports ... and nested package files".
