findings.truth: Since 10.0.0 (published 2026-09-05; the skill was written 2026-09-01) the toolchain ships `xy plan lint` (experimental, `xyex plan lint` preferred, not part of `xy check`). It enforces a fixed layout. Required root files are AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, CHANGELOG.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and README.md, and each must be a regular file, not a symlink. `papers/` may hold only README.md, WHITE-PAPER.md, YELLOW-PAPER.md and an optional GREEN-PAPER.md; any other file is an error, and `--fix` moves it into `notes/`. `docs/README.md`, `docs/ROADMAP.md` and `notes/README.md` are required. CLAUDE.md must `@AGENTS.md`, and AGENTS.md must not use `@path` imports. docs/repo-docs.md also says "Do not add `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` inside packages." The reference repo (toolchain) follows this layout: papers/{README,WHITE-PAPER,YELLOW-PAPER}.md, a flat docs/ with ROADMAP.md, notes/README.md, and a regular-file CLAUDE.md that imports AGENTS.md.
findings.evidence: toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/plan/lint.ts:19-38 (REQUIRED_ROOT_PATHS, REQUIRED_PAPER_PATHS, OPTIONAL_PAPER_PATHS=['papers/GREEN-PAPER.md'], REQUIRED_DOC_PATHS, REQUIRED_NOTES_PATHS, ALLOWED_PAPER_PATHS) and :151-154 ("must be a regular, non-symlink file"); rootDocs.ts:38,44,106-119; toolchain/docs/repo-docs.md:16, :22, :37-44 ("`xy plan lint` remains experimental and is **not** part of `xy check`"); `node packages/toolchain/dist/bin/xy.mjs plan lint --rules` (10.1.0) lists plan.papers.unexpected-files (error, fix: "flatten other regular files into notes/"), plan.root.claude-imports-agents, plan.root.agents-no-at-imports, plan.root.docs-index, plan.docs.required-files, plan.notes.required-files; stability.ts:60-62 plan/plan init/plan lint = experimental; CHANGELOG.md:15-19,30-32; first tag that contains the plan commit 622d1ccb2 is v10.0.0; `ls toolchain/papers toolchain/docs toolchain/notes`.
findings.recommendation: Add a short "Toolchain-enforced contract" paragraph to the router, after line 14. It should say that in a repository that runs `xyex plan lint` / `xy repo lint`, those rules win over this skill, and list them: regular-file CLAUDE.md with `@AGENTS.md`; no `@` imports in AGENTS.md; root CHANGELOG.md and CONTRIBUTING.md; `papers/{README,WHITE-PAPER,YELLOW-PAPER[,GREEN-PAPER]}.md` only; `docs/README.md` and `docs/ROADMAP.md`; `notes/README.md`; no AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md inside packages. findings.title: Front-matter templates use a single `state` / `reviewed` vocabulary that does not map onto the toolchain's published document-metadata model
findings.current: Decision template: templates.md:98-105 (`state: normative`, with acceptance only in prose `status: "accepted YYYY-MM-DD"`). Evidence template: templates.md:131-138 (`state: active`). Runbook template: templates.md:162-169 (`reviewed:`). Vocabulary from lifecycle.md:11 (draft|active|normative|superseded|retired).
findings.truth: The toolchain's plan-manifest schema, shipped in @ariestools/toolchain 10.1.0, defines document metadata on two separate axes. The first is `lifecycle` (accepted, active, archived, deprecated, draft, proposed, superseded). The second is `authorityLevel` (descriptive, evidentiary, informative, normative). It also has `lastReviewed` and `supersededBy`. A repo may hand ownership of exactly these fields to front matter (`metadata.source: front-matter`). The skill's single `state` field merges the two axes: a decision cannot be both `accepted` and `normative`, and evidence cannot be marked `evidentiary`. The field names (`reviewed` vs `lastReviewed`) also differ. So the templates' front matter cannot serve as that owner without translation. There is also an internal inconsistency: lifecycle.md:33 says `normative` lives in `papers/`, `specs/`, yet the decision template and index example (templates.md:221) mark `docs/decisions/` normative.
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/toolchain/schemas/plan-manifest.v1.schema.json:334-390 (documentMetadata: lifecycle, authorityLevel, lastReviewed, supersededBy). toolchain docs/plan-manifest.md:29-34 ("Document lifecycle metadata has exactly one owner... may set `metadata.source` to `front-matter`"), 315. skills/xy-agent/lifecycle.md:7-35.
findings.recommendation: Coordinate with lifecycle.md and settle the front-matter contract in one place. Either adopt the schema's two axes (for example, a decision gets `lifecycle: accepted` + `authority: normative`, evidence gets `lifecycle: active` + `authority: evidentiary`, and `lastReviewed` replaces or aliases `reviewed`), or document an explicit mapping table from `state` to (`lifecycle`, `authorityLevel`). Then update the three templates and the index example columns to match. At minimum, fix the decision template so `accepted` is a machine field, not prose only.

findings.title: Evidence 'Tier' ladder vocabulary differs from the toolchain's assurance facets for evidence
findings.current: templates.md:144-145 "**Tier.** This is <local | local-chain | testnet | hosted> evidence. It does not establish <the tiers it explicitly does not>."
findings.truth: The toolchain's published evidence model, used when a plan-manifest gate cites a `kind: document` evidence file, records orthogonal facets rather than a single tier. The facets are artifact (source/built/packed/published/deployed), execution, environment (local/ci/preview/hosted/production), network (none/simulated/devnet/testnet/mainnet), access, and validation. The docs state explicitly that "The facets are not a maturity ladder". `local-chain` is not a value. `testnet` is a network value and `hosted` is an environment value, so they are different axes.
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/toolchain/schemas/plan-manifest.v1.schema.json:806-850 (assuranceScope). toolchain docs/plan-manifest.md:260-279.

It does not establish <facets/values not covered>." Optionally add `observedOn` as a front-matter alias so evidence documents transcribe directly into gate evidence.

findings.title: Front-matter state vocabulary and field names do not match the toolchain's Plan Manifest v1 document-metadata contract
findings.current: lifecycle.md:11 `state: normative  # draft|active|normative|superseded|retired`; state table :29-35 (normative lives in `papers/`, `specs/`); :14 `reviewed:` "required for kind: runbook" only; :17 `supersededBy: docs/plans/NEW.md`.
findings.truth: The toolchain ships plan-manifest.v1.schema.json. Its documentMetadata keeps two axes separate: `lifecycle` (accepted|active|archived|deprecated|draft|proposed|superseded) and `authorityLevel` (descriptive|evidentiary|informative|normative). It requires `lastReviewed` on every reviewed document, and `supersededBy` is a manifest document id. docs/plan-manifest.md:29-34 lets a repo with a shared front-matter contract set `metadata.source: front-matter`; front matter then owns lifecycle, authority level, review date, and supersession. The skill's single `state` field mixes lifecycle with authority (`normative`), which goes against its own advice at :37-39 to keep those axes apart. It has `retired`, which has no manifest equivalent (the manifest uses archived/deprecated). It has no accepted/proposed, although decision records are "immutable once accepted" (:45). It requires `reviewed` only for runbooks. Within the skill, decisions are `state: normative` and live in docs/decisions/ (templates.md:100-101, 222), but the table says normative documents live only in papers/ and specs/.
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/toolchain/schemas/plan-manifest.v1.schema.json:334-420 (documentMetadata oneOf: source manifest with lifecycle enum :343-353, authorityLevel enum :355-362, lastReviewed :364-367, supersededBy localId :368-370; source const front-matter :413-420); docs/plan-manifest.md:29-34; schema :436 planRole is "distinct from a generic file kind in front matter" (so `kind:` itself is compatible); skills/xy-agent/templates.md:100-101.
findings.recommendation: Align the schema with Plan Manifest v1 so that `metadata.source: front-matter` works. Preferred: split `state` into `lifecycle:` (the manifest enum) and `authority:` (descriptive|evidentiary|informative|normative), use or alias `lastReviewed` for `reviewed`, and recommend it on every kind (required for runbooks). If renaming is too disruptive, add an explicit mapping table instead: draft→draft; active→active; normative→accepted + authority normative; superseded→superseded (supersededBy path→manifest id); retired→archived or deprecated. Add `docs/decisions/` to the 'Where it lives' column for normative.

findings.title: The claim that front-matter workItems is the 'only structured connection' to xy work is inaccurate
findings.current: lifecycle.md:114 "Nothing in `xy work` links back — `WorkAnchor` supports only `kind: 'file'`, and there is no document or URL anchor kind — so this front-matter field is the only structured connection between the two"
findings.truth: WorkAnchor does support only kind 'file', with no document or URL kind; that part is correct. But a file anchor accepts any repo-relative path, including a document, through `xy work add --file docs/plans/X.md [--line N]`, so work items can point at documents. Separately, the shipped Plan Manifest v1 links documents and roadmap phases to work items in a structured way. Roadmap phases carry `workItems: [{id, relation: blocks|implements|tracks|verifies}]`, and a `planned` paper slot must list at least one work id. Work id prefixes are configurable (default XYW), and imported issues may use GH-*. `xy work` is experimental (`xyex work` is preferred).
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/toolchain/src/actions/work/schema.ts:17-21 (WorkAnchor), :181 (kind must be file), :81 (idPrefix 'XYW'); helpers.ts:16-23 normalizeAnchor; store.ts:134-147 pathInsideRepo (any in-repo path); `xy.mjs work add --help` shows "--file  Repo-relative file anchor", "--line", and "(experimental — prefer xyex)"; plan-manifest.v1.schema.json:158-186 (workItemId, workReference relations), :620-645 (plannedPaper.workItems minItems 1); docs/plan-manifest.md:129, 232-246, 283.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the paragraph. xy work items can anchor to a document path with `--file` (file anchors only; no document-aware or URL anchor kind). `workItems:` in front matter is the document-side link. In repos with a reviewed `.xy/plan.json`, phase-to-work and planned-paper-to-work links belong in the manifest (relation blocks/implements/tracks/verifies) and must not be duplicated in front matter. Note that the id prefix is configurable (XYW by default, GH-* for imported issues).

findings.title: Missing: .xy/plan.json as a third authority index, and its single-owner rule for lifecycle metadata
findings.current: absent. lifecycle.md:110 describes only two indexes: "`AGENTS.md` keeps the compact authority table ... `docs/README.md` is the exhaustive inventory."
findings.truth: Toolchain 10.x ships the experimental `xy plan init`, which creates `.xy/plan.json`. This is a machine-readable index of which Markdown governs which subjects (planRole, describes current/target/mixed/historical, authorityFor, standing, scope) plus the roadmap phase graph. The manifest and front matter must not both hold lifecycle metadata: "Use inline manifest metadata until front matter is adopted; never maintain both." The manifest's `describes` and evidence `assurance` facets are the toolchain's structured form of the skill's 'authority vs evidence' and 'name the tier' rules.
findings.evidence: toolchain docs/plan-manifest.md:1-7, 17-34, 50-72, 260-279; plan-manifest.v1.schema.json:335 ("never maintain both"); `xy.mjs --stability --json` reports plan init as experimental; CHANGELOG.md:14-15; git tag --contains for plan/lint.ts lists v10.0.9 and v10.1.0 (released, not main-only).
findings.recommendation: Add a short 'Plan manifest' subsection near 'The generated index'. Where `.xy/plan.json` exists, it routes agents to governing documents; AGENTS.md keeps the compact authority table and docs/README.md the inventory. Exactly one of `.xy/plan.json` or front matter owns lifecycle, authority, review date, and supersession: set `metadata.source: front-matter` once this front matter is adopted, and never fill in both. Point to the xy-toolchain skill and plan-manifest docs for `xyex plan init` and `xyex plan lint`.

findings.title: Lifecycle rules ignore the docs/ROADMAP.md and notes/ files that xy plan lint requires, and its scaffolds lack front matter
findings.current: lifecycle.md:3 "Every document under `docs/`, `papers/`, and `specs/` carries YAML front matter." The file never mentions docs/ROADMAP.md or notes/.
findings.truth: `xy plan lint` (experimental, shipped in 10.x) requires docs/README.md, docs/ROADMAP.md, notes/README.md, and papers/{README,WHITE-PAPER,YELLOW-PAPER}.md, and its --fix creates them from built-in templates that have no YAML front matter (papers get a '## Status / Draft.' section instead). notes/ is defined as freeform, non-governing material "unless the plan manifest explicitly references it", and --fix moves unexpected papers/ files there. lifecycle.md says nothing about where the required living docs/ROADMAP.md fits (kind, state, whether it can ever be superseded or archived, given lint requires it to exist) or whether notes/ needs front matter. The toolchain's own reference docs/ and papers/ carry no front matter.
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/toolchain/src/actions/plan/lint.ts:27-37 (required paths); templates.ts:54-147 (templates without front matter; notes/README.md text at :82-87); docs/plan-manifest.md:85-94, 109-113; `xy.mjs plan lint --rules` (8 error rules incl. plan.docs.required-files, plan.notes.required-files); head -1 of toolchain docs/*.md and papers/*.md shows plain H1s, no '---'.
findings.recommendation: Add to the lifecycle rules: (1) docs/ROADMAP.md is the canonical living plan (kind: plan, state: active). It is revised in place and never superseded or archived, because plan lint requires it; finished phase plans under docs/plans/ are what get archived. (2) notes/ is non-governing and exempt from front matter unless the manifest or AGENTS.md cites a file there. (3) After `xyex plan lint --fix`, an adopting repo must add front matter to the scaffolded docs/README.md, ROADMAP.md, and papers.

findings.title: Evidence rules do not cover machine-readable (JSON) and dated-directory evidence, the dominant form in real repos
findings.current: lifecycle.md:60 "Name it `docs/evidence/YYYY-MM-DD-slug.md`"; :65 "`commit:` in front matter, and the exact command in the body".
findings.truth: Workspace repos mostly record evidence as JSON reports, which cannot carry YAML front matter. Some use dated directories that contain only JSON; others pair *_EVIDENCE.md with *_REPORT.json. lifecycle.md gives an agent no rule for where commit and command metadata go for JSON artifacts, or how immutability and front matter apply to a directory bundle.
findings.evidence: ls XYOracleNetwork/xyo-chain/docs/evidence/2026-10-01-mainnet-durability/ → 10 *.json, no .md; XYOracleNetwork/chain-event-service/docs/evidence/2026-10-08-current-graph/ → CES-CURRENT-GRAPH-PUBLIC.json, runtime-qualification-public.json; ariestools/actor-kit/docs/evidence/*.json; XYOracleNetwork/dapp-kit/docs/evidence/*.json; XYOracleNetwork/crypto-cards/docs/*_EVIDENCE.md + *_REPORT.json pairs (e.g. ACTOR_PROVIDER_ENGINE_CATALOG_2026_09_18_EVIDENCE.md / _REPORT.json).
findings.recommendation: Add an 'Evidence bundles' rule. A dated directory `docs/evidence/YYYY-MM-DD-slug/` is acceptable. It must contain a README.md (or a sibling .md) that carries the front matter (commit, command, tier) and links each JSON artifact. JSON reports should embed the commit and command too. The immutability rule covers every file in the bundle.

findings.title: zod is described as optional, but importing the root barrel or the hex/object/zod subpaths fails without it
findings.current: overview.md:40 "`zod` | **Optional peer** — install only if you use zod helpers (`@ariestools/sdk/zod`, hex zod helpers, etc.)"; overview.md:25 shows the root-barrel import `import { assertEx, delay, exists, fetchJson } from '@ariestools/sdk'` without that caveat; overview.md:43-45 "# Only if you use zod helpers from the SDK / pnpm add zod".
findings.truth: package.json does mark zod as an optional peer. However, the published 9.0.1 dist imports it with static top-level ESM imports in the root barrel (`dist/{neutral,node,browser}/index.mjs`) and in `dist/neutral/hex.mjs`, `object.mjs` and `zod.mjs`. Importing `@ariestools/sdk`, `/hex`, `/object` or `/zod` without zod installed therefore throws ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND, even if the code never calls a zod helper. Subpaths such as `/assert`, `/fetch` and `/telemetry` load without zod. The sdk README repeats the same wrong claim (sdk-js packages/sdk/README.md:234).
findings.evidence: sdk-js/packages/sdk/package.json:404-410 (zod peer optional). `grep -nE '^import .*zod' dist/neutral/hex.mjs` -> line 2 `import * as z from "zod/mini"`; dist/neutral/index.mjs:988,1010,... `import * as z from "zod/mini"`; dist/neutral/object.mjs:186,189; dist/neutral/zod.mjs:2. The installed 9.0.1 copy (sdk-react/node_modules/@ariestools/sdk) also has 9 zod/mini imports in index.mjs and 8 in hex.mjs. Runtime check in a scratch dir with sdk 9.0.1 + async-mutex + @ariestools/telemetry + @opentelemetry/api but no zod, run with `node --preserve-symlinks --input-type=module -e "await import(spec)"`: `@ariestools/sdk` -> "ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: Cannot find package 'zod' imported from .../@ariestools/sdk/dist/node/index.mjs"; `/hex`, `/object`, `/zod` -> ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND; `/assert`, `/fetch`, `/telemetry` -> ok. Source: src/modules/hex/zod.ts:1 and hex/address/*, hex/hash/*, object/JsonObject.ts import zod.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the zod row as: "`zod` — declared an optional peer, but in practice required whenever you import the root barrel `@ariestools/sdk`, or `@ariestools/sdk/hex`, `/object` or `/zod`. Only consumers who use zod-free subpaths exclusively (for example `/assert`, `/delay`, `/fetch`, `/promise`) can omit it." Change the install snippet comment to match, and add a note under the root-barrel example at line 25 that the root import requires zod.

findings.title: Module rows for hex, object and zod misstate the zod requirement
findings.current: modules.md:41 "`hex` ... Hex strings, hashes, address helpers, optional zod"; modules.md:43 "`object` ... Object helpers (prefer non-deprecated exports)" (no zod note); modules.md:56 "`zod` ... Zod helpers — requires optional peer `zod`".
findings.truth: The `/hex` subpath statically imports `zod/mini` in eight places, so zod is not optional for hex. `/object` imports `zod/mini` and `zod/v4/core`. Both fail to load without zod. The `/object` subpath and the root barrel publish only `#object/index-un-deprecated`, so the deprecated `isType` is not reachable through `/object` at all; it lives in `/typeof`.

findings.title: fetchJson example treats the return value as the DTO, but it is a FetchJsonResponse wrapper
findings.current: fetch.md:22 "const data = await fetchJson<MyDto>('https://api.example.com/item')"
findings.truth: `fetchJson<T>` returns `Promise<FetchJsonResponse<T>>`, an object `{ data: T | null, headers, response, status, statusText }`, not `T`. `data` can be null, including for non-2xx responses with malformed JSON.
findings.evidence: sdk-js/packages/sdk/src/modules/fetch/fetchJson.ts:31 `export async function fetchJson<T>(url: string, options: FetchJsonOptions = {}): Promise<FetchJsonResponse<T>>`; src/modules/fetch/types.ts:10-21 (FetchJsonResponse fields; `data: T | null`). README.md (packages/sdk) lines ~172-175: "Non-2xx malformed JSON still produces `data: null`".
findings.recommendation: Change the example to `const { data, status } = await fetchJson<MyDto>(url)` and add a line explaining that `data` is `MyDto | null`, so callers must check `status` and null before use. Also say that `fetchJson` does not throw on non-2xx responses, while `FetchClient`/`FetchJsonClient` throw `FetchClientError` (a FetchError of type 'http-status') unless `validateStatus` allows the status.

The skill text is unchanged since 2026-07-31 (`git log -- skills/ariestools-sdk/fetch.md` -> only 8a7d4f0).

An oversized body raises `FetchError.type === 'response-too-large'`. These were added in b86f3a024 (2026-08-27, bounded cancellable reads) and changed in 158476cd7 (2026-09-18, non-stream bodies fall back to response.text()).

findings.title: retry example hides that retry defaults to 0 retries and does not retry on thrown errors
findings.current: modules.md:79 "await retry(async () => doWork(), { /* options per package API */ })"
findings.truth: `retry(func, config?)` retries only when `complete(result)` is false; by default that means the result is `undefined`. The defaults are `retries = 0` (no retries), `interval = 100` and `backoff = 2`. There is no try/catch, so a thrown error propagates immediately with no retry. When retries run out it resolves `undefined` instead of throwing.
findings.evidence: sdk-js/packages/sdk/src/modules/retry/retry.ts:5-12 (RetryConfig with defaults documented: backoff 2, interval 100, retries 0), :15-18 (`complete`), :26-41 (implementation: `const result = await func()` with no catch; returns undefined when retries <= 0).
findings.recommendation: Replace the example with `const value = await retry(() => tryFetchOrUndefined(), { retries: 3, interval: 100, backoff: 2 })`. Add a note: retries happen on `undefined` (or on a custom `complete` returning false), not on exceptions, so wrap a throwing call to return `undefined`. The result is `T | undefined` once retries run out, and the default is 0 retries.

findings.title: Import style should say the root barrel loads every peer; subpaths are what keep peers optional
findings.current: conventions.md:5-6 "Prefer **named exports** from `@ariestools/sdk/<module>` or the root barrel." / "Prefer **subpath imports** for clarity and smaller mental graphs … when only a few symbols are needed." and :17 "Bundlers can drop unused modules when you import subpaths or when the root barrel is tree-shakeable."
findings.truth: The root barrel is one pre-bundled file per platform that statically imports zod/mini, zod/v4/core, @ariestools/telemetry (and through it @opentelemetry/api) and async-mutex. In Node, without a bundler, tree-shaking does not apply, so every one of those must resolve no matter which symbol you import. Subpaths keep the runtime graph small: only /hex, /object and /zod need zod; only /telemetry and /telemetry-exporter need OTel; /creatable needs async-mutex; the rest import no external packages. Libraries should prefer subpaths for a functional reason, not just readability.
findings.evidence: Bare-import scan of sdk-js/packages/sdk/dist/*: node/index.mjs and browser/index.mjs import "@ariestools/telemetry" "async-mutex" "zod/mini" "zod/v4/core"; neutral/creatable.mjs "async-mutex"; neutral/hex.mjs "zod/mini"; neutral/object.mjs "zod/mini" "zod/v4/core"; neutral/zod.mjs "zod/v4/core"; neutral/telemetry*.mjs "@ariestools/telemetry"; no other neutral entry imports a bare package. packages/sdk/src/index.ts re-exports #telemetry, #telemetry-exporter and #zod.
findings.recommendation: Add to Import style: "In libraries, import from subpaths. The root barrel `@ariestools/sdk` statically loads zod, @ariestools/telemetry/@opentelemetry/api and async-mutex. Only `/hex`, `/object` and `/zod` need zod, and only `/telemetry*` needs OTel." Reword line 17 so it no longer suggests that tree-shaking makes root imports cheap at Node runtime.

findings.title: Tree-shaking omits that each subpath bundle has its own copy of shared classes, so instanceof fails across entries
findings.current: conventions.md:17 "Subpath exports map one-to-one with modules. Bundlers can drop unused modules when you import subpaths…"
findings.truth: @ariestools/sdk builds with the monolith default `moduleLinkage: 'bundle'`, which copies every referenced module into each entry. Shared code is duplicated, and object identity does not hold between subpaths or between a subpath and the root. For example, FetchError is defined separately in dist/neutral/api.mjs, fetch.mjs and the root index.mjs, and Base in base/creatable/events and the root. `err instanceof FetchError` therefore fails when the error comes from the copy in a different entry. The SDK ships `isFetchError` (a marker-based check) to cover this.
findings.evidence: sdk-js/packages/sdk/xy.config.ts sets no moduleLinkage. toolchain packages/toolchain/src/actions/package/compile/MonolithConfig.ts:155-166 ("`bundle` (default) … shared code is duplicated across entries so object identity does not hold between subpaths"; released since 78175963c 2026-07-06). dist: `var FetchError = class` at neutral/api.mjs:73, neutral/fetch.mjs:51, node/index.mjs:84. `var Base = class _Base` at neutral/base.mjs:20, creatable.mjs:34, events.mjs:20, node/index.mjs:1374. src/modules/fetch/FetchError.ts:35,149,202 (marker `'$$xylabs-fetch-error'` used by isFetchError).
findings.recommendation: Add: "Each subpath is self-contained, and shared classes are duplicated across entries. Do not use `instanceof` with SDK classes across different entry points. Use the provided guards (`isFetchError`, etc.), or import a given class from one entry point consistently, and do not mix root and subpath imports of the same class."

findings.title: Package-level AGENTS.md conflicts with toolchain policy and is not loaded "on demand" the way the skill claims
findings.current: agents-md.md:91: "Package-specific instructions → `packages/<pkg>/AGENTS.md`, which loads on demand." agents-md.md:130-136: "A package gets its own `AGENTS.md`... Codex composes root toward leaf. Claude Code loads a nested `CLAUDE.md` on demand..."
findings.truth: (1) The toolchain's documented contract (10.1.0) says: "Keep agent instructions at the repository root. Do not add `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` inside packages." (2) Claude Code reads AGENTS.md directly, including a subdirectory's AGENTS.md, only when no CLAUDE.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md or CLAUDE.local.md exists in the working directory or any directory above it. The root `@AGENTS.md` adapter that this same skill mandates suppresses that, and in this workspace CLAUDE.md always counts. So a lone `packages/<pkg>/AGENTS.md` never loads in Claude Code; only a nested CLAUDE.md that imports it does. (3) Codex builds its chain once at startup, from the Git root down to the current working directory. A package AGENTS.md is invisible to a Codex session started at the repo root.
findings.evidence: toolchain/docs/repo-docs.md:16 (also present at v10.1.0); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory, "When Claude Code reads AGENTS.md": the "Count, so Claude reads them instead of AGENTS.md" list and "As Claude works in subdirectories: a subdirectory's AGENTS.md... [only] when none count"; Codex docs (developers.openai.com/codex/guides/agents-md → learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/agents-md): "Starting at the project root... Codex walks down to your current working directory" and "builds an instruction chain when it starts"; CLAUDE.md exists above every repo.
findings.recommendation: Reconcile with toolchain/docs/repo-docs.md first: either drop the nested-file tier, or get the toolchain doc changed. If the tier stays, rewrite line 91 and the Nested files section as follows. A package delta needs both `packages/<pkg>/AGENTS.md` and a `packages/<pkg>/CLAUDE.md` containing `@AGENTS.md` (Claude loads that pair when it reads, writes or edits a file in the directory). findings.title: `.claude/rules/` overflow advice omits that rules are Claude-only and ignores the legacy toolchain rule files
findings.current: agents-md.md:90: "Path-scoped instructions → `.claude/rules/*.md` with `paths:` frontmatter. These load only when a matching file is touched." agents-md.md:136: "...in `.claude/rules/` with `paths:` frontmatter."
findings.truth: The path-scoping mechanics are accurate: rules load when Claude reads, writes or edits a matching file, and rules without `paths` load at launch. Three things are missing. (1) .claude/rules is read only by Claude Code. Content moved there out of the canonical AGENTS.md is invisible to Codex and Copilot, which defeats the skill's own "AGENTS.md is canonical" rule. Copilot's path-scoped equivalent is `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md` with `applyTo`. (2) Many workspace repos still carry generated `.claude/rules/xylabs-*.md` files with no `paths:` frontmatter, so they load every session. They are headed "Auto-managed by `pnpm xy claude-rules`. Do not edit manually.", that command no longer exists (toolchain 8.7+), and the workspace CLAUDE.md says to treat them as legacy read-only output. (3) The toolchain itself no longer touches .claude/rules at all.
findings.evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory, "Organize rules with .claude/rules/" and "Path-specific rules"; CLAUDE.md ("Older repos may still carry generated .claude/rules/xylabs-*.md files... treat them as legacy and do not hand-edit them"); AGENTS.md:246, 258; `ls` shows xylabs-*.md in ariestools/sdk-react/.claude/rules and 9 XYOracleNetwork repos; ariestools/sdk-react/.claude/rules/xylabs-style.md:3; `grep -rn claude/rules` over toolchain/packages/toolchain/src returns nothing. Copilot path-scoped instructions: docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/configure-custom-instructions/add-repository-instructions.
findings.recommendation: Amend item 1 at line 90 to say that .claude/rules is Claude-only. Use it for Claude-specific or file-pattern detail that other agents can live without; anything every agent must obey stays in AGENTS.md. Add one line on legacy files: "Existing `.claude/rules/xylabs-*.md` are legacy output of the removed `xy claude-rules` command. They have no `paths:` and load every session, so delete them rather than adding rules beside them, and never hand-edit them."

findings.title: Overflow list omits skills, the documented destination for procedures and the workspace's managed guidance mechanism
findings.current: agents-md.md:88-94 lists three overflow destinations: `.claude/rules/`, `packages/<pkg>/AGENTS.md`, and `docs/`. Skills are absent.
findings.truth: Claude Code's guidance says multi-step procedures, or entries that matter for only part of the codebase, belong in a skill or a path-scoped rule. Skills load only when invoked or judged relevant, while rules load every session or on file match. In this workspace, per-repo agent guidance is managed as skills: tracked `.agents/skills/**`, `.claude/skills/*` symlinks, pinned by skills-lock.json, managed with `pnpm xy skills`, validated by `pnpm xy check`. The toolchain repo itself carries a local `.agents/skills/xy-work`.
findings.evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory, "When to add to CLAUDE.md" ("If an entry is a multi-step procedure or only matters for one part of the codebase, move it to a skill or a path-scoped rule instead") and the Note under "Organize rules with .claude/rules/"; CLAUDE.md (skills paragraph); toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/skills/installed.ts:6 (PROJECT_SKILL_DIRS = ['.claude/skills', '.agents/skills']); toolchain/.agents/skills/xy-work; toolchain/skills-lock.json.
findings.recommendation: Add a fourth overflow item: "Procedures and task-specific how-tos → a skill (`.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, linked into `.claude/skills/` and managed with `pnpm xy skills`). It loads only when relevant, so it costs nothing per session." Point to the xy-toolchain skill's `xy skills` reference.

findings.title: Adapter guidance for Copilot and Gemini does not reflect their current native AGENTS.md and import support
findings.current: agents-md.md:98: "Every other tool gets a thin adapter that **imports or links** it — never a copy." agents-md.md:120: "Other adapters follow the same rule: `.github/copilot-instructions.md` and `GEMINI.md` carry tool-specific *additions* only."
findings.truth: GitHub Copilot reads AGENTS.md natively, from anywhere in the repo with the nearest file winning, and also accepts a root CLAUDE.md or GEMINI.md. It needs no adapter: copilot-instructions.md is purely additive and is combined with the other instruction files. Its link-only template (templates.md:83-92) is the kind of prose pointer that agents-md.md:118 calls "not good enough". Gemini CLI does not read AGENTS.md by default. GEMINI.md can import it with `@./AGENTS.md` (Memory Import Processor, recursive, default depth 5), or `context.fileName` can list AGENTS.md. So the import pattern used for CLAUDE.md works for GEMINI.md too.
findings.evidence: docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/configure-custom-instructions/add-repository-instructions (AGENTS.md "stored anywhere within the repository"; "the nearest AGENTS.md file in the directory tree will take precedence"; "Alternatively, you can use a single CLAUDE.md or GEMINI.md file stored in the root"); geminicli.com/docs/cli/gemini-md and geminicli.com/docs/reference/memport (context.fileName; @file imports).
findings.recommendation: Rewrite line 120: "Copilot reads AGENTS.md natively, so add `.github/copilot-instructions.md` only for Copilot-specific additions, never as a pointer. Gemini CLI needs `GEMINI.md` containing `@./AGENTS.md` (or `context.fileName` including AGENTS.md), with Gemini-only additions below the import." Soften line 98 to "tools that do not read AGENTS.md natively get a thin import adapter".

findings.title: Size budget omits Codex's 32 KiB combined cap
findings.current: agents-md.md:84-94 cites only Anthropic's under-200-lines guidance. That citation is accurate: the docs say "target under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md file" and that imports "don't reduce its context cost".
findings.truth: Codex stops adding AGENTS.md content once the combined root-to-cwd chain reaches `project_doc_max_bytes`, which defaults to 32 KiB, and silently truncates the rest. That is the hard ceiling for the canonical file, plus any nested files, for Codex users.
findings.evidence: Codex docs (developers.openai.com/codex/guides/agents-md → learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/agents-md): "Codex stops adding files once the combined content reaches the project_doc_max_bytes limit, which defaults to 32 KiB"; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory "Write effective instructions" (Size bullet).
findings.recommendation: Add one sentence: "Codex truncates the combined AGENTS.md chain at 32 KiB (`project_doc_max_bytes`). The 200-line target keeps you well under it, but nested files count toward the same cap."

findings.title: 'Pass an explicit stable id' cannot be done: xy work add has no --id flag, the library has no runtime entry, and ids are random per call
findings.current: auditing.md:102 "**Use a deterministic id.** `createWorkId` embeds today's date, so a re-derived id changes daily and every run creates a duplicate. Pass an explicit stable id derived from the check and the path, and check existence before adding."
findings.truth: `xy work add` / `xyex work add` has no `--id` option. Only the internal `workAdd()` function takes `id`, and @ariestools/toolchain ships no runtime JS entry: the package has only a `types` field, with no main or exports. yargs strict-option mode is not on, so an agent that passes `--id` has it silently ignored and still gets a new id. `createWorkId` also appends 3 random bytes of entropy, so the id changes on every call, not just once a day. Ids must match ^[A-Z0-9][A-Z0-9-]*[A-Z0-9]$, max 250 chars, so a raw path cannot be used. An existing id is overwritten without warning. No CLI command checks whether an item exists without creating the store.
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/toolchain/src/xy/common/work/addCommand.ts:25-80 (options: description, area, tag, file, line, inline, acceptance, verify, impact, urgency, effort, risk, confidence; no id) and :85-104 (handler never passes id); `node packages/toolchain/dist/bin/xyex.mjs work add --help` lists no --id; actions/work/index.ts:104 `id?: string`, :171 `const id = options.id ?? createWorkId(...)`; actions/work/id.ts:13-17 (assertSafeWorkId regex), :20 `entropy = randomBytes(3)...`, :32 `${prefix}-${date}-${entropy}`; store.ts:92-95 writeWorkItem overwrites; packages/toolchain/package.json:30 only `"types": "./dist/index.d.ts"` (`npm view @ariestools/toolchain@10.1.0 main exports module types` → only ./dist/index.d.ts); `grep -rn '.strict()\|strictOptions' packages/toolchain/src/xy` → no hits
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the bullet. Ids are generated randomly on every call and cannot be set from the CLI. To dedupe, anchor each item to the document with `--file <doc path>` and give it a fixed tag (for example `--tag docs-audit`). Before adding, run `pnpm xyex work list --json` and match on `anchors[].path` plus the tag. If a match exists, use `pnpm xyex work update <id> ...` instead of adding a second item. Delete the 'explicit stable id' advice, or label it as future tooling (toolchain work item XYW-20260901-263436).

findings.title: Check catalog is missing the root-document contract the toolchain already enforces
findings.current: auditing.md:27-53 Entry point and Documents tables: no row for AGENTS.md @imports, for README.md/AGENTS.md links to papers/ and docs/, or for the required root/docs/papers/notes files

findings.title: 'Suppress the GitHub dual-write' gives no mechanism; the only switch is repo-wide config, and any xy work command creates the store with dual-write on
findings.current: auditing.md:103 "**Suppress the GitHub dual-write for machine-generated items,** or confirm with the operator first. It is enabled by default and opens a real issue per item as soon as `gh` is authenticated."
findings.truth: No CLI flag or per-item switch exists. Dual-write is controlled only by `stores.github.enabled` in `.xy/work/config.json`, which applies to the whole repo and defaults to true. Running any `xy work` command (add, list, show, triage) in a repo without a store creates that config with GitHub enabled. Dual-write also needs gh installed, authenticated, and pointing at a GitHub repo. If an item is added while gh is unavailable, the next `xy work sync` creates the issue anyway. The toolchain's own docs say read-only inspection must not call `xy work show` or `xy work list`, because they can create store directories.
findings.evidence: toolchain actions/work/schema.ts:79-96 (default `github: { enabled: true }` at :85); store.ts:55-72 (readWorkConfig → ensureWorkStore writes config and creates dirs); sync.ts:29-36 (resolveGithubBridge checks only config.stores.github.enabled plus availability), :145-148 (sync creates issues for unlinked active items); lib/github/runner.ts:42-46 (gh --version, auth status, repo view); addCommand.ts:25-80 (no github flag); docs/plan-manifest.md:285; skills/xy-toolchain/commands.md:221-229 (disable via config.json)
findings.recommendation: Spell out the mechanism. Suppressing dual-write means setting `stores.github.enabled: false` in `.xy/work/config.json`, which changes the setting for the whole repo, so get operator consent. If the repo has no `.xy/work/config.json`, do not run any `xy work` command without consent, because the first run creates the store with dual-write on. Link to xy-toolchain/commands.md#skills-and-work-tracking.

findings.title: 'Close the loop' command omits the required id, and done alone does not close the linked GitHub issue
findings.current: auditing.md:105 "**Close the loop.** When a finding is resolved, `xy work done --evidence <text>`"
findings.truth: The syntax is `xy work done <id> --evidence <text>`: `<id>` is a required positional and `--evidence` is required. `workDone` only writes the local item and never contacts GitHub. The linked issue is closed only by `xy work sync`. Until then, `xy work lint` reports '<id> done/wontfix but GitHub #N open'. If the owner rejects a finding, the right status is `wontfix`, set via `xy work update <id> --status wontfix`.
findings.evidence: toolchain xy/common/work/doneCommand.ts:15-22 (`command: 'done <id>'`, evidence demandOption); actions/work/lifecycle.ts:42-59 (no GitHub call); sync.ts:287-296 (sync closes the issue for done/wontfix), :424-430 (statusMismatch drift); `xyex work update --help` (--status choices include wontfix)
findings.recommendation: Change the example to `pnpm xyex work done <id> --evidence "<what proves it>"`. Add: 'If the item is GitHub-linked, run `pnpm xyex work sync` afterwards (or let `xyex work lint` flag the drift). Close rejected proposals with `xyex work update <id> --status wontfix`.'

findings.title: Orphan-check script's git pathspec skips every top-level docs/*.md file
findings.current: auditing.md:76-77 `for f in $(git ls-files 'docs/**/*.md'); do grep -rqF "$(basename "$f")" AGENTS.md docs/README.md $(git ls-files 'docs/**/*.md' | grep -v "^$f$") ...`
findings.truth: Without `:(glob)` magic, git treats `docs/**/*.md` as an fnmatch pattern that requires a '/' after `docs/<something>`. Files directly under docs/ never match. In the toolchain repo, `git ls-files 'docs/**/*.md'` returns 0 files while `git ls-files 'docs/*.md'` returns 11. The script therefore silently reports no orphans for top-level docs, and they are also left out of the set of files it searches for links.
findings.evidence: cd toolchain && git ls-files 'docs/**/*.md' → (empty); git ls-files 'docs/*.md' | wc -l → 11; git ls-files ':(glob)docs/**/*.md' | wc -l → 11
findings.recommendation: Use `git ls-files ':(glob)docs/**/*.md'`, or `git ls-files 'docs/*.md'` (whose `*` already matches '/'), in both places in the loop.

findings.title: Link-resolution script ignores Markdown links (the form the toolchain requires) and directories
findings.current: auditing.md:58-60 "# links from AGENTS.md that no longer resolve" grep -oE '`[a-zA-Z0-9._/-]+\.(md|json|ts|tsx|mjs|astro)`' ...; auditing.md:36 calls this 'The single highest-value check — it catches renames, deletions, and moved packages'
findings.truth: The regex matches only backticked file paths with six extensions. It never checks Markdown link targets `[x](path)`, which plan.root.docs-index requires AGENTS.md to use for papers/ and docs/, and it never checks directory paths, which are what repository-map rows name, so it cannot catch moved packages. Run against the toolchain's AGENTS.md, it finds 4 backticked paths and misses all 9 Markdown link targets.
findings.evidence: cd toolchain && grep -oE '`...`' AGENTS.md → CLAUDE.md, packages/toolchain/src/bin/xy.ts, packages/toolchain/src/xy/stability.ts, src/bin/xyex.ts; grep -oE '\]\([^)#]+' AGENTS.md → 9 targets (./CONTRIBUTING.md, ./docs/README.md, ./docs/ROADMAP.md, ./docs/STABILITY.md, ./docs/repo-docs.md, ./papers/README.md, ./papers/YELLOW-PAPER.md, ...); toolchain plan/rootDocs.ts:80-102
findings.recommendation: Add a second extraction for Markdown link targets, for example `grep -oE '\]\([^)#[:space:]]+' AGENTS.md | sed 's/^](//'`, skipping http(s) links and resolving each target relative to AGENTS.md. Also check backticked directory paths ending in '/'.

findings.title: Front-matter, staleness and supersession checks ignore .xy/plan.json, which can own document lifecycle metadata
findings.current: auditing.md:46-50 assumes front matter is the only metadata source (front matter present, `state: superseded` ⇒ `supersededBy`, `reviewed`/`date` staleness)
findings.truth: The toolchain ships Plan Manifest v1 (`.xy/plan.json`, created via `xyex plan init`). Its per-document `metadata.source` is either `manifest` or `front-matter`. With `manifest`, the lifecycle, authorityLevel, lastReviewed and supersededBy fields live in the manifest, and the schema says to 'never maintain both'. In such a repo, flagging missing front matter is a false positive, and adding front matter would break the manifest's single-owner rule.
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/toolchain/schemas/plan-manifest.v1.schema.json:334-421 (documentMetadata oneOf; description at :335 'never maintain both'); docs/plan-manifest.md:28-33; `xyex plan --help` (plan init, plan lint); stability.ts:60-62
findings.recommendation: Add a step before the Documents checks: if a reviewed `.xy/plan.json` exists, read each document's `metadata.source`. Where it is `manifest`, take state and review dates from the manifest (lifecycle, lastReviewed, supersededBy) and do not require front matter. Link to the toolchain's docs/plan-manifest.md.

findings.title: 'Nested files are delta-only' contradicts the toolchain contract, which forbids package-level AGENTS.md
findings.current: auditing.md:39 "Nested files are delta-only | warn | A `packages/*/AGENTS.md` that restates the root" (implies a delta-only nested AGENTS.md is fine)
findings.truth: The toolchain's repository Markdown contract, the reference implementation for monorepos, says: 'Keep agent instructions at the repository root. Do not add `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` inside packages.' The package README is the consumer document. No lint rule enforces this yet.

findings.recommendation: Reconcile the two. Either adopt the toolchain rule (any packages/*/AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md is a warn) or keep delta-only and record the divergence with the toolchain. In either case, align agents-md.md 'Nested files' and structure.md:24 with the same decision.

findings.title: Fixer guidance is internally inconsistent and ignores the fixers xy plan lint --fix already ships
findings.current: auditing.md:21 "Only `index` and `archive` are safe to automate as fixers. ... Structural fixes — move a file, regenerate the index, insert a missing front-matter key — are safe"

findings.title: Work-item guidance names fields but not the flags or item type to use
findings.current: auditing.md:104 "Supply `area`, priority, acceptance criteria, and verification." (no flags, no type, no anchor guidance)
findings.truth: `work add <type> <title>` requires a type: bug, todo, feature, idea, debt, research, question or risk. The fields map to flags: `--area`; any one of `--impact`, `--urgency`, `--effort`, `--risk`, `--confidence` sets priority, with unset values defaulting to 3; `--acceptance` and `--verify` are repeatable; `--file`/`--line` anchor the item; `--tag` labels it. findings.title: storage-adapters omits its optional peers idb/mongodb, and the root barrel imports both
findings.current: packages.md:34-47 lists subpaths and `pnpm add @ariestools/storage-adapters` only; lists `@ariestools/storage-adapters` (root barrel) as a normal entry point

findings.title: Fetcher-injection example spreads a Headers instance and silently drops the SDK's Accept/Content-Type/Content-Encoding headers
findings.current: fetch.md:39-40 `const fetcher: FetchFunction = (input, init) => globalThis.fetch(input, { ...init, headers: { ...init?.headers, authorization: token } })`
findings.truth: fetchJson and FetchClient always pass `init.headers` to the fetcher as a `Headers` instance, built by buildHeaders(). fetchCompress also creates `new Headers(init.headers)` and sets `Content-Encoding: gzip` when a body exceeds compressMinLength (1024). Object-spreading a Headers object yields `{}`. The skill's wrapper therefore sends only `authorization`. JSON requests lose Content-Type/Accept, and gzip-compressed bodies arrive without Content-Encoding, so servers receive bodies they cannot decode.
findings.evidence: sdk-js/packages/sdk/src/modules/fetch/fetchJson.ts:9-20 (buildHeaders returns new Headers()), :40; FetchClient.ts:60-71, :174; fetchCompress.ts:49 (compressMinLength = 1024), :57-63 (new Headers + Content-Encoding: gzip). Command: `node -e "const h=new Headers({'content-type':'application/json',accept:'x'}); console.log(JSON.stringify({...h, authorization:'t'}))"` -> `{"authorization":"t"}`.
findings.recommendation: Replace the example with a Headers-safe merge, for example: `const fetcher: FetchFunction = (input, init) => { const headers = new Headers(init?.headers); headers.set('authorization', token); return globalThis.fetch(input, { ...init, headers }) }`. Add a note that init.headers is a Headers object and that injected fetchers must forward `signal`.

findings.title: fetchJson returns a {data,status,...} envelope and does not throw on non-2xx; FetchClient throws FetchClientError. The skill implies neither
findings.current: fetch.md:22 `const data = await fetchJson<MyDto>('https://api.example.com/item')`; fetch.md:24-25 FetchClient get; fetch.md:28-30 lists helpers and error classes with no result or throw semantics
findings.truth: fetchJson and the fetchJsonGet/Post/Put/Patch/Delete helpers resolve to `FetchJsonResponse<T>` = { data: T | null, headers, response, status, statusText }. They do NOT throw on HTTP error statuses: non-2xx bodies are best-effort parsed (malformed gives data: null). Empty bodies give data: null. FetchClient and FetchJsonClient (plus the `fetchJsonClient` singleton) return the same envelope but throw `FetchClientError` (a FetchError of type 'http-status' that carries `config`) when `validateStatus` rejects. The default accepts 2xx and `validateStatus: null` disables the check. Transport and parse failures throw FetchError (types: timeout, aborted, http-status, parse, response-too-large, network).
findings.evidence: sdk-js/packages/sdk/src/modules/fetch/types.ts:10-21 (FetchJsonResponse); fetchJson.ts:31,43-53 (non-ok -> tryParseJson, returns envelope); parseJson.ts:60-82 (tryParseJson returns null on malformed); methods.ts:7-40; FetchClient.ts:17-21 (validateStatus doc), :39-58 (FetchClientError), :197-205 (default 2xx check, throw); FetchJsonClient.ts (subclass + `fetchJsonClient` singleton); FetchError.ts:19-31 (FetchErrorType union).
findings.recommendation: Change the example to `const { data, status } = await fetchJson<MyDto>(url)` and add a short 'Result and error semantics' section: fetchJson* returns the envelope and does not throw on 4xx/5xx (check `status`/`response.ok`); FetchClient/FetchJsonClient throw FetchClientError unless validateStatus allows the status; list the FetchErrorType values and FetchClientError/isFetchError usage.

findings.title: Bounded/cancellable response reads (8.2.0) and the non-stream body fallback (9.0.1) are not covered
findings.current: absent. fetch.md:1-117 covers only fetcher resolution and Undici caching; no mention of maxResponseBytes, timeout, signal, readResponseText, FetchJsonClient options or response-too-large
findings.truth: 8.2.0 (b86f3a024, 2026-08-27) added `maxResponseBytes`, a positive safe integer validated before the request and applied to 2xx and non-2xx bodies. It also added client `timeout`, composed with the caller `signal` through body consumption (first abort wins), the `response-too-large` FetchError type, and the public `readResponseText(response, { maxResponseBytes, signal })` with `ReadResponseTextOptions` in `@ariestools/sdk/fetch/model`. With a cap or signal set, non-2xx read errors propagate instead of resolving to null. 9.0.1 (158476cd7, 2026-09-18) changed bodies that are not WHATWG streams (node-fetch/cross-fetch Readable, React Native whatwg-fetch, test doubles) to fall back to `response.text()`. Abort still rejects promptly, but the body cannot be cancelled, and the cap is checked after buffering against UTF-8 byte length. Before this fix these cases threw `body.getReader is not a function`.
findings.evidence: sdk-js/packages/sdk/src/modules/fetch/types.ts:4-7 (maxResponseBytes); FetchClient.ts:14-15 (timeout), :169 requestSignal(signal, timeout); readResponseText.ts:40 responseTooLargeError, :47 unlessAborted, :130 getReader check, :133-143 text() fallback; index.ts exports readResponseText; model.ts exports ReadResponseTextOptions; sdk-js/packages/sdk/README.md:133-211 'Bounded response reads and cancellation'; `git -C sdk-js show 158476cd7 -s` message; tags v8.2.0 (3814c5f0b) and v9.0.1 (298fbb5bb).
findings.recommendation: Add a 'Bounded reads, timeouts, and cancellation' section to fetch.md with a FetchJsonClient example ({ maxResponseBytes, timeout } plus a per-request signal), the 'response-too-large'/'aborted'/'timeout' error types, readResponseText for text bodies, the rule that injected fetchers must honor `signal`, and the 9.0.1 note on non-stream bodies (requires @ariestools/sdk >= 9.0.1 for node-fetch/cross-fetch/React Native transports). Also add `readResponseText`, `FetchJsonClient`/`fetchJsonClient` and `FetchClientError` to the helper list at fetch.md:28-30.

findings.title: No runtime baseline: 9.0.0 raised every @ariestools/* sdk-js package to engines node >=26
findings.current: absent. overview.md:1-78 and conventions.md:11-13 say only 'ESM only'; nothing on the Node/engines baseline, Vitest major or zod major
findings.truth: The 9.0.0 major (commit 70c8e1942 'Node 26', 2026-09-16; Deploy 5d0008348) changed engines.node from >=18 / >=18.17.1 to >=26 in all 11 published packages, and the repo Volta pin moved to node 26.8.2. crypto-auth now depends on native `Uint8Array.prototype.toBase64` / `Uint8Array.fromBase64` (Node >= 26 and modern browsers). The same window brought Vitest 5 (8.3.0) and zod ^4.6 peers (9.x). There is no other API break between v8.3.0 and v9.0.1 beyond engines, @metamask/json-rpc-engine 10.5 to 11.0, and the zod 4.5 to 4.6 peer bump.
findings.evidence: `git -C sdk-js diff v8.3.0 v9.0.1 -- 'packages/*/package.json'` (engines >=18 -> >=26 in every package; zod ^4.5 -> ^4.6; @metamask/json-rpc-engine ~10.5.0 -> ~11.0.0); sdk-js/packages/sdk/package.json:412-413; sdk-js/package.json volta node 26.8.2; sdk-js/packages/crypto-auth/src/base64.ts:1-14; `npm view @ariestools/testing@9.0.1` engines { node: '>=26' }.
findings.recommendation: Add a 'Runtime baseline' subsection to overview.md: @ariestools/* 9.x requires Node >= 26 (engines), ESM only, Zod 4.6+ where zod helpers or express are used, and Vitest 5 for @ariestools/testing. Consumers on Node < 26 must stay on 8.x. Note the 8 to 9 major is engines-only for most packages, and that crypto-auth additionally needs native Uint8Array base64 support in browsers.

findings.title: @ariestools/testing: `/extended` is a side-effect matcher registration (and the root does it too); vitest 5 is a hard dependency

findings.title: crypto-auth API, versioned PBKDF2 and native-base64 runtime constraint are undocumented
findings.current: packages.md:83-91 "Self-contained password and seed-phrase encryption/decryption (vault-style crypto)." plus an install line and a note about logging secrets
findings.truth: Since 8.1.5 and 8.1.6 (2026-07-22 to 07-27), the package exposes `SeedPhraseVault(store: SeedPhraseStore, walletKind?, crypto: VaultCrypto = defaultVaultCrypto)`, with the storage and crypto backend both injected. Key methods: addSelfDescribingPhrase (returns { key, record }), openSeedPhrase, verifyPasswordForRecord, upgradeRecordKdf, deriveKeyForRecord, static recordNeedsRehash/resolveRecordKdf, plus `SeedPhraseDecryptError`. Supporting exports: `Pbkdf2AesGcmVaultCrypto`, `PasswordKey`, deriveKeyFromPassword/deriveKeyFromValues/deriveKeyAndValues/verifyPassword/needsRehash, encryptSeedPhrase/decryptSeedPhrase, and bytesToBase64/base64ToBytes. Records are self-describing (salt + keyMetadata { algorithm: 'PBKDF2', params.iterations }). New keys use DEFAULT_PBKDF2_ITERATIONS = 600_000, legacy records without metadata are read at LEGACY_PBKDF2_ITERATIONS = 100_000, and keys are non-extractable. Since 9.0.0 base64 uses native `Uint8Array.prototype.toBase64` / `Uint8Array.fromBase64` (Node >= 26 and modern browsers).
findings.evidence: sdk-js/packages/crypto-auth/src/index.ts:1-7; src/SeedPhraseVault.ts:17,31-41,52,63,87-106,183,205,230; src/models/VaultCrypto.ts:13-25; src/models/SeedPhraseStore.ts:8-15; src/models/KeyMetadata.ts:12,20,42; src/password.ts:16,28,38,53,67; src/base64.ts:1-14; commits b55822092, 74fb068a3, e3ecb8f0f, f04856eca (2026-07-22/23).
findings.recommendation: Expand packages.md:83-91 with: the SeedPhraseVault + injected SeedPhraseStore/VaultCrypto pattern; use addSelfDescribingPhrase for new records and openSeedPhrase/verifyPasswordForRecord for reads; check recordNeedsRehash/needsRehash and call upgradeRecordKdf to raise legacy 100k records to 600k; never persist or log derived keys. State the runtime requirement for native Uint8Array base64 (Node >= 26 or a current browser).

findings.title: @ariestools/threads: no API or entry-point guidance; exports are node/browser-conditional only
findings.current: packages.md:49-57 "Run work in worker threads or web workers with a function-call style API." plus an install line, nothing else
findings.truth: Master side: `spawn`, `Pool`, `Thread`, `Worker`, `BlobWorker`, `Transfer`, `registerSerializer`, `DefaultSerializer`, with Node-only `installWorkerSignalHandlers` and `isWorkerRuntime`. Worker side: `expose` (plus registerSerializer and Transfer) from `@ariestools/threads/worker`. `@ariestools/threads/register` is a Node-only side-effect import that installs `globalThis.Worker`. The root, /master, /pool, /worker and /implementation exports have only `browser` and `node` conditions, with no default. `observable-fns ^0.6` is a peer and is also a direct dependency. The package README marks it as public-only with zero consumers inside the monorepo, and 8.3.0 added node pool/spawn E2E coverage.
findings.evidence: sdk-js/packages/threads/package.json:29-104 (exports map; ./register at :89-93 node-only; ./worker at :95-103); src/index-node.ts and src/index-browser.ts; src/master/index-node.ts (spawn, Pool, Thread, Worker, BlobWorker, installWorkerSignalHandlers); src/worker/worker.node.ts:53-73 (export { expose }); src/master/register.ts:7-11; packages/threads/README.md 'Internal status: public-only package with zero consumers'; commit d4dadd220 (threads hardening).

findings.title: Compile config does not deep-merge root into package; nearest xy.config wins for compile.*
findings.current: compilation.md:29 "Root configuration cascades to packages under that root. Package-level configuration overrides or deep-merges the applicable root settings."
findings.truth: Only `commands.*` merge root + workspace (loadWorkspaceCommandConfig). `xy compile` spawns `package-compile` in each workspace directory, and packageCompile loads config with a cosmiconfig search from that directory, so the nearest config file wins. A package xy.config.ts replaces the root `compile` block completely (shared fields such as `compiler` must be repeated). A package with no config of its own inherits the root file unchanged. `compile.validator`, and the native check that goes with it, is read from the root config only. The publint expected-output check deep-merges root + package, so it can disagree with what compile actually emits.
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/toolchain/src/actions/package/compile/compile.ts:16-19 (packageCompile → loadConfig(inConfig) from cwd); lib/loadConfig.ts:52-59,61-93 (cosmiconfig search() from process.cwd(); loadConfig = deepMerge(nearestConfig, params)); lib/loadConfig.ts:195-207,229-245 (only command configs merge root+workspace); pm/pnpmPackageManager.ts:180-188 (`pnpm --filter <pkg> exec run-or-exec package-compile` runs in the package dir); actions/compile.ts:348-355 (validator from root config only); actions/package/expectedCompileOutputs.ts:83-88 (publint deep-merges root+pkg, which is inconsistent with compile). Real-world corroboration: sdk-js/xy.config.ts:4 sets `compile: { compiler: 'native' }` yet every sdk-js packages/*/xy.config.ts (crypto-auth:2, crypto, eth-address:2, express, meta:2, pixel, sdk) repeats `compiler: 'native'`. Toolchain docs/xy-config.md:15 makes the same inaccurate deep-merge claim.
findings.recommendation: Replace line 29 with: "`commands.*` settings cascade: root and package configs merge (arrays concatenate, maps merge, `rules` replace per rule id). `compile` does not merge. Each package compiles with the nearest xy.config file, so a package xy.config.ts replaces the root `compile` block. Repeat shared compile fields such as `compiler` in every package config that exists. Set `compile.validator` at the root only." Also file a toolchain issue to make compile and publint's expectedCompileOutputs agree, and to fix docs/xy-config.md:15.

findings.title: `commands.dependabot.rules` fails typecheck in a typed XyConfig (key missing from CommandsConfig)
findings.current: commands.md:150 "raise levels under `commands.dependabot.rules` to gate" (the skill's standard pattern is `const config: XyConfig = {...}`)
findings.truth: At runtime, `xy secure dependabot` reads `commands.dependabot`. The published 10.1.0 `CommandsConfig` type has no `dependabot` key, and no `workLint` key either. A typed object literal with `commands: { dependabot: ... }` is rejected with TS2353. Full-package validation and editors then fail.
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/toolchain/src/actions/package/compile/XyConfig.ts:655-678 (CommandsConfig keys: apiExposure, clean, dead, deplint, gitLint, gitlint, license, lintLint, lintlint, nodeLint, npmOrgLint, packman, planLint, publint, repoLint, skillsLint; there is no dependabot or workLint key); same in published dist/actions/package/compile/XyConfig.d.ts:598-621; lib/ruleCommandRegistry.ts:48-53,125-130 (configKey 'dependabot' / 'workLint'); actions/secure/dependabot.ts:111-117. Scratch check with toolchain tsc 7.0.2 against the dist types: `check.ts(5,5): error TS2353: Object literal may only specify known properties, and 'dependabot' does not exist in type 'CommandsConfig'.` (same for workLint). The spread form `commands: { deplint: {}, ...{ dependabot } }` typechecks.
findings.recommendation: State that `commands.dependabot` (and `commands.workLint`) work at runtime but are missing from the `XyConfig` type in 10.1.0. Give the workaround of spreading a hoisted object into `commands` (`...{ dependabot: { rules: {...} } }`) alongside at least one typed key. File a toolchain fix that adds `dependabot?: { rules?: RuleLevelConfigMap }` and `workLint?: { rules?: RuleLevelConfigMap }` to CommandsConfig, then drop the workaround once that ships.

findings.title: Document experimental `compile.compiler: 'native'` / `nativePackage` and `xyex enable ts-native`
findings.current: absent: compilation.md covers `validator` (lines 84-93) but never mentions `compile.compiler` or `nativePackage`
findings.truth: `compile.compiler` is 'typescript' (the default) or 'native', which uses TypeScript 7 Go. It is an experimental config surface. `nativePackage` defaults to 'typescript-native', installed as the alias `npm:typescript@~7.0.2`. The supported setup is `xyex enable ts-native`, which adds the alias, sets the field, and clears a shared validator. `validator: 'shared'` with `compiler: 'native'` silently falls back to per-package validation. The flagship @ariestools/sdk-js sets `compiler: 'native'` in the root config and every package config, and 21 xy.config.ts files in the workspace use `compiler:`.
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/toolchain/src/actions/package/compile/XyConfig.ts:142-157,171-177; xy/stability.ts:147-151 (id compile.compiler.native: 'Enable with `xyex enable ts-native`... public examples must not require it'); actions/package/compile/resolveTscBin.ts:22,29,34; actions/compile.ts:348-355 (shared+native → warn, per-package); `node dist/bin/xy.mjs enable --help` → "pnpm xy enable ts-native ... (experimental — prefer xyex)"; sdk-js/xy.config.ts:4 and sdk-js/packages/*/xy.config.ts.
findings.recommendation: Add a "Compiler implementation (experimental)" subsection under Type validation. Cover: `compile.compiler: 'typescript' | 'native'` and `compile.nativePackage`. Enable with `pnpm xyex enable ts-native` rather than editing by hand. TS7 exports no compiler API. It cannot combine with `validator: 'shared'`, which falls back to per-package. It is listed under `xy --stability`. Do not require it in public examples. Because of the compile cascade rule, set it in every package config that exists.

findings.title: entryMode semantics are wrong or incomplete (`auto` is a no-op alias of `single`; custom entries location; monolith rejects entryMode)
findings.current: compilation.md:58-64 "`single` targets the normal package entry... `platform` uses platform entry files. `custom` accepts explicit `{ in, out }` entries. `auto` lets the compiler derive the applicable shape."
findings.truth: buildEntries has no `auto` branch, so `auto` falls to the default `['index.ts']`, the same as `single`. `platform` means exactly `index-node.ts` + `index-browser.ts`. `custom` starts empty and uses only the per-target `entry` list (`compile.<node|browser|neutral>: { src: { entry: [...] } }`). That list takes string paths or `{in,out}`, and `{in,out}` throws unless entryMode is 'custom'. In other modes, `entry` items are appended to the defaults. `transpile` defaults entryMode to 'all'. Monolith mode throws if `compile.entryMode` is set. `compile.esbuild.options` is the esbuild passthrough, and `compile.tsup` is deprecated but still honored.
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/toolchain/src/actions/package/compile/buildEntries.ts:17-48; packageCompileEsbuild.ts:131-138 ("{in, out} entries require entryMode 'custom'"); resolveCompileBundleOptions.ts:90-93; packageCompileMonolith.ts:20-21 ('monolith mode computes entries; remove compile.entryMode'); resolveCompilePlatforms.ts:17 (`true` → `{ src: {} }`); XyConfig.ts:35,224-239,253-272. Usage: sdk-js/packages/crypto/xy.config.ts and packages/pixel/xy.config.ts (`entryMode: 'custom'` with `browser: { src: { entry: ['./index.ts', './model.ts'] } }`).
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the entryMode list. `single` (default): `src/index.ts`. `all`: every source file except specs, stories and .d.ts (default for `transpile`). `platform`: `src/index-node.ts` + `src/index-browser.ts`. `custom`: only the `entry` array under `compile.<target>.src`, as strings or `{in,out}`. Say `auto` currently behaves like `single` and should not be used. Add that monolith rejects `entryMode`, and that extra `entry` items append in non-custom modes. Mention `compile.esbuild.options` for esbuild overrides, and `tsup` as deprecated.

findings.title: Stable command configs missing: commands.publint, apiExposure, license, packman
findings.current: absent: commands.md:129-131 (publint), 125-127 (api-exposure), 137-139 (license: 'against the configured allowlist') and 159 (packman) say nothing about how to configure them, and the 'Configuration and automation' example (293-317) shows only dead/deplint
findings.truth: `commands.publint` takes `{ include | exclude: <check names>, pack (default true), rules: { 'pub.<check>' | '<check>': level } }`. The `boolean` form is accepted by the type but ignored, because booleans normalize to `{}`. `commands.apiExposure` takes `packages[name].classification`, `peerForwarding` (default 'when-exposed'; 'always' or 'when-used'), `peerWithDefault`, `rules`, `thresholds` (39/79/119/179) and `treeShaking` (default true). findings.title: Skills-lint config (`commands.skillsLint.additionalSkills`, package.json `xy.skills`) missing, plus the cosmiconfig shadowing hazard
findings.current: commands.md:171 "Use `xy skills lint --fix` to install missing profile-required skills" and nothing else about configuration
findings.truth: `commands.skillsLint.additionalSkills` adds required skills on top of the detected profile. Root and workspace lists are unioned, and unknown names are config errors. Packages can recommend skills through package.json `xy.skills` (`[{ name, source? }]`), enforced by the error-level `skills.package-recommended`. Hazard: cosmiconfig('xy') puts `package.json` first in its search places and reads its `xy` property as config. A package.json with an `xy` key therefore becomes that directory's entire xy config, and a sibling xy.config.ts (compile, commands) is silently ignored.
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/toolchain/src/actions/package/compile/XyConfig.ts:634-647; actions/skills/packageSkills.ts:159-170; docs/xy-config.md:62-101; `xy skills lint --rules` → `error │ skills.package-recommended`; lib/loadConfig.ts:52-57 (cosmiconfig('xy') with default searchPlaces); node_modules/cosmiconfig@10.0.1 dist/defaults.js:5-28 ('package.json' first) and Explorer.js:115-121 (reads packageProp = moduleName). Empirical probe in scratch: dir containing package.json {"xy":{"skills":[...]}} plus xy.config.ts → search() returned filepath package.json, config {"skills":[...]}, and xy.config.ts was ignored. No current repo uses a top-level `xy` key, so the hazard is latent. Added 2026-09-08 (a4cd25cdc) and 2026-09-25 (881eede39).
findings.recommendation: Add a Skills subsection covering `additionalSkills` with an example, and `xy.skills` in package.json. Warn that a package.json `xy` key replaces xy.config.ts for that directory, so `xy.skills` should only go in packages that have no xy.config.ts until the toolchain fixes the clash. Also raise a toolchain issue: set cosmiconfig `searchPlaces` to exclude package.json, or use a non-colliding packageProp.

findings.title: Says no tooling exists, but experimental `xyex plan lint/init` + `commands.planLint` + `.xy/plan.json` ship with a conflicting fixed layout

findings.title: The canonical tree contradicts the toolchain's `xyex plan lint` layout; its `--fix` moves xy-agent-style papers into notes/
findings.current: The canonical tree at structure.md:5-27 has `papers/`, `specs/`, `docs/{README,decisions,runbooks,plans,evidence,archive}`, `references/` and `prototypes/`. It has no `notes/`, no `docs/ROADMAP.md`, and no root CHANGELOG.md or CONTRIBUTING.md. structure.md:29 says "Not every repository needs every tier… an empty `papers/` directory is a lie", and :50 sets the naming as `<PRODUCT>_{WHITE,YELLOW,GREEN,LIGHT}_PAPER.md`.
findings.truth: `xyex plan lint` (experimental, shipped in 10.1.0) enforces a different canonical layout, with every rule at error level. It requires root AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, CHANGELOG.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and README.md. It requires papers/README.md, papers/WHITE-PAPER.md and papers/YELLOW-PAPER.md, allows only GREEN-PAPER.md besides those, and flags any other file (error `plan.papers.unexpected-files`). It also requires docs/README.md, docs/ROADMAP.md and notes/README.md. `--fix` relocates unexpected paper files into notes/. A repository that follows xy-agent (for example `ACME_WHITE_PAPER.md` or `ACME_LIGHT_PAPER.md`, and no notes/) therefore fails plan lint, and the fix moves its papers.
findings.evidence: packages/toolchain/src/actions/plan/lint.ts:19-37 (required and optional path lists), :477-512 (rules with defaultLevel 'error'; "fixes flatten other regular files into notes/"). `xy.mjs plan lint --help`: "Create missing required files and relocate unexpected regular paper files to notes/". The toolchain CHANGELOG [Unreleased] says canonical planning documents now use papers/WHITE-PAPER.md, papers/YELLOW-PAPER.md and docs/ROADMAP.md. stability.ts:60 marks plan as experimental.
findings.recommendation: Reconcile the two layouts; they come from the same owner and should not disagree. One option is to adopt the toolchain's names (papers/WHITE-PAPER.md, YELLOW-PAPER.md, optional GREEN-PAPER.md and README.md, docs/ROADMAP.md, notes/README.md, root CHANGELOG.md and CONTRIBUTING.md) and say where specs/, LIGHT papers and product-prefixed names belong. The other is to file a toolchain work item to make plan lint's allowlist configurable through `commands.planLint`. At minimum, add a note that repositories using `pnpm xyex plan lint` must follow its layout, and that `--fix` moves non-allowlisted papers into notes/.

findings.title: The `xy skills` surface is thin: `xy skills defaults`, the passthrough subcommands and the skills-lint configuration are missing
findings.current: commands.md:169-171 has one sentence: "`xy skills` wraps the bundled Skills.sh CLI and adds XY-aware defaults, linting, and updates. Use `xy skills lint --fix` to install missing profile-required skills; use `--offline`…"
findings.truth: `xy skills defaults [-g] [-a <agent>] [--copy]` installs ariestools-skills `--all` plus the XYO/XL1 stack from xyo-skills. `xy skills lint` accepts --fix, --offline, --rules and --strict. Its `--fix` installs missing skills, migrates relocated sources and updates outdated ones. Requirements come from the detected tier, from `package.json` `xy.skills` on workspaces and dependencies, and from `commands.skillsLint.additionalSkills`. Other subcommands pass through to Skills.sh (add, update, list/ls, remove, find, use, experimental_install from skills-lock.json, experimental_sync). `xy skills --help` prints Skills.sh help, not the XY additions. xyo-skills tells users to run `xy skills defaults` 24 times.
findings.evidence: src/xy/common/skills/index.ts:14-30 (defaults help), :31 (LINT_FLAGS), :46-77 (lint help: xy.skills, commands.skillsLint.additionalSkills, --fix semantics, --strict). src/actions/skills/defaults.ts:13-27 and :66-73. `xy.mjs skills --help` output. xyo-skills README.md:23 and :150.
findings.recommendation: Add a small "Skills" table: `xy skills defaults` (what it installs from each source), `xy skills lint [--fix|--offline|--strict|--rules]` (what --fix changes), passthrough commands such as `xy skills add/update/list/experimental_install`, `xy skills lint --help` for XY-specific help, and the `xy.skills` / `commands.skillsLint.additionalSkills` requirement sources.

findings.title: The `xy repo lint` description omits error-level rules that a new package will trip, such as the package README rules
findings.current: commands.md:160: "Workspace structure, versions, engines, package-manager fields, spec layout, and Dependabot enablement". The new-package steps in toolchain.md:110-122 never say to add a README.
findings.truth: Several `repo lint` rules default to error and run inside `xy check`. `repo.package-readme` requires a consumer README.md in every workspace package except the root, and `repo.package-readme-files` requires publishable packages to list README.md in `files`. The others are repo.internal-dependency-ranges, repo.internal-peer-ranges, repo.root-private, repo.volta-only-root, repo.no-private-publish-config and repo.workspace-glob-coverage, plus repo.pnpm-no-overrides at warn. Both README rules can be fixed with `--fix`.
findings.evidence: src/actions/package-lint.ts:350-361 (package-readme rules with fixers). `xy.mjs --rules --json` shows those rule IDs and levels. Present in the 10.1.0 dist (`grep -l repo.package-readme packages/toolchain/dist/bin/xy.mjs`). CHANGELOG [Unreleased] "Added" lists both README rules. src/xy/common/checkCommand.ts runs packageLintMonorepo inside `xy check`.
findings.recommendation: Expand the repo lint row to name the README, internal-range and root-private families. Add a step to the new-package baseline: each workspace package gets a consumer README.md, and publishable ones include it in `files`. Point to `pnpm xy repo lint --rules` for the full list and to `xy check --fix` to scaffold the files.

findings.title: The release commands `xy deploy` and `xy publish` (including `--tag`) are not documented
findings.current: Absent. The skill never mentions `deploy` or `publish`; the router in SKILL.md only says "validating publish surfaces".
findings.truth: Both commands are stable. `xy deploy [patch|minor|major|prerelease]` bumps lockstep versions, runs `xy clean` and `xy build`, then applies the version. `xy publish` publishes to npm and accepts `--tag <dist-tag>` (prereleases should use next or canary so latest stays on stable) and `--chunk-size <n>` (pnpm only; each chunk triggers a separate 2FA prompt).
findings.evidence: src/xy/stability.ts:34-35. src/actions/deploy.ts:7-18. `xy.mjs deploy --help` (choices patch/minor/major/prerelease, default patch). `xy.mjs publish --help` (--tag, --chunk-size). docs/STABILITY.md:26-32 ("pnpm xy publish --tag next"). Toolchain README.md:107-109.
findings.recommendation: Add a "Release" subsection: `pnpm xy deploy <level>` (what it runs, and that it bumps every lockstep package), then `pnpm xy publish` or `pnpm xy publish --tag next` for prereleases. Note that repositories using release-please or CI publishing should follow their own workflow instead.

findings.title: The experimental and React-only commands are not catalogued (plan, orphan, npm-org, enable ts-native, tsc-validate, packman convert/clean, sonar, start/analyze/eject/sitemap)
findings.current: Absent. compilation.md:90 alludes to the shared validator without naming `xyex tsc-validate`, and nothing else in the skill mentions these commands.
findings.truth: All of these are registered in 10.1.0. Experimental: `xyex plan init [--dry-run --project-id --summary]`, `xyex plan lint [--fix]`, `xyex orphan list|clean` (overlaps `xy clean --full`), `xyex npm-org lint [org] [--min-downloads --max-age-days --include-deprecated]`, `xyex enable ts-native [--no-install]`, `xyex tsc-validate [package]`, `xyex packman convert <bun|npm|pnpm|yarn>`, `xyex packman clean` (removes node_modules and lockfiles), and `xyex sonar` (quarantined; needs a local sonar.eslintrc; may be removed). The React commands register only in React repositories: `start` is stable, while analyze, eject and sitemap are experimental. start and eject wrap `react-scripts`.
findings.evidence: src/xy/stability.ts:20, 31, 49, 53-55, 58-60, 71-74. --help output for each command, run in an empty directory with XY_NO_DEFER=1. src/xy/xy.ts (React commands register only when `isReactProject()`). src/actions/start.ts and eject.ts (`react-scripts start` / `eject`). docs/STABILITY.md:90-102 (why each stays experimental).
findings.recommendation: Add a compact "Labs (xyex) and framework commands" table with one line per command: purpose, the `xyex` invocation, and any hazard (packman clean deletes lockfiles; sonar is quarantined; start and eject are legacy CRA wrappers, not for Vite or Next). Cross-link plan lint from xy-agent.

findings.title: Layer 1 recommends `pnpm --filter <package> build`, which fails in xy-toolchain repositories
findings.current: workflow.md:24-27: "Use workspace-aware commands: `pnpm --filter <package> build`, not `cd packages/foo && pnpm build`". Lines 18-21 treat root `build`/`lint`/`test` scripts as the norm.
findings.truth: In xy monorepos, packages usually have no `build` script; the root `xy` CLI orchestrates them. In sdk-js, toolchain and sdk-react, none of the 32 packages has a `build` script, and sdk-js and sdk-react have no root build, lint or test scripts either. `pnpm --filter <pkg> build` therefore fails with a missing-script error. The workspace convention is to run from the repo root and pass the package name: `pnpm xy build @ariestools/sdk`. xy-toolchain never explicitly overrides the Layer 1 example.
findings.evidence: `grep -l '"build"' packages/*/package.json` returns 0 of 13 in sdk-js, 0 of 8 in toolchain and 0 of 11 in sdk-react. sdk-js/package.json scripts contain only docs and test:coverage entries. CLAUDE.md: "Always run from the repo root, never from inside a package directory… Append a package name to scope: `pnpm xy build @ariestools/sdk`". src/xy/build/buildCommand.ts accepts `build [package]`.
findings.recommendation: Make the Layer 1 example generic, for example: "use the repository's workspace-scoping mechanism (a toolchain package argument or `pnpm --filter`) rather than `cd`, and defer to the Layer 2 toolchain skill when one is installed". In xy-toolchain/toolchain.md, state explicitly: "target a package with `pnpm xy <cmd> <package>` from the root; do not use `pnpm --filter <pkg> build`, because packages have no build script".

findings.title: The templates embed a nonexistent command (`pnpm xy agent index`) and the experimental `pnpm xy work list`
