findings.title: The global-flag table has the wrong `--jobs` default and omits `-v`, `-i` and the environment-variable equivalents
findings.current: commands.md:21: "`--jobs <n>` | Limit parallel work; default is 16". The table at :19-27 has no `--verbose` or `--incremental`, and no `XY_STRICT` or `XY_NO_DEFER`. The `--no-defer` row says only "Bypass a same-named local package script".
findings.truth: The `--jobs` default is `availableParallelism()`; it shows 16 only on a 16-core machine. Other global flags are `-v/--verbose` and `-i/--incremental`; the latter defaults to on for compile, build and lint, and `--no-incremental` disables it. `XY_STRICT=1` equals `--strict` and `XY_NO_DEFER=1` equals `--no-defer`. Deferral applies only to a root package.json script with the same name, and only when no subcommand is given.
findings.evidence: src/xy/xyParseOptions.ts:58, :61 and :88-100 (`default: availableParallelism()`). src/lib/tryRunLocalScript.ts:13-37. src/xy/build/buildCommand.ts and compileCommand.ts (`incremental: argv.incremental !== false`).
findings.recommendation: Change the default to "available CPU parallelism". Add rows for `-v/--verbose` and `-i/--incremental`, and a note on `XY_STRICT=1`, `XY_NO_DEFER=1` and when deferral happens (root script with the same name, no subcommand).

findings.title: Stable lifecycle and utility commands are missing: cycle, gitignore, npmignore-gen, copy-assets, statics, install, reinstall, up, updo
findings.current: Absent; the skill never mentions any of these commands.

findings.evidence: src/xy/stability.ts:15-45. --help output for each command. src/actions/reinstall.ts:1-11 (calls packmanClean). `xy.mjs packman clean --help`: "Remove node_modules and lock files". src/actions/up.ts (`pm.outdated()`).
findings.recommendation: Add a short "Other stable commands" table. Warn that `xy reinstall` and `xy gitignore` are destructive (lockfile and .gitignore removal), consistent with typescript.md:125's advice against reinstalling as a first response. Mention `xy updo` as the toolchain's dependency-update flow.

findings.title: The ESLint commands table lacks `--mode`, `--no-cache`, `--meta` and the `xy cycle` companion

The hidden flags `--next` and `--prev` are deprecated aliases for `--mode`. `xy cycle [--depth]` runs import-cycle checking separately.

findings.title: The `xy publint` check-selection and pack flags are undocumented
findings.current: commands.md:129-131 describes only `--fix`.

The `pub.importsMatchExports` and `pub.platform` rules default to error.
findings.evidence: `xy.mjs publint --help`. `xy.mjs --rules --json` (publint pub.* levels).
findings.recommendation: Add one line covering `--include/--exclude <checks>`, `--fresh`, and `--no-pack` for quick local runs. Mention the two error-level rules, which cannot be auto-fixed.

findings.title: The validation section omits the native compiler (`xyex enable ts-native`) and `xyex tsc-validate`
findings.current: compilation.md:84-93 covers `compile.validate`, the package-compile flags and `compile.validator`, but never mentions `compile.compiler` or the tsc-validate command.
findings.truth: `compile.compiler: 'native'` (TypeScript 7 / Go) is an experimental surface enabled with `pnpm xyex enable ts-native [--no-install]`, and it is incompatible with the shared validator. `xyex tsc-validate [package]` runs the shared-host engine as a standalone command. Public examples must not require the native compiler.
findings.evidence: src/xy/stability.ts:20 and :49. EXPERIMENTAL_CONFIG_SURFACES entries compile.compiler.native and compile.validator.shared (stability.ts, around line 140). `xy.mjs enable ts-native --help`. docs/ROADMAP.md D4.
findings.recommendation: Add two bullets: `compile.compiler: 'native'` is experimental, is set up via `xyex enable ts-native`, does not combine with `validator: 'shared'`, and should not appear in public templates. `xyex tsc-validate` is the standalone form of the shared validator.

findings.title: The `xy fix` composition is inaccurate, and node lint's relation to check and fix is unstated
findings.current: commands.md:40: "`xy fix [package]` | Git lint, deplint, repo lint, publint, and ESLint fixes". The policy table at :156-163 lists `xy node lint` alongside the `xy check` families.
findings.truth: `xy fix` runs git lint --fix, deplint --fix, repo lint --fix, publint --fix, lint --fix and `lint lint --fix` (ESLint-config normalization). It does not run packman lint or skills lint fixes, so it differs from `xy check --fix`. `xy node lint` is in neither `xy check` nor `xy fix`; run it separately with `--fix`.
findings.evidence: src/actions/fix.ts:17-27. src/xy/common/checkCommand.ts (git, packman, publint, repo, lint lint, skills). src/actions/ruleCatalog.ts:320-342.
findings.recommendation: Change the row to "git lint, deplint, repo lint, publint, ESLint, and ESLint-config (lint lint) fixes; not packman or skills — use `xy check --fix` for those". Note under the policy table that `xy node lint [--fix]` runs standalone.

findings.title: The `package-*` hook guidance conflicts with STABILITY.md and the hook list is incomplete
findings.current: toolchain.md:68-90 tells agents to "Use `package-*` binaries as per-package hooks" and lists seven hooks plus the `-only` variants. compilation.md:103-108 tells agents to run `package-sync-layout` by hand.
findings.truth: STABILITY.md calls the `package-*` bins an implementation detail of `xy` and asks docs and automation to prefer the `xy` CLI. The package also ships package-copy-assets-cjs, package-copy-assets-esm, package-lint-verbose, package-relint (the counterpart of the deprecated relint) and run-or-exec. `xy compile` already re-syncs the monolith layout, so manual `package-sync-layout` is needed only for `--check` drift detection.
findings.evidence: docs/STABILITY.md:53. packages/toolchain/package.json bin map. src/actions/package/compile/packageCompileMonolith.ts:157 (calls syncMonolithLayout during compile). src/bin/package/sync-layout.ts:11 (`--check`).
findings.recommendation: State that `package-*` hooks are for package-script extension only, not for direct use in docs or CI. Keep the `-only` recursion guidance. Note that `xy compile` syncs monolith layout automatically and that `package-sync-layout --check` is the CI drift check.

findings.title: The work section omits the triage and anchor flags and the `.xy/work`-tracked / `.xy/cache`-ignored rule
findings.current: commands.md:177-201 shows `work add <type> <title>` with no `--area`, priority, `--acceptance`, `--verify`, `--file`/`--line`/`--inline` or list filters. Git policy at :158 says only "LF settings and case sensitivity".
findings.truth: `work add` and `work update` accept --area, --tag, --impact, --urgency, --effort, --risk, --confidence (each 1-5), --acceptance and --verify (both repeatable), and --file/--line/--inline; an item missing these counts as untriaged. `work list` accepts --status, --type and --sort created|priority, and `work queue` accepts --name, --limit and --status. `work.store-not-gitignored` (error) requires `.xy/work` to stay tracked, while `git.ignore-toolchain-cache` expects `**/.xy/cache/` to be ignored in every package.
findings.evidence: `xyex work add|list|queue|update --help`. Toolchain-local .agents/skills/xy-work/SKILL.md:24-56 and :146-150. `xy --rules --json` (work.store-not-gitignored error; git.ignore-toolchain-cache warn). src/actions/gitlintIgnore.ts:7-9 (`'**/.xy/cache/'`, "never .xy/work, which is tracked").
findings.recommendation: Add a capture example with triage fields, for example `pnpm xyex work add bug "…" --area x --impact 4 --urgency 2 --effort 1 --risk 2 --confidence 3 --acceptance "…" --verify "pnpm xy build"`. Add the list and queue filters, and a one-line gitignore rule: ignore `**/.xy/cache/`, never `.xy/work`. Consider folding in the toolchain-local xy-work skill's content.

findings.title: `any` escape hatch says a TODO comment is enough, but `any` is a lint error at every tier
findings.current: "5. **Only then: `any`** — with a `// TODO: [reason alternatives don't work]` comment explaining the constraint." (skills/xy-development/typescript.md:17)
findings.truth: `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` is `error` at every tier, type-checked or not, because it comes from typescript-eslint `flat/recommended`. Code that follows step 5 fails `xy lint` / `xy build` unless a disable directive is added. Workspace policy also says 'no `any` (use `unknown` + guards)'.
findings.evidence: Effective config computed via ESLint calculateConfigForFile on toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/index.ts with eslint-config-flat dist 10.1.0: `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any error` at tier 0 (isTypeChecked false), tier 2, tier 3 and tier 4. Source: toolchain/packages/eslint-config-flat/src/typescript/index.ts:185-203 (scopes flatConfigs['flat/recommended'] and 'flat/recommended-type-checked', with no override for no-explicit-any). CLAUDE.md:45 says "no `any` (use `unknown` + guards)".
findings.recommendation: Rewrite step 5 to say `any` is lint-forbidden (`@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` = error). The last resort becomes a scoped `// eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any -- <why unknown/generics/overloads fail>` on the single line, never a file-level disable. Keep the containment advice in lines 19-21.

findings.title: `xy lint init` is described as automatic; it is interactive and offers deprecated or nonexistent SDK barrels
findings.current: "It detects React, installs the applicable config package and ESLint, generates `eslint.config.ts`, includes repository `.gitignore` behavior when the file exists, and derives root-barrel import restrictions from installed SDK barrels." (eslint.md:22). Also "Add `configReactStorybook` explicitly only when Storybook files need that layer" (eslint.md:70) while eslint.md:28 says "Use the generator's output as canonical."
findings.truth: lint-init asks readline y/N questions: whether to replace an existing eslint.config.ts/.mjs, plus one question per barrel. The 7 offered barrels are @xylabs/sdk-js (deprecated, use @ariestools/sdk), @xylabs/sdk-react (deprecated, use @ariestools/sdk-react), @xyo-network/sdk-js (deprecated, use @xyo-network/sdk), @xyo-network/react-chain (npm E404), and three live @xyo-network barrels. @ariestools/sdk is not offered. Answering y to a barrel that is not installed adds it as a devDependency at 'latest' and runs install. The generator always adds `...configReactStorybook` for React repos, ignores `**/*.md`, and writes `eslint: '^10.0.0'`, which is below the config package peer `^10.3`.
findings.evidence: toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/lint-init.ts:60-68 (BARREL_DESCRIPTORS), :76-82 (eslint '^10.0.0'), :107-114 and :130 (React always imports and spreads configReactStorybook), :129 (ignores include '**/*.md'), :201-215 (ensureBarrelInstalled adds `latest` and installs), :244-253 (replace prompt), :262-268 (per-barrel prompts). `npm view @xylabs/sdk-js deprecated` returns 'Use @ariestools/sdk instead…'. `npm view @xylabs/sdk-react deprecated` returns 'Use @ariestools/sdk-react instead…'. `npm view @xyo-network/sdk-js deprecated` returns 'Use @xyo-network/sdk instead…'. `npm view @xyo-network/react-chain` returns E404. eslint-config-flat/package.json:71-73 sets peer eslint ^10.3.
findings.recommendation: State that `xy lint init` is interactive (replace prompt plus one y/N per barrel), so an agent must answer the prompts or run it where a human can. Tell agents to decline the deprecated @xylabs/* and @xyo-network/sdk-js barrels, since accepting installs them at `latest`, which conflicts with SKILL.md:12. Note that @ariestools/sdk barrel restrictions are not generated. Make line 70 match the generator, which always adds configReactStorybook for React (remove it if there are no stories), or say plainly that the generator differs from the README's opt-in stance. Raise the toolchain issue separately.

findings.title: Tier severity description is stale after the unicorn v77 staging in 10.1.0
findings.current: "Tier 3 and 4 additions commonly begin as warnings. Use `pnpm xy lint --strict` … Use tier 4 for evaluation" (eslint.md:96). The table row reads "4 | Experimental/canary rules for migration testing" (eslint.md:94).
findings.truth: Moving from tier 2 to tier 3 turns 38 rules into errors (29 off→error, 9 warn→error) and adds only 22 new warnings. The errors include the unicorn opinionated preset, `@typescript-eslint/strict-boolean-expressions`, `unicorn/filename-case`, and `workspaces/no-relative-imports` / `require-dependency`. Moving from tier 3 to tier 4 adds 68 warnings (unicorn v67/v69/v72) and promotes 22 unicorn v77 rules from warn to their upstream `error`. In 10.1.0 the v77 rules are off at tier 2, warn at tier 3, and error at tier 4.
findings.evidence: Computed with ESLint calculateConfigForFile against eslint-config-flat dist 10.1.0: tier 2→3 {"off->error":29,"warn->error":9,"off->warn":22}; tier 3→4 {"off->warn":68,"warn->error":22}. `unicorn/no-leading-empty-lines` and `unicorn/no-invalid-dom-token` are off/warn/error at tiers 2/3/4. Source: toolchain/packages/eslint-config-flat/src/tiers/tier-builder.ts:87-110; src/tiers/opinionated.ts:72-77 (opinionated preset at 'error'), :134-148 (v77 warn at tier 3, unicornDefaultRules at tier 4); src/unicorn/index.ts:243-277 (v77 queue), :332-338 (default severity = recommended = 'error'). Commit a499070cc (2026-10-06), released in v10.1.0 (tag at 3320116a4).
findings.recommendation: Replace line 96 with an accurate summary. Tier 3 (the default) promotes a set of rules to errors, including strict-boolean-expressions, the opinionated unicorn preset, filename-case and the workspaces rules, and stages the newest unicorn rules (v77) as warnings. Tier 4 adds older queued unicorn rules as warnings and enables v77 rules at upstream error severity, so moving to tier 4 can fail lint without `--strict`. Point to `xy lint --analyze` to preview the impact before changing tier.

findings.title: No list of the high-impact enforced rules agents hit when writing code
findings.current: absent. eslint.md:84-111 describes tiers and plugin families only, and skills/xy-development/typescript.md:5 defers lint-enforced opinions to ESLint.
findings.truth: At the default tier 3 with type checking, these rules are errors: strict-boolean-expressions (nullable string/number/boolean in conditions; this is why toolchain code writes `isVerbose === true`), no-explicit-any, consistent-type-definitions (interface), unicorn/import-style and prefer-node-protocol (`import PATH from 'node:path'`), unicorn/prefer-export-from, `no-restricted-imports` of `./index.ts` barrels and of another package's `src/`, complexity 18, max-depth 6, max-lines 512, max-statements 32, member-ordering (alphabetical), unicorn/filename-case (camel/kebab/pascal), workspaces/no-relative-imports and require-dependency, no-floating-promises, and no-misused-promises. These stay warnings: enum ban via no-restricted-syntax, consistent-type-imports (separate `import type`), simple-import-sort, @stylistic/max-len 200, and explicit-member-accessibility (no-public).

findings.title: Base tsconfig summary omits options that change what code compiles
findings.current: "The base currently supplies strict, ESM-oriented settings including:" … "`isolatedModules`, `erasableSyntaxOnly`" (typescript.md:29-38), with no explanation of what erasableSyntaxOnly rejects.
findings.truth: The base also sets experimentalDecorators: true (legacy decorator semantics, used by the SDK's `staticImplements`), importHelpers: true (tslib becomes an implicit devDependency once decorators are used), esModuleInterop, allowSyntheticDefaultImports, skipLibCheck, removeComments: false and incremental: false, and excludes .github, .vscode, .yarn, dist, node_modules, storybook-static and build. With erasableSyntaxOnly, enums, constructor parameter properties, runtime namespaces and `import x = require()` are TS1294 compile errors.
findings.evidence: toolchain/packages/tsconfig/tsconfig.json:3-28. A scratchpad tsconfig extending the base, run with `tsc` 6.0.3, reports `error TS1294: This syntax is not allowed when 'erasableSyntaxOnly' is enabled` for `enum`, `constructor(private readonly x: number)` and `namespace NS { export const y = 1 }`. toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/deplint/implicitDevDependencies.ts:107-110 (tslib needed when decorators are present). sdk-js/packages/sdk/src/modules/static-implements/staticImplements.ts (legacy decorator).
findings.recommendation: Under 'Understand the base config', state that erasableSyntaxOnly makes enums, parameter properties, runtime namespaces and `import =` compile errors (use const objects or unions and explicit field assignment). Add experimentalDecorators (legacy decorators) together with importHelpers (add `tslib` when decorators are used), and add esModuleInterop and skipLibCheck. Note that a package-level `exclude` replaces the base exclude list.

findings.title: Node types in non-node packages fail publint, but the skill frames it as advice with an escape clause
findings.current: "Keep browser and neutral packages free of Node types unless the source genuinely requires them. The compiler resolves platform-specific types when producing browser, neutral, and node targets." (typescript.md:82)
findings.truth: Compile does strip `node` from `types` for non-node platforms. Separately, `xy publint` (and therefore `xy build`) has a `platform` rule that is error by default. In a package with no node export target, it fails when the root tsconfig `compilerOptions.types` contains "node", when a portable export imports a Node builtin, or when its declarations expose Node ambient types. The 'unless the source genuinely requires them' clause leads to a failing build.
findings.evidence: toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/package/platformPublint.ts:387-397 (collectTsconfigDiagnostics: skipped only when a node target exists), :434-436 (message 'non-node package tsconfig.json should not include compilerOptions.types "node"'), :459-463 (every diagnostic increments errors). src/actions/package/publintRules.ts:51 (`platform` is ERROR_BY_DEFAULT). src/actions/package/compile/resolvePlatformTypes.ts:32-41 (compile-time stripping).
findings.recommendation: Replace line 82: a package without a node export target must not list `node` in `compilerOptions.types`, import `node:*` builtins from portable exports, or leak Node types into declarations, because `xy publint`'s `platform` rule errors on all three. If the source needs Node, add `compile.node: true` / a node export (see compilation.md) instead of adding types. Keep the note that compile strips `node` types per platform.

findings.title: Enum guidance is soft ('prefer') though enums are compiler-rejected, and parameter properties and namespaces are not mentioned
findings.current: "**Prefer union types** over enums: `type Status = 'active' | 'inactive'` rather than `enum Status { Active, Inactive }`" (skills/xy-development/typescript.md:85)
findings.truth: Under the org base tsconfig (erasableSyntaxOnly), enums are a compile error (TS1294) and an ESLint no-restricted-syntax warning. So are constructor parameter properties and runtime namespaces, which the skill never mentions. Workspace policy is 'No enum (use string-literal unions or const objects)'.
findings.evidence: toolchain/packages/tsconfig/tsconfig.json:8. tsc 6.0.3 scratchpad check reports TS1294 on `enum`, `constructor(private readonly x: number)` and `namespace NS {…}`. toolchain/packages/eslint-config-flat/src/typescript/index.ts:161-167 (enum no-restricted-syntax, warn at tiers 1-4 per computed config). CLAUDE.md:45.
findings.recommendation: Reword as a rule: 'Do not use `enum`; use string-literal unions or `as const` objects. Also avoid constructor parameter properties and runtime `namespace`s. Only erasable TypeScript syntax is allowed (toolchain repos enforce this at compile time).'

findings.title: 'Do not annotate return types' contradicts the workspace rule for exported functions
findings.current: "**Do not annotate return types** unless one of these applies: - It's a public API boundary where the contract must be explicit …" (skills/xy-development/typescript.md:23-31)
findings.truth: Workspace conventions require 'Explicit return types on exported functions'. ESLint does not enforce it (explicit-module-boundary-types and explicit-function-return-type are off), so this file, which covers what linters can't catch, is the place for it. Practice follows the workspace rule: about 98% of exported functions in toolchain src are annotated.
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md:43 and AGENTS.md:251 ('Explicit return types on exported functions'). toolchain/packages/eslint-config-flat/src/typescript/index.ts:101 and rule-catalog/managed-rules.ts:54 (explicit-module-boundary-types off). Computed tier-3 config shows explicit-function-return-type off. In toolchain/packages/toolchain/src, 713 `export function` declarations, of which only 16 single-line signatures lack a return type.
findings.recommendation: Rephrase: annotate the return type of every exported function or method; let inference work for local and private helpers and callbacks. For async functions, annotate `Promise<T>`, never `Promise<Promisable<T>>` (CLAUDE.md:46). Keep the type-guard and recursion exceptions.

findings.title: Claims the flat config composes JSON rules; JSON is opt-in, and generated configs ignore Markdown
findings.current: "The non-React config composes TypeScript ESLint, core JavaScript/JSON/Markdown rules, Import X, …" (eslint.md:109)
findings.truth: recommendedConfig() includes markdownConfig at tier 0 but never JSON. jsonConfig, jsoncConfig and json5Config (json/no-duplicate-keys) are only exported and bundled into `docsConfig`, which nothing generates. Separately, `xy lint init` writes `'**/*.md'` into ignores, so generated configs never lint Markdown files.
findings.evidence: toolchain/packages/eslint-config-flat/src/tiers/tier-builder.ts:37-43 (tier 0 = markdownConfig + correctness + typescript, no JSON). src/index.ts:9-14 (docsConfig = markdown + json*). src/json/index.ts:6-28. grep for docsConfig/jsonConfig across packages/*/src finds no consumer. toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/lint-init.ts:129 ('**/*.md' in generated ignores).
findings.recommendation: Say that the preset lints TS/JS (plus Markdown at tier 0), that JSON/JSONC/JSON5 duplicate-key checks are opt-in via `...[jsonConfig, jsoncConfig, json5Config]` (or `docsConfig`, which also re-adds Markdown), and that `lint init` output ignores `**/*.md`.

findings.title: Troubleshooting for type-aware lint on files outside any tsconfig omits the exported gate layer
findings.current: "If type-aware lint is slow or fails on config files, verify the applicable tsconfig before disabling type checking." (eslint.md:132)

The toolchain's own eslint.config.ts uses it, with projectService disabled, for scaffold files excluded from tsconfig. findings.evidence: toolchain/packages/eslint-config-flat/src/index.ts (exports buildTypeCheckGateLayer and RULE_CATALOG). src/tiers/rule-catalog/index.ts:77-82. toolchain/eslint.config.ts:17-28 (files glob + parserOptions projectService:false + `rules: buildTypeCheckGateLayer().rules`). eslint-config-react-flat/src/index.ts:1-2 (no re-export).
findings.recommendation: Add a short example: for files intentionally outside every tsconfig, append `{ files: [...], languageOptions: { parserOptions: { projectService: false, project: false } }, rules: buildTypeCheckGateLayer().rules }` imported from @ariestools/eslint-config-flat. findings.title: CLAUDE.md adapter may be a symlink or absent: both break shipped toolchain lint, and in this workspace an absent CLAUDE.md hides AGENTS.md from Claude Code
findings.current: agents-md.md:110-116 "A symlink works equally well when there is nothing Claude-specific to add: ln -s AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md". templates.md:75-79 repeats the symlink option. auditing.md:32 says the adapter check passes when "CLAUDE.md is an @AGENTS.md import, a symlink, or absent". This contradicts structure.md:7 in the same skill: "CLAUDE.md @AGENTS.md import — required, not optional".
findings.truth: `xy plan lint` (toolchain 10.1.0, experimental) requires CLAUDE.md to be a regular, non-symlink file, and both a symlink and a missing file are errors. docs/repo-docs.md:22 says the bridge is "a real import, not a Markdown link and not a symlink". Claude Code by default reads AGENTS.md only when no CLAUDE.md exists in the working directory or any directory above it. CLAUDE.md sits above every repo here, so a repo with only an AGENTS.md is not loaded. crypto-cards, the repo this skill's examples come from, has no CLAUDE.md today. Claude Code docs also list symlink problems: Edit/Write refuse to write through a symlink, and Git on Windows checks a committed symlink out as plain text unless core.symlinks is set.
findings.evidence: toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/plan/lint.ts:19-25 (REQUIRED_ROOT_PATHS includes CLAUDE.md), :146-156 ("must be a regular, non-symlink file"). rootDocs.ts:35-39 skips symlinked files. toolchain/docs/repo-docs.md:22. Command: `cd XYOracleNetwork/crypto-cards && xyex plan lint --json` returns "plan.root.required-files CLAUDE.md CLAUDE.md is required and must be a regular, non-symlink file". `ls crypto-cards/CLAUDE.md` gives "No such file". https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory, section AGENTS.md: "By default, Claude reads AGENTS.md only when you have no CLAUDE.md in your working directory or above it". Same page, symlink section: Edit/Write refuse to write through a symlink; Windows Git `core.symlinks` caveat.
findings.recommendation: Remove the symlink option from agents-md.md:110-116 and templates.md:75-79. Make the regular-file CLAUDE.md containing `<!-- ... -->` and `@AGENTS.md` the only adapter, matching structure.md:7 and toolchain templates.ts:30-32. Change auditing.md:32 to "CLAUDE.md is a regular file that imports @AGENTS.md (never a copy, symlink, or absent)". Explain why the import stays required: (1) `xy plan lint` requires it, (2) a parent-directory CLAUDE.md (as in this workspace) stops Claude Code from reading AGENTS.md natively, and (3) symlinks break Claude's Edit tool and Windows checkouts.

findings.title: Paper filename convention conflicts with the exact papers/ allowlist in xy plan lint
findings.current: structure.md:50-55: "The house convention is `<PRODUCT>_{WHITE,YELLOW,GREEN,LIGHT}_PAPER.md`" with a Light paper ("Ship a PDF of this one only"). The canonical tree (structure.md:10) shows no papers/README.md.
findings.truth: `xy plan lint` allows only papers/README.md, WHITE-PAPER.md, YELLOW-PAPER.md and an optional GREEN-PAPER.md, case-sensitive and checked recursively. Every other file (a <PRODUCT>_*_PAPER.md, a LIGHT paper, a PDF, papers/archive/*) is an error. `--fix` moves those files into notes/ (flattened, provenance discarded) and creates stub WHITE/YELLOW papers. The light paper exists only as a manifest slot, never as a file in papers/. The toolchain and simple-eula-dapp use WHITE-PAPER.md naming. The XYO paper-first repos the skill was modeled on (crypto-cards, dapp-kit, chain-event-service) use <PRODUCT>_*_PAPER.md and fail the lint.
findings.evidence: toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/plan/lint.ts:27-41 (REQUIRED/OPTIONAL/ALLOWED_PAPER_PATHS), :478-490 ("papers/ permits only README.md, WHITE-PAPER.md, YELLOW-PAPER.md, and optional GREEN-PAPER.md"), :296-314 (relocation into notes/). toolchain/docs/plan-manifest.md:85-94, 113, 118-131. Tracked files: toolchain/papers/{README,WHITE-PAPER,YELLOW-PAPER}.md; XYOracleNetwork/simple-eula-dapp/papers/{WHITE,YELLOW,GREEN}-PAPER.md; crypto-cards/papers/CRYPTO_CARDS_*_PAPER.md. Command: `xyex plan lint --json` in crypto-cards returns 12 errors, including 3 x plan.papers.unexpected-files for CRYPTO_CARDS_{GREEN,WHITE,YELLOW}_PAPER.md.
findings.recommendation: Make papers/README.md, papers/WHITE-PAPER.md and papers/YELLOW-PAPER.md (plus an optional GREEN-PAPER.md) the canonical names, with the roles from plan-manifest.md:118-131. Move the Light paper and any PDF outside papers/ (notes/, or a manifest `light` slot). Add a warning: in a repo that already uses <PRODUCT>_*_PAPER.md, do not run `xy plan lint --fix` unless the owner has agreed to the rename, because the fixer moves the papers into notes/ and creates template stubs.

findings.title: AGENTS.md template fails plan.root.docs-index and differs from the toolchain's AGENTS.md scaffolds

findings.title: Advice to pass an explicit stable work-item id cannot be followed from the CLI
findings.current: auditing.md:102 "Use a deterministic id. createWorkId embeds today's date... Pass an explicit stable id derived from the check and the path, and check existence before adding."
findings.truth: `xy work add` has no --id flag. Its options are description, area, tag, file, line, inline, acceptance, verify, impact, urgency, effort, risk, confidence and the workspace flags. workAdd() accepts `options.id` only as an internal API, and the command handler never passes it, so every CLI-created item gets `<PREFIX>-<YYYYMMDD>-<random>`.
findings.evidence: toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/xy/common/work/addCommand.ts:12-105 (no 'id' option; handler at :85-104 does not pass id). toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/work/index.ts:171 `const id = options.id ?? createWorkId(...)`. id.ts:19-35. Command: `xy.mjs work add --help` lists no --id.
findings.recommendation: Replace the bullet. Since ids cannot be chosen from the CLI, dedupe by content: before adding, search existing items (`xyex work list --json`, or read .xy/work/items/*.json) for a stable key placed in the title or a tag (for example `--tag audit:<check>:<path>`), and update the existing item rather than adding a new one. Add an explicit --id only after the toolchain ships one (track it as a toolchain work item).

findings.title: Tooling status says checks are done by hand, but xy plan lint/init and xy repo lint already automate part of the catalog
findings.current: auditing.md:9 "There is no `xy agent` command yet. The checks below are performed by hand today". auditing.md:11-19 describes a future `xy agent lint|init|audit|index|archive` surface.
findings.truth: Since 2026-09-08 the published toolchain ships the experimental `xy plan lint` (xyex preferred), which enforces: required root AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/CHANGELOG.md/CONTRIBUTING.md/README.md, CLAUDE.md imports @AGENTS.md, no @imports in AGENTS.md, AGENTS.md/README.md link papers/ and docs/, the papers allowlist, docs/README.md + docs/ROADMAP.md, and notes/README.md. The stable `xy repo lint`, which `xy check` runs, enforces repo.package-readme and repo.package-readme-files. `xy plan lint` is not part of `xy check`.
findings.evidence: Command: `xy.mjs --stability --json` lists plan / plan init / plan lint as experimental and repo as stable. `xy.mjs plan lint --rules` lists the 8 plan.* rules. `xy.mjs repo lint --rules` includes repo.package-readme and repo.package-readme-files. toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/xy/common/checkCommand.ts:13, 63-64 (repo lint in check, no plan lint). toolchain/docs/repo-docs.md:33-46. toolchain/docs/plan-manifest.md:74-116. git log: rootDocs.ts and repo-docs.md added eb11282ab on 2026-09-08, after xy-agent's 2026-09-01 release.

Lead with what exists: `pnpm xyex plan lint [--rules|--json|--fix]` for the root/papers/docs/notes layout and adapter contract, and `pnpm xy repo lint` (in `xy check`) for package READMEs. Map each catalog row that tooling covers to its rule id (for example, "Adapters are thin" maps to plan.root.claude-imports-agents). Say that the rest is still manual. Remove the speculative `xy agent` verb list or move it to a note pointing at toolchain item XYW-20260901-263436.

findings.title: Missing rule that AGENTS.md must use Markdown links, never @path imports (plan.root.agents-no-at-imports)
findings.current: absent. agents-md.md:96-120 praises imports ("an import puts the content in context whether it chooses to or not") and never says AGENTS.md itself must not import.
findings.truth: The toolchain makes it an error for AGENTS.md to contain Claude @path imports, because CLAUDE.md imports AGENTS.md and imports are recursive. An @papers/... line would load whole papers into every Claude session. Claude Code expands imports recursively up to four hops, and imported files load at launch.
findings.evidence: toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/plan/rootDocs.ts:66-78, 112-117 (plan.root.agents-no-at-imports, error, not fixable). markdown.ts:15-24. toolchain/docs/repo-docs.md:31 "AGENTS.md must use Markdown links to papers/ and docs/, never @papers/YELLOW-PAPER.md". toolchain/AGENTS.md:18. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory: "Imported files can recursively import other files, with a maximum depth of four hops" and "imported files also load at launch".
findings.recommendation: Under "Per-tool adapters", add: "`@` imports belong only in adapter files (CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md). AGENTS.md refers to papers/ and docs/ with Markdown links and never uses `@path`, since the import is recursive and would load those documents into every session. `xy plan lint` reports this as plan.root.agents-no-at-imports." Add the same row to the auditing.md entry-point table.

findings.title: "Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md, not AGENTS.md" is outdated: Claude Code now reads AGENTS.md natively
findings.current: agents-md.md:100 "Claude Code reads `CLAUDE.md`, not `AGENTS.md`, and supports `@path` imports expanded into context at launch". agents-md.md:124 gives `/context` (Memory files) as the only check.
findings.truth: Claude Code v2.1.277 and later reads AGENTS.md as project instructions when no CLAUDE.md or CLAUDE.local.md exists in the working directory or above it. A `claude-md-and-agents-md` Project instructions setting exists. A CLAUDE.md that imports @AGENTS.md never causes a double load. A natively read AGENTS.md is listed by `/memory` (and by `/context` from v2.1.280). The import is still the right adapter here, for the reasons in the symlink/absent finding.
findings.evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory, section AGENTS.md: "Claude Code can read AGENTS.md as your project instructions, so a repository already set up for other coding agents works without adding a CLAUDE.md"; "Reading AGENTS.md directly requires Claude Code v2.1.277 or later"; "A CLAUDE.md containing @AGENTS.md: you can leave it. Keeping the import never makes Claude read AGENTS.md twice"; "To check whether Claude read your AGENTS.md, run /memory".
findings.recommendation: Rewrite agents-md.md:100 to: "Recent Claude Code can read AGENTS.md directly, but only when no CLAUDE.md exists in the working directory or any parent. In this workspace the parent CLAUDE.md suppresses that, and `xy plan lint` requires a CLAUDE.md, so always keep a regular CLAUDE.md that imports @AGENTS.md." Under "Verifying the adapter loaded", add `/memory` for an AGENTS.md read directly.

findings.title: The toolchain's plan manifest (.xy/plan.json, xy plan init) is not mentioned, though it overlaps the authority table and front matter
findings.current: absent. structure.md:5-27 and agents-md.md:25-37 make the AGENTS.md authority table plus front matter the only authority and lifecycle layer.
findings.truth: The toolchain defines .xy/plan.json (Plan Manifest v1 JSON Schema, shipped in @ariestools/toolchain/schemas) as "the machine-readable entry point for an agent that needs to orient itself". It holds the document catalog with planRole, describes, authorityFor, standing, scope and metadata; the white/yellow/green/light paper slots; the roadmap phase graph with gates and evidence assurance facets; and work-item foreign keys. `xy plan init` (experimental) writes a non-governing `status: bootstrap` manifest. The doc also prescribes a read-only interrogation sequence.
findings.evidence: toolchain/docs/plan-manifest.md:1-7, 17-34 (authority boundaries and single metadata owner), 36-47 (required sections), 50-72 (xy plan init), 287-299 (agent interrogation sequence). toolchain/packages/toolchain/schemas/plan-manifest.v1.schema.json. toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/plan/types.ts:63-89. `xy.mjs --stability --json` lists "plan init" as experimental.
findings.recommendation: Add `.xy/plan.json` to the canonical tree as optional, adopted with `pnpm xyex plan init`, and add a short section that states the division of authority: source and tests for what is implemented, a reviewed .xy/plan.json for strategy, xy work for tasks, and Markdown for long-form contracts. In agents-md.md "Orient before acting", say that when a reviewed .xy/plan.json exists the AGENTS.md authority table should summarize it rather than compete with it, and that a `status: bootstrap` manifest is never authority.

findings.title: Canonical tree omits files the toolchain requires (docs/ROADMAP.md, notes/, papers/README.md, CHANGELOG.md, CONTRIBUTING.md)

Other docs/ content, including lifecycle subfolders, is allowed and not linted.

State that the docs/ lifecycle subfolders sit alongside the files `xy plan lint` requires and are not checked by it.

findings.title: Rule that every document carries front matter, and its state vocabulary, conflict with the toolchain's single-owner metadata model
findings.current: lifecycle.md:3 "Every document under docs/, papers/, and specs/ carries YAML front matter." lifecycle.md:7-35 lists `state: draft|active|normative|superseded|retired`.
findings.truth: The plan manifest requires exactly one owner for lifecycle metadata: `metadata.source: manifest` (the documented norm for existing repos, "Use inline manifest metadata until front matter is adopted; never maintain both") or `front-matter`. The manifest separates `lifecycle` (accepted|active|archived|deprecated|draft|proposed|superseded) from `authorityLevel` (descriptive|evidentiary|informative|normative). xy-agent's `state` mixes the two by treating `normative` as a state. No toolchain doc or paper carries YAML front matter. The papers use a visible header, and plan-lint paper templates use a `## Status` section.
findings.evidence: toolchain/docs/plan-manifest.md:29-34. plan-manifest.v1.schema.json $defs.documentMetadata (oneOf manifest | front-matter; lifecycle and authorityLevel enums; description "never maintain both"). `head -1` of toolchain/docs/*.md and papers/*.md shows a Markdown H1 with no `---`. toolchain/papers/YELLOW-PAPER.md:3-5 header block. toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/plan/templates.ts:100-147.
findings.recommendation: Make front matter conditional: use it only where the repository has chosen front matter as the metadata owner (manifest `metadata.source: front-matter`), and never duplicate lifecycle, review date or supersession in both places. Align the vocabulary with the shipped schema. Either rename `state` to `lifecycle` with the schema's values and add `authorityLevel` (normative/informative/descriptive/evidentiary), or document an explicit mapping (normative → lifecycle accepted + authorityLevel normative; retired → archived/deprecated).

findings.title: Nested packages/<pkg>/AGENTS.md guidance contradicts the toolchain contract, actual practice, and how the tools load files
findings.current: agents-md.md:91 "Package-specific instructions → packages/<pkg>/AGENTS.md, which loads on demand". agents-md.md:130-136 (Nested files). structure.md:24 `packages/<pkg>/AGENTS.md delta only`. auditing.md:39 has a nested-delta check.
findings.truth: toolchain/docs/repo-docs.md:16 says "Keep agent instructions at the repository root. Do not add AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md inside packages.", and package READMEs are the consumer docs. No ariestools repo tracks a nested AGENTS.md. With the root CLAUDE.md that this skill requires, Claude Code's default mode reads no AGENTS.md at all, so a lone packages/x/AGENTS.md is never loaded (it does not "load on demand"). Codex only concatenates AGENTS.md files from the project root down to the working directory, not files below it, and caps the combined size at 32 KiB (project_doc_max_bytes).
findings.evidence: toolchain/docs/repo-docs.md:16. `git ls-files | grep AGENTS.md` across toolchain, cli-kit, sdk-js, actor-kit, browser-kit, sdk-react and ariestools-skills finds only root files. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory: AGENTS.md is read "only when you have no CLAUDE.md in your working directory or above it"; a subdirectory AGENTS.md loads only when that subdirectory "has none of the three CLAUDE.md files" and AGENTS.md mode is active. https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/agents-md: "Starting at the project root... Codex walks down to your current working directory"; "stops adding files once the combined size reaches... project_doc_max_bytes" (default 32 KiB).
findings.recommendation: For ariestools monorepos, follow the toolchain: no AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md inside packages. Put consumer docs in packages/*/README.md and path-specific agent rules in .claude/rules/ (plus .github/instructions/*.instructions.md for Copilot). If a non-toolchain repo really needs a nested file, say it must be a nested CLAUDE.md importing the nested AGENTS.md for Claude to load it, and that Codex sees it only when started inside that package. Remove "which loads on demand" (line 91) and downgrade the nested row in auditing.md:39.

findings.title: Copilot adapter template is the prose pointer the skill itself rejects, and Copilot already reads AGENTS.md natively
findings.current: templates.md:81-91: `.github/copilot-instructions.md` says "Repository guidance lives in [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md). Read it first." agents-md.md:118 says "A prose pointer is not good enough". agents-md.md:120 treats copilot-instructions.md and GEMINI.md as additions-only adapters without saying how they pick up AGENTS.md.
findings.truth: GitHub Copilot reads AGENTS.md files anywhere in the repo (nearest wins) and also supports path-specific `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md` with `applyTo` globs. All relevant instruction sets are provided together, so a copilot-instructions.md is only needed for Copilot-only additions, and a pointer adds nothing. Gemini CLI GEMINI.md supports `@file` imports, and `context.fileName` in settings.json can list AGENTS.md.
findings.evidence: https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/configure-custom-instructions/add-repository-instructions: "You can create one or more AGENTS.md files, stored anywhere within the repository... the nearest AGENTS.md file in the directory tree will take precedence"; path-specific files use `applyTo`; "all sets of relevant instructions are provided to Copilot". https://geminicli.com/docs/cli/gemini-md/: `context.fileName` may list ["AGENTS.md", ...]; GEMINI.md supports `@./path.md` imports.
findings.recommendation: Replace the Copilot template with: "Copilot reads AGENTS.md natively. Create .github/copilot-instructions.md only for Copilot-specific additions, and never restate or point at AGENTS.md." Mention `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md` (`applyTo:`) as the Copilot counterpart of .claude/rules/. For Gemini, give `@AGENTS.md` in GEMINI.md (or `context.fileName`) as the adapter.

findings.title: Orient step `pnpm xy work list` is experimental and writes files in repos that have no work store
findings.current: templates.md:21-23 makes "3. `pnpm xy work list` — the open work items." part of the read-only orientation sequence.
findings.truth: `work` is classified experimental (`xyex` preferred). `xy work list` calls readWorkConfig(), which calls ensureWorkStore(), which creates .xy/work/, the items and queues folders, and a default config.json with `stores.github.enabled: true` when they are missing. The toolchain's plan-manifest doc says side-effect-free interrogation "must not call the current xy work show or xy work list paths".
findings.evidence: Command: `xy.mjs --stability --json` lists {"name":"work","stability":"experimental"}. toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/work/list.ts:90. store.ts:55-71 (mkdirSync, then writeJson of defaultWorkConfig). schema.ts:82-85 (github enabled: true by default). toolchain/docs/plan-manifest.md:285 and 296.
findings.recommendation: Make the step conditional and side-effect free, for example: "3. If `.xy/work/config.json` is tracked, `pnpm xyex work list` — the open work items." Or point at .xy/work/items/ directly. Add a note that `xy work list` and `xy work show` initialize a missing store.

findings.title: Hand-run audit scripts miss Markdown links and top-level docs, giving false negatives and false positives
findings.current: auditing.md:58-60: the link check greps only backtick code spans (`` `...\.(md|json|ts...)` ``). auditing.md:76-79: the orphan scan iterates `git ls-files 'docs/**/*.md'`.
findings.truth: (1) The link check ignores Markdown links, which are exactly what the toolchain convention requires (plan.root.docs-index). It also resolves package-relative prose paths against the repo root, producing false MISSING results. (2) Without `:(glob)` magic, git pathspec `docs/**/*.md` needs an extra path segment and silently skips every top-level docs/*.md file.
findings.evidence: Command in toolchain: the code-span grep finds only CLAUDE.md, packages/toolchain/src/bin/xy.ts, packages/toolchain/src/xy/stability.ts and src/bin/xyex.ts, and reports "MISSING src/bin/xyex.ts" (a false positive: the path is relative to packages/toolchain). All 9 Markdown link targets in toolchain/AGENTS.md (./docs/README.md, ./papers/YELLOW-PAPER.md, ...) go unchecked. `git -C toolchain ls-files 'docs/**/*.md'` returns 0 files, while `':(glob)docs/**/*.md'` returns docs/README.md, docs/ROADMAP.md and the rest. In crypto-cards, `'docs/**/*.md'` returns 331 files against 560 with `:(glob)`.
findings.recommendation: Add a Markdown-link extractor to the link check, for example `grep -oE '\]\(([^)#]+)' AGENTS.md | sed -E 's/^\]\(//; s#^\./##'`, resolved relative to the file, and keep the code-span check as secondary. Change the orphan scan to `git ls-files ':(glob)docs/**/*.md'` (or `'docs/*.md'`, since a default-pathspec `*` already crosses `/`).

findings.title: Entry-point checks at error and warn level fail every AGENTS.md the toolchain generates and every ariestools repo
findings.current: auditing.md:33 "H1 names the product, not the filename | warn". auditing.md:34 "Required sections present | error | Orient, authority table, repository map, commands, failures". agents-md.md:138-142 says the title convention "is not cosmetic".
findings.truth: Both toolchain scaffolds produce AGENTS.md without these H1s or sections. `xy repo init` writes `# AGENTS.md` with Documentation/Overview/Commands/Architecture. The `xy plan lint --fix` template writes `# Agent Instructions` with Documentation/Repository guidance/Verification. Every ariestools repo that has an AGENTS.md (toolchain, sdk-js, sdk-react, ariestools-skills) uses `# AGENTS.md` and none has the five required sections. cli-kit, actor-kit and browser-kit have no AGENTS.md at all. SKILL.md:18 calls the pattern "recommended, not required", which conflicts with error-level checks.
findings.evidence: toolchain/packages/toolchain/templates/repo/cli/root/AGENTS.md.tmpl:1-39. toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/plan/templates.ts:2-22. `head -1` gives `# AGENTS.md` for toolchain/AGENTS.md:1, sdk-js/AGENTS.md:1, sdk-react/AGENTS.md:1 and ariestools-skills/AGENTS.md:1. `git ls-files` in cli-kit, actor-kit and browser-kit shows no AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md.
findings.recommendation: Lower "Required sections" to warn and define it against the toolchain scaffold: a Documentation link section (enforced by plan.root.docs-index) plus commands and constraints, with Orient, authority table, map and What NOT to do as recommended additions. Either drop the H1 rule's "not cosmetic" rationale (an imported file's H1 is harmless) or record a toolchain work item to change the H1 in AGENTS.md.tmpl and templates.ts so tooling and skill agree. Until then, tell agents to retitle after scaffolding.

findings.title: Toolchain skills tooling does not know about xy-agent: never installed, mis-sourced, and Layer 1 links to it are dead in every consumer
findings.current: defaults.ts:13-17 ARIESTOOLS_SKILLS = ['ariestools-sdk','xy-development','xy-toolchain']. skills/xy-development/SKILL.md:33 and workflow.md:47 link to `../xy-agent/SKILL.md`.
findings.truth: skillSourceForName('xy-agent') falls through to XYOracleNetwork/xyo-skills (defaults.ts:84-86), so a version check or reinstall would look in the wrong repo. isXyoSkillName() excludes xy-agent, so `xy skills lint` never checks it. None of the six ariestools consumer repos lists xy-agent in skills-lock.json, so the installed xy-development links to `../xy-agent/SKILL.md` point at a missing directory. Example: toolchain/.agents/skills contains only xy-development, xy-toolchain and xy-work.
findings.evidence: toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/skills/defaults.ts:13-17, 84-86. versions.ts:9 (version URL built from skillSourceForName). skillRules.ts:24, 126-128. skills-lock.json in toolchain, cli-kit, sdk-js, actor-kit, browser-kit and sdk-react lists only ariestools-sdk, xy-development and xy-toolchain. toolchain/.agents/skills/xy-development/SKILL.md:33 links ../xy-agent/SKILL.md, which is absent. toolchain/.xy/work/items/XYW-20260901-263436.json notes "The skill also needs registering in src/actions/skills/defaults.ts (ARIESTOOLS_SKILLS) plus an optional-skills list".
findings.recommendation: In the toolchain, add 'xy-agent' to ARIESTOOLS_SKILLS (so it is sourced from ariestools/ariestools-skills) and to an optional-skills list for all tiers. In this repo, make the xy-development references degrade gracefully: name the skill and its install command (`pnpm xy skills add ariestools/ariestools-skills --skill xy-agent`) next to the relative link, so a consumer without it is not left with a dead link.

findings.title: xy-toolchain does not document `xy plan init` / `xy plan lint`, which xy-agent needs to defer to
findings.current: absent. A grep for 'plan' in skills/xy-toolchain/commands.md finds nothing. xy-agent SKILL.md:45 sends readers to xy-toolchain for the xy CLI.

findings.title: Moving AGENTS.md overflow into .claude/rules/ makes it Claude-only, contradicting "AGENTS.md is canonical"
findings.current: agents-md.md:88-94 tells agents to move over-budget content to ".claude/rules/*.md with paths: frontmatter". The 200-line budget (agents-md.md:84-86) is framed only in Claude terms.
findings.truth: Codex and Copilot do not read .claude/rules/. Copilot's equivalent is .github/instructions/*.instructions.md with `applyTo`. Codex has no path-scoped mechanism and caps combined AGENTS.md content at 32 KiB. The Claude claims themselves check out: target under 200 lines, path rules load on Read/Write/Edit of matching files, and block HTML comments are stripped.
findings.evidence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory: "target under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md file"; "Path-scoped rules trigger when Claude uses the Read, Write, or Edit tool on a file matching the pattern"; "Block-level HTML comments... are stripped". https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/configure-custom-instructions/add-repository-instructions (applyTo). https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/agents-md (project_doc_max_bytes, 32 KiB default).
findings.recommendation: Add a caveat: content moved to .claude/rules/ is invisible to other agents. Keep cross-tool rules in AGENTS.md or a Markdown-linked doc, and mirror path-scoped rules as .github/instructions/*.instructions.md when Copilot matters. Mention Codex's 32 KiB combined cap alongside the 200-line budget.

findings.title: Evidence naming covers only single dated .md files, but practice pairs Markdown with JSON reports or uses evidence directories
findings.current: lifecycle.md:60 and structure.md:18 "Name it `docs/evidence/YYYY-MM-DD-slug.md`". auditing.md:49 checks immutability only for `docs/evidence/` .md files.

findings.title: Install command pulls TypeScript 7, which the toolchain does not support
findings.current: toolchain.md:41-45 "requires Node.js 22 or newer and TypeScript 5.9 or 6:" followed by `pnpm add -D @ariestools/toolchain @ariestools/tsconfig typescript` (no version on typescript)
findings.truth: `typescript@latest` on npm is now 7.0.2, the Go native compiler, which exports no compiler API. @ariestools/toolchain peers on `typescript: ^5.9 || ^6.0`, and ESLint, deplint, dead and api-exposure all load the API from `typescript`. The toolchain's own scaffold pins `typescript: ~6.0.3`, and `xy updo` will not offer a 6→7 bump. TS7 is supported only side by side, as `typescript-native: npm:typescript@~7.0.2` plus `compile.compiler: 'native'` (`xyex enable ts-native`, experimental).
findings.evidence: `npm view typescript dist-tags` → latest "7.0.2". toolchain/packages/toolchain/package.json peerDependencies typescript "^5.9 || ^6.0". toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/lib/updo/majorCeiling.ts:16-28 (maxMajor 6: "typescript@7 is the native compiler and exports no compiler API — ESLint, deplint, dead-code and api-exposure all load it from `typescript`"). Commit c2b9db449 (2026-08-10, v9.0.0). toolchain/packages/toolchain/templates/repo/cli/root/package.json.tmpl:48 "typescript": "~6.0.3". toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/enable/tsNative.ts:144-147.
findings.recommendation: Change the install line to `pnpm add -D @ariestools/toolchain @ariestools/tsconfig typescript@~6.0.3` (or `typescript@^6`). Add one sentence: do not upgrade to typescript@7; it is a different distribution with no API. Use `xy updo`, which caps typescript at 6. TS7 is only an experimental side-by-side alias via `xyex enable ts-native`.

findings.title: tsconfig install snippets install TypeScript 7 (npm latest)
findings.current: typescript.md:14-23 three `pnpm add -D ... typescript` commands with no version; typescript.md:25 "Use TypeScript 5.9 or 6 with the current toolchain."
findings.truth: With an unversioned `typescript`, pnpm now resolves 7.0.2, the native Go compiler with no API, which violates the toolchain peer `^5.9 || ^6.0`. The version sentence is correct, but the commands right above it contradict it.
findings.evidence: `npm view typescript dist-tags` → latest 7.0.2. toolchain/packages/toolchain/package.json peer typescript "^5.9 || ^6.0"; toolchain/packages/tsconfig/package.json:45 devDependency typescript "~6.0.3"; toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/lib/updo/majorCeiling.ts:16-28.
findings.recommendation: Use `typescript@~6.0.3` (or `typescript@^6`) in all three snippets. In the version paragraph, add that typescript@7 must not replace 6, with a pointer to the experimental `compile.compiler: 'native'` / `xyex enable ts-native` side-by-side install.

findings.title: No xy vs xyex channel or stability contract (explicit SKILLS-FOLLOWUP ask)
findings.current: absent. `grep -rn xyex skills/` returns nothing. commands.md:13-29 'Global behavior' lists flags but no `--stability` and no `xyex` binary.
findings.truth: Since 9.2.0 (2026-09-01) the toolchain ships two bins. `xy` is semver-stable. `xyex` is the experimental superset and may change on a minor. Experimental commands still run under `xy` but print "Experimental: ... Prefer xyex ...", and a future major will make that a hard error. `xy --stability [--json]` lists command, package and experimental-config stability. Experimental commands are dead, work, plan, npm-org, enable, orphan, tsc-validate, sonar, analyze, eject and sitemap; relint is deprecated. Experimental config is compile.validator 'shared', compile.compiler 'native', compile.mode 'tsc', ESLint tier 4, lint --mode shared-typecheck, and non-pnpm package managers.
findings.evidence: toolchain/docs/SKILLS-FOLLOWUP.md:5-7 ("Document `xy` vs `xyex` in skills/xy-toolchain/commands.md and the SKILL.md router", "Point agents at docs/STABILITY.md", "Prefer `xy` in examples unless the task requires an experimental command"). toolchain/docs/STABILITY.md:9-14, 55-62, 90-102. toolchain/docs/ROADMAP.md:52 (D2 hard-error next major), 194 and 212 (Phase 4 "Blocks: ... skills must mention xyex first"). `node packages/toolchain/dist/bin/xy.mjs --stability` output (10.1.0).
findings.recommendation: Add an 'xy vs xyex' subsection under Global behavior: the two bins, the semver contract, the warn-now/error-next-major migration window, `pnpm xy --stability --json` as the source of truth, and a link to https://github.com/ariestools/toolchain/blob/main/docs/STABILITY.md. Prefer `xy` in examples. Use `xyex` only for commands the catalog marks experimental. Add `--stability` to the global flag table.

findings.title: Router and description do not mention xyex, stability, or experimental status
findings.current: SKILL.md:3 description and SKILL.md:32-34 'Command and policy catalog' router list `work`, `dead`, and others as ordinary commands. No mention of `xyex` or STABILITY.
findings.truth: SKILLS-FOLLOWUP item 1 asks for the router to cover xy vs xyex. `work` and `dead` are experimental and print an xyex warning on every leaf invocation (nested leaves since 10.1.0). The STABILITY promotion rubric also requires experimental commands' flags and config to be documented in xy-toolchain skills before promotion.

Prefer "xyex work list"'.
findings.recommendation: Add one router line, e.g. "Read commands.md#xy-vs-xyex before running any command marked experimental (work, dead, plan, npm-org, tsc-validate, enable, orphan)." Add 'xy/xyex stability channels' to the description keywords.

findings.title: Experimental commands shown as plain `pnpm xy …` invocations

findings.title: @ariestools/vitest-config defaults and single-package guidance are stale (10.1.0)
findings.current: testing.md:73 "Default include: `packages/*/src/**/spec/**/*.spec.ts`."; testing.md:77 same in the options table; testing.md:98 "keep a hand-rolled config when the package is a single-package repo"; testing.md:27-30 gives no vitest version.
findings.truth: In 10.1.0, XY_VITEST_DEFAULT_INCLUDE is ['packages/*/src/**/spec/**/*.spec.{ts,tsx,mts,cts}', 'packages/*/spec/**/*.spec.{ts,tsx,mts,cts}'] (package-root spec/ now included). Both realms also exclude **/node_modules/** and **/.claude/**. The peer is `vitest ^5.0`. Per decision D8, a single-package repo uses the preset with an explicit `include`; `xy repo init --no-monorepo` emits defineXyVitestConfig({ include: ['src/**/spec/**/*.spec.{ts,tsx,mts,cts}'] }).

Commit e7ea93749 (code-review items 12-13) → v10.1.0.

Replace the single-package guidance with `defineXyVitestConfig({ include: ['src/**/spec/**/*.spec.{ts,tsx,mts,cts}'] })`, keeping hand-rolled config only for deliberate divergence.

findings.title: Monolith identity invariant, platform config and declaration sharing (10.0.9) missing
findings.current: compilation.md:95-110 covers modules, platforms, moduleLinkage 'external', export/model/subpaths/internal/reexport, copyEntries, and package-sync-layout only.
findings.truth: Under external linkage, `#<module>` and `./<module>` must load the same file in every environment. A real platform variant is declared on both sides, as `conditionalImports.<module>` and `platformEntries.<platform>.<module>`. Layout sync (in `xy compile` and `package-sync-layout`) warns about platformEntries shims that re-export the modules-platform source (a byte-identical second build), about shims `#module` does not select, and about `#module` imports that disagree with exports. Since 10.0.9, platform trees drop declarations identical to the modules-platform copy and import the shared one. MonolithConfig also has modulesPlatform, barrelPlatforms, aliasImports and index.entries.
findings.evidence: toolchain/CHANGELOG.md:21, 27 (Unreleased section, shipped in v10.0.9: commits 92cf6bce9, 6e056462a, d0f17a92d). toolchain/papers/YELLOW-PAPER.md (§6.3 identity invariant added in d0f17a92d). toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/package/compile/MonolithConfig.ts:124-187.
findings.recommendation: Add an 'Identity invariant' paragraph to Monolith mode: declare platform variants via conditionalImports plus platformEntries, never as a modules-platform forwarding shim. Treat layout-sync warnings and pub.importsMatchExports errors as identity splits. Declarations are shared across platforms, so do not hand-copy .d.ts files.

findings.title: Publint description missing pub.importsMatchExports and new --fix behavior
findings.current: commands.md:131 "Validate the npm package surface, including upstream publint checks, compiled output/export-map parity, platform portability, export condition order, published files, source leakage, side effects, root legacy fields, and workspace peer ranges."
findings.truth: 10.0.9 added `pub.importsMatchExports` (error by default, not fixable): every exact runtime `#alias` in `imports` must select the same file as its same-named public subpath under every condition. Export-map `--fix` no longer adds a condition the same-named `#alias` does not select, and inserts platform conditions before `default`. `pub.platform` now checks every monolith compile output against exports.
findings.evidence: `xy.mjs publint --rules` lists `error │ pub.importsMatchExports │ no`. toolchain/CHANGELOG.md:20, 25-26. Commits af6712ba5 and 26db53993 → v10.0.9.
findings.recommendation: Add `#imports` aliases vs same-named exports (`pub.importsMatchExports`, not auto-fixable) to the list. Note that `--fix` refuses to add a condition its `#alias` does not select. Point to compilation.md#monolith-mode for the identity invariant.

findings.title: Deplint not-public rules (error) missing
findings.current: commands.md:48 "Detect unlisted, unused, misplaced, redundant, unsatisfied, range-style, and workspace-protocol problems."
findings.truth: Since 10.0.3, `dep.dependencies.not-public` and `dep.peerDependencies.not-public` default to error and are not auto-fixable: a public package must not list a non-public npmjs package in dependencies or peers. `xy build` runs deplint, so this breaks builds.
findings.evidence: `xy.mjs deplint --rules` shows both rules at error with Fix 'no'. toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/deplint/rules.md:3. Commit 2f9db7e4e (2026-09-07) → v10.0.3.
findings.recommendation: Add 'non-public dependencies of public packages (`*.not-public`, error, manual fix: publish the dep, vendor it, or make the package private)' to the deplint detection list.

findings.title: repo lint / node lint rows omit README, engines/volta, and nodeTrack policy
findings.current: commands.md:160 `xy repo lint` → "Workspace structure, versions, engines, package-manager fields, spec layout, and Dependabot enablement"; commands.md:161 `xy node lint` → "Root Volta pin and package `engines.node` portability"
findings.truth:
`xy check` runs repo lint, and these rules default to error:
- repo.package-readme and repo.package-readme-files (10.0.5): every workspace package except the root needs a consumer README.md, and publishable packages list README.md in `files`.
- repo.engines-non-terminal: the root and private packages must not declare engines (use volta); libraries must.
- repo.engines-lts: engines ranges must include the latest Node.
- repo.volta-only-root, repo.root-private, repo.packages-folder, repo.pnpm-minimum-release-age and repo.pnpm-release-age-excludes.
Since 10.0.7, `commands.repoLint.nodeTrack` and `commands.nodeLint.nodeTrack` ('current' | 'lts') select the Node track.
findings.evidence: `xy.mjs repo lint --rules` and `xy.mjs node lint --rules` (10.1.0). toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/package-lint-engines.ts:65-94, 176-223. toolchain/docs/xy-config.md:47-56. toolchain/docs/repo-docs.md:41-46. Commits eb11282ab → v10.0.5 and a2b5c6ea3 → v10.0.7.
findings.recommendation: Expand both rows, or add a short repo-policy subsection listing these rule families. Document `nodeTrack: 'lts'` for LTS-pinned repos. Tell agents that a new workspace package needs a README.md and that `xy repo lint --fix` scaffolds one.

findings.title: New-project baseline misses the policy gates `xy check` enforces
findings.current: toolchain.md:110-124: 'Require Node.js 22 or newer', install packages, `type: module`, configs, `xy lint init`; toolchain.md:124 'Use `xy repo init cli` only after inspecting its generated output and passing an explicit scope.'; toolchain.md:96-104 root scripts use `"test": "vitest run"`.
findings.truth:
A baseline that passes `xy check` also needs:
- Node via root `volta` only, with no `engines` on the root or private packages, and libraries declaring an open range such as `>=22` that includes current Node (26.x). A capped range like `^22` is an error.
- root `private: true`.
- pnpm `minimumReleaseAge`, `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` and `verifyDepsBeforeRun` (packman lint, error).
- a README.md in every package.
- `.xy/cache` ignored in every package.
Since 9.2.0, `xy repo init` is interactive when the template is omitted, defaults to scope @ariestools, MIT and pnpm, and takes --pm, --monorepo, --react, --skills-tier and -y. Its root scripts are build, compile, lint, fix, test and check, all via xy ("test": "xy test").
findings.evidence: `xy.mjs repo lint --rules`, `xy.mjs packman lint --rules`, `xy.mjs git lint --rules` (git.ignore-toolchain-cache). toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/package-lint-engines.ts:71-87, 194-202. toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/lib/latestVersions (nodeCurrent 26.8.2). `xy.mjs repo init --help`. toolchain/packages/toolchain/templates/repo/cli/root/package.json.tmpl scripts block. toolchain/CHANGELOG.md:58.
findings.recommendation: Add these items to the baseline checklist and end it with `pnpm xy check --fix`, then `pnpm xy check`. Update the repo-init sentence with the real defaults and flags (still inspect the output). Align the root-scripts example with the scaffold (`test: xy test`, plus `fix` and `check`).

findings.title: packman row does not separate stable lint from experimental convert/clean (SKILLS-FOLLOWUP #5)
findings.current: commands.md:159 `xy packman lint` → "Package-manager safety configuration, including pnpm release-age policy"
findings.truth: `xy packman lint` is stable and part of `xy check`. Its rules are packman.pnpm.minimumReleaseAge, packman.pnpm.minimumReleaseAgeExclude, packman.pnpm.verifyDepsBeforeRun and packman.yarn.enableScripts, all errors. `packman convert <target>` and `packman clean` are experimental (xyex).
findings.evidence: toolchain/docs/SKILLS-FOLLOWUP.md:9. toolchain/docs/STABILITY.md:80-88. `xy.mjs packman --help` and `xy.mjs packman lint --rules`. toolchain/CHANGELOG.md:59.
findings.recommendation: State that packman lint is stable and in `xy check`, and list its four rules. Mention `xyex packman convert pnpm` (experimental) as the yarn/npm→pnpm migration aid, and that `packman clean` is not a build-artifact cleaner (use `xy clean`).

findings.title: Skills section omits defaults, tier detection, xy.skills, and additionalSkills
findings.current: commands.md:169-171 "`xy skills` wraps the bundled Skills.sh CLI ... Use `xy skills lint --fix` to install missing profile-required skills; use `--offline` ..."
findings.truth: `xy skills defaults` installs all of ariestools/ariestools-skills plus the xyo-skills stack. `xy skills lint` detects tier xy/xyo/xl1. It requires ariestools-sdk when sdk-js packages are used, and xl1-dapp-kit for @xyo-network/dapp-kit (10.0.8). It also requires skills declared in package.json `xy.skills` on workspace packages and direct dependencies (skills.package-recommended, 10.0.8), and honors `commands.skillsLint.additionalSkills`. Rules: skills.required-installed, required-current, migrated-source, package-recommended, unnecessary and duplicate-install. `--fix` installs missing skills, migrates xyo-skills-locked xy-development and xy-toolchain, and updates outdated ones.

findings.title: Release commands (deploy, publish --tag) are not documented

STABILITY: prereleases publish with an explicit dist-tag (`pnpm xy publish --tag next`); keep `latest` for intentional stable cuts. A same-named package.json script runs instead of the command unless `--no-defer` is passed (code-review item 20).

findings.title: xy work flags, lint rules, and the 10.1.0 sync identity check are undocumented
findings.current: commands.md:177-201 lists subcommands only. No `work add` flags, no `work lint` rule ids, and no sync safety note.
findings.truth: `work add` takes --description, --area, --tag (repeatable), --file/--line/--inline, --acceptance (repeatable), --verify (repeatable), and --impact/--urgency/--effort/--risk/--confidence (1-5), plus --workspace/--workspace-file/--repo. `work lint` rules are work.store-not-gitignored (error), work.github-available (warn) and work.github-synced (warn). Since 10.1.0, sync edits or closes a GitHub issue only when the body marker matches the local id and the stored URL matches. The STABILITY promotion rubric requires these flags to be documented in xy-toolchain. xy-agent auditing.md:104 already tells agents to supply area, priority, acceptance and verification, which they cannot do from this skill.
findings.evidence: `xyex.mjs work add --help`; `xyex.mjs work lint --rules`. toolchain/docs/code-review-2026-10-06.md:76-83 (item 8, fixed in e7ea93749 → v10.1.0). toolchain/docs/STABILITY.md:113. toolchain/.agents/skills/xy-work/SKILL.md:24-55, 112-136 (unpublished, more complete copy).
findings.recommendation: Add a 'Capture and triage' example (`pnpm xyex work add bug "…" --area … --acceptance … --verify … --impact 4 --urgency 2 --effort 1 --risk 2 --confidence 3`), the work lint rule table, the under-triaged definition, and the sync identity guarantee. Port this from the toolchain's local xy-work skill.

findings.title: Experimental compile surfaces: 'tsc' mode now errors; native compiler and tsc-validate missing
findings.current: compilation.md:78 "`mode: 'tsc'` is reserved in the public type but is not wired into `packageCompile`."; compilation.md:89-91 list validator per-package/shared and `xy compile --validator shared` without experimental labeling; no `compile.compiler`.
findings.truth: Since 9.2.0, `compile.mode: 'tsc'` errors instead of silently using esbuild. `compile.compiler: 'native'` (TS7, via `xyex enable ts-native`) is experimental and incompatible with `compile.validator: 'shared'`, which is itself experimental (same engine as `xyex tsc-validate`).
findings.evidence: toolchain/CHANGELOG.md:60. toolchain/docs/xy-config.md:33-39. `xy.mjs --stability` 'Experimental config' (compile.validator.shared, compile.mode.tsc, compile.compiler.native). Commit c2b9db449 → v9.0.0.
findings.recommendation: Say `mode: 'tsc'` fails at compile time. Mark the shared validator as experimental. Add a one-line experimental note for `compile.compiler: 'native'` and `xyex tsc-validate`, including the incompatibility, and say public examples must not require them (ROADMAP D4).

findings.title: Lint modes, worker memory budget, and xy cycle not covered
findings.current: eslint.md:113-132 command table and troubleshooting mention performance but not `--mode`, `--meta`, `XY_LINT_WORKER_MAX_RSS_MB`, or `xy cycle`.
findings.truth: `xy lint --mode package-workers|shared-typecheck|workspace-eslint`: default package-workers; shared-typecheck is experimental (9.0.3). `--meta full|skip` covers root/meta packages. Since 10.0.8, lint workers are recycled past an RSS budget (default 2048 MiB, set with XY_LINT_WORKER_MAX_RSS_MB). `xy cycle [package] --depth` runs import-cycle checking.
findings.evidence: `xy.mjs lint --help`; toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/lintMode.ts:1-9; commit bc8e52802 message (XY_LINT_WORKER_MAX_RSS_MB) → v10.0.8; `xy.mjs cycle --help`; `xy.mjs --stability` (lint.mode.shared-typecheck experimental).
findings.recommendation: Add `--mode` (marking shared-typecheck experimental), `--meta`, `xy cycle`, and the RSS budget variable to the commands table and troubleshooting paragraph.

findings.title: git lint toolchain-cache rule and remaining maintenance/experimental commands unlisted

findings.title: Migration section omits the documented manual boundary and packman convert

findings.title: package-* hooks presented without their non-stable status
findings.current: toolchain.md:68-90 hook table and `-only` guidance; compilation.md:103-108 recommends `package-sync-layout --check`.
findings.truth: STABILITY classes `package-*` bin scripts as implementation details of `xy`, not semver-stable, and prefers the `xy` CLI in docs and automation. Since 10.1.0, run-or-exec bypasses `pnpm run` for identity scripts (`"package-compile": "package-compile"`) so `--emit-only` is preserved.

findings.title: 'Always pnpm add latest' now installs typescript@7 and breaks xy repos
findings.current: workflow.md:35 "when adding new dependencies, always use `pnpm add <package>` ... to resolve the latest published version ... If a specific version is required for peer dependency compatibility, pin to that version explicitly"
findings.truth: For `typescript`, latest is 7.0.2 (native Go compiler, no API), outside the toolchain peer `^5.9 || ^6.0`. In xy repos, pnpm `minimumReleaseAge` (enforced by packman lint) also means 'latest' resolves to the newest version old enough. Deplint enforces full-patch tilde ranges (`~x.y.z`) via dep.*.range-style.
findings.evidence: `npm view typescript dist-tags` (latest 7.0.2). toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/lib/updo/majorCeiling.ts:16-28. `xy.mjs packman lint --rules` (packman.pnpm.minimumReleaseAge error). `xy.mjs deplint --rules` (dep.dependencies.range-style: "full-patch tilde form").
findings.recommendation: Add a caveat: check toolchain peer ranges before taking latest. TypeScript stays on 6.x for @ariestools/toolchain; see the xy-toolchain skill. In xy repos, prefer `pnpm xy updo` for upgrades and let `xy deplint --fix` normalize range style.

findings.title: Workspace-scoped command advice fails in xy monorepos
findings.current: workflow.md:27 "Use workspace-aware commands: `pnpm --filter <package> build`, not `cd packages/foo && pnpm build`"
findings.truth: In xy toolchain repos, workspace packages generally have no `build` script; the scaffold gives packages only `package-compile`. Builds, lints and tests are run from the root with a package argument (`pnpm xy build <package>`), so `pnpm --filter <pkg> build` finds no script.
findings.evidence: sdk-js/packages/sdk/package.json scripts (sync-sdk-layout, test only); sdk-js/packages/telemetry and toolchain/packages/vitest-config have no scripts; toolchain/packages/toolchain/templates/repo/cli/package/package.json.tmpl scripts = { package-compile }. CLAUDE.md 'Always run from the repo root ... Append a package name to scope: pnpm xy build @ariestools/sdk'.
findings.recommendation: Rephrase generically: use the repo's workspace-aware form. Give two examples: `pnpm --filter <pkg> <script>` when packages define the script, and `pnpm xy <command> <package>` from the root in xy-toolchain repos (see xy-toolchain).

findings.title: ESM rule mandates .js import extensions; toolchain and SDK use .ts
findings.current: typescript.md:62 "Use `.js` extensions in relative import paths (TypeScript resolves `.ts` → `.js`)"
findings.truth: @ariestools/tsconfig sets `allowImportingTsExtensions: true` with `noEmit: true` (the toolchain emits). The toolchain source, the `xy repo init` templates and sdk-js all use `.ts` extensions on relative imports.
findings.evidence: toolchain/packages/tsconfig/tsconfig.json. toolchain/packages/toolchain/templates/repo/cli/package/src/index.ts.tmpl and src/commands/index.ts (`./versionCommand.ts`). grep: sdk-js/packages/*/src 670 `.ts` vs 22 `.js`; toolchain/packages/toolchain/src 1134 `.ts`, 0 `.js`.
findings.recommendation: Say: use explicit extensions on relative imports and match the repo. XY toolchain repos use `.ts` (enabled by `allowImportingTsExtensions`); `.js` is only for repos whose tsc emits directly.

findings.title: Package-manager discovery ignores packageManager field and bun
findings.current: workflow.md:11-15 detection by lock file only: pnpm-lock.yaml → pnpm, yarn.lock → yarn, package-lock.json → npm
findings.truth: The toolchain resolves the root `packageManager` field first, then pnpm lock or workspace, then bun.lock/bun.lockb, then yarn.lock/.yarnrc.yml, then npm lock. pnpm is the only supported manager; the others are experimental.
findings.evidence: toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/pm/detectPackageManager.ts:9-19. toolchain/docs/STABILITY.md:62.
findings.recommendation: Make step 1 read the root `packageManager` field first, add bun lockfiles, and note that pnpm is the default for new XY repos.
