findings.title: papers/ and docs/ layout contradicts the toolchain's `xy plan lint` contract
findings.current: structure.md:50 "The house convention is `<PRODUCT>_{WHITE,YELLOW,GREEN,LIGHT}_PAPER.md`"; structure.md:29 "Add a tier when it has real content, never as a placeholder"; structure.md:5-27 tree has no `notes/` and no `docs/ROADMAP.md`.
findings.truth: `xy plan lint` (experimental, 9.2.1 and 10.0.5) enforces a different canonical layout. papers/ must contain README.md, WHITE-PAPER.md and YELLOW-PAPER.md, with optional GREEN-PAPER.md; anything else is an error, and `--fix` flattens it into notes/. docs/README.md and docs/ROADMAP.md are required, as are notes/README.md and root AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, CHANGELOG.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and README.md. A repo following this skill fails plan lint, and `--fix` moves its papers. ROADMAP: code wins until docs are revised.
findings.evidence: toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/plan/lint.ts:19-40, 483-501. `xy.mjs plan lint --rules` (plan.papers.required-files, plan.papers.unexpected-files, plan.docs.required-files, plan.notes.required-files, plan.root.required-files). toolchain/CHANGELOG.md:16, 30. toolchain/docs/ROADMAP.md:7. Commits 5fe4948cd → v9.2.1, eb11282ab → v10.0.5.
findings.recommendation: Reconcile one way or the other. Either adopt the plan-lint names in the skill (papers/WHITE-PAPER.md etc., docs/ROADMAP.md, notes/), or record the divergence and change plan lint. Until then, add a note that `xyex plan lint --fix` relocates non-canonical papers into notes/.

findings.title: Says no tooling exists and points to a nonexistent `xy agent index`; plan lint now implements part of the catalog
findings.current: auditing.md:9 "There is no `xy agent` command yet. The checks below are performed by hand today"; auditing.md:14-18 future `xy agent lint/init/audit/index/archive`; templates.md:212 `<!-- Generated. Do not edit. Run: pnpm xy agent index -->`; structure.md:14 `docs/README.md GENERATED index — never hand-edited`
findings.truth:
No `xy agent` command exists in 10.1.0. However, `xyex plan lint` and `xyex plan init` (experimental, not in `xy check`) check several items in this catalog:
- `CLAUDE.md` imports `@AGENTS.md` (plan.root.claude-imports-agents).
- `AGENTS.md` uses no `@path` imports (plan.root.agents-no-at-imports).
- root README/AGENTS link to papers/ and docs/ (plan.root.docs-index).
- the required root files exist.
Its `--fix` scaffolds a hand-written `docs/README.md` index, not a generated one. The template's 'Run: pnpm xy agent index' tells agents to run a command that does not exist.
findings.evidence: `xy.mjs --help` (no `agent` command; `plan` experimental). `xy.mjs plan lint --rules`. toolchain/docs/repo-docs.md:33-50. toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/plan/templates.ts:55-64 (docs/README.md and ROADMAP templates).
findings.recommendation: Update 'Tooling status' to name `xyex plan lint` / `xyex plan init` and the checks they cover. Keep the `xy agent` surface explicitly labelled 'proposed'. Remove the `pnpm xy agent index` instruction from templates.md:212, or replace it with 'maintained by hand until a generator ships'.

findings.title: Allows symlinked or absent CLAUDE.md and nested package AGENTS.md, which the toolchain contract forbids
findings.current: agents-md.md:110-114 "A symlink works equally well ... `ln -s AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md`"; auditing.md:32 "`CLAUDE.md` is an `@AGENTS.md` import, a symlink, or absent"; agents-md.md:130-136 and structure.md:24 allow `packages/<pkg>/AGENTS.md` deltas
findings.truth: The toolchain's monorepo markdown contract requires CLAUDE.md to be a regular file containing `@AGENTS.md` (plan.root.required-files, plan.root.claude-imports-agents). It says "Keep agent instructions at the repository root. Do not add `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` inside packages." Every workspace package needs a consumer README.md listed in `files` (repo.package-readme, error in `xy check`).
findings.evidence: toolchain/docs/repo-docs.md:13-16, 22, 37-42. `xy.mjs repo lint --rules` (repo.package-readme, repo.package-readme-files at error). `xy.mjs plan lint --rules`.
findings.recommendation: Make the `@AGENTS.md` import the only accepted adapter for monorepos. Drop the symlink option, or mark it non-conforming with plan lint. Reconcile the nested-AGENTS.md guidance with repo-docs.md: either remove it or note that the toolchain contract forbids package-level agent files. Add that package READMEs are consumer docs required by `xy repo lint`.

findings.title: AGENTS.md template tells agents to run experimental `xy work` via the stable bin
findings.current: templates.md:23 "3. `pnpm xy work list` — the open work items."; auditing.md:100-105 reference `xy work triage` / `xy work done`

findings.title: CLAUDE.md adapter guidance (symlink or absent) contradicts the toolchain's `xy plan lint` contract
findings.current: agents-md.md:110-116 "A symlink works equally well when there is nothing Claude-specific to add: ln -s AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md"; templates.md:75-79 repeats the symlink option; auditing.md:32 "CLAUDE.md is an @AGENTS.md import, a symlink, or absent". structure.md:7 says the import is "required, not optional", which disagrees with auditing.md:32 inside the same skill.
findings.truth: `xy plan lint` (published in v10.0.5+, inside the 10.1.0 deploy, experimental) requires root CLAUDE.md to exist as a regular file that is not a symlink, and requires it to contain @AGENTS.md. The toolchain's docs/repo-docs.md:22 says the bridge is "a real import, not a Markdown link and not a symlink". The rule landed 2026-09-08 (eb11282ab), one week after xy-agent was written (2026-09-01, 2d8f995).
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/toolchain/src/actions/plan/lint.ts:19-25 (REQUIRED_ROOT_PATHS includes CLAUDE.md) and :84-91 (regularFiles = stat.isFile() && !stat.isSymbolicLink()); plan/rootDocs.ts:61 ("CLAUDE.md must import AGENTS.md with @AGENTS.md"); `node packages/toolchain/dist/bin/xy.mjs plan lint --rules` lists plan.root.required-files and plan.root.claude-imports-agents at level error; stability.ts 'plan lint': 'experimental'; `git merge-base --is-ancestor eb11282ab 3320116a4` returns true (rule is in the 10.1.0 deploy).
findings.recommendation: Remove the symlink option from agents-md.md:110-116 and templates.md:75-79, or label it as failing `xyex plan lint`. Make the adapter a regular CLAUDE.md that holds `@AGENTS.md`, optionally with the HTML-comment header from repo-docs.md:25-26. Change auditing.md:32 to "CLAUDE.md is a regular file containing @AGENTS.md (required)" so it agrees with structure.md:7. Keep the Windows rationale in agents-md.md:116 as the reason for preferring the import.

findings.title: Canonical tree and papers naming conflict with the layout `xy plan lint` requires and auto-fixes
findings.current: structure.md:5-27: the canonical tree has no CHANGELOG.md, no CONTRIBUTING.md, no notes/, no docs/ROADMAP.md and no papers/README.md. structure.md:50-55 names papers "<PRODUCT>_{WHITE,YELLOW,GREEN,LIGHT}_PAPER.md" and agents-md.md:31 uses `papers/X_YELLOW_PAPER.md`. structure.md:8 limits README.md to "what it is, install, commands. NOT policy."
findings.truth: `xy plan lint` requires these files: root AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, CHANGELOG.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and README.md; papers/README.md, papers/WHITE-PAPER.md and papers/YELLOW-PAPER.md (papers/GREEN-PAPER.md is optional); docs/README.md and docs/ROADMAP.md; notes/README.md. `plan.papers.unexpected-files` is an error, and its fix flattens every other file in papers/ into notes/. A repo that follows xy-agent's naming (for example ACME_LIGHT_PAPER.md) therefore fails the check, and `--fix` moves the papers. `plan.root.docs-index` also requires the root README.md and AGENTS.md to Markdown-link into papers/ and docs/.
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/toolchain/src/actions/plan/lint.ts:19-37 (REQUIRED_ROOT_PATHS, REQUIRED_PAPER_PATHS, OPTIONAL_PAPER_PATHS = ['papers/GREEN-PAPER.md'], REQUIRED_DOC_PATHS, REQUIRED_NOTES_PATHS); output of `xy.mjs plan lint --rules` (plan.papers.unexpected-files: "fixes flatten other regular files into notes/"; plan.root.docs-index); toolchain docs/repo-docs.md:9-16 audience map.
findings.recommendation: Choose one owner for this contract and align the other side. findings.title: Layer 1's root-barrel import rule contradicts ariestools-sdk's subpath guidance and relies on a downstream XYO pack
findings.current: typescript.md:64-78 tells agents to "Import from the root barrel package of each monorepo… Avoid — importing from sub-packages", with an `@xyo-network/sdk` example and "See the XYO and XL1 knowledge skills for the specific root barrel packages."

The toolchain's `xy lint init` barrel restrictions target only multi-package barrels (@xylabs/sdk-js, @xylabs/sdk-react, @xyo-network/sdk-js, xl1-sdk, chain-sdk, react-chain, react-sdk) and nothing for @ariestools/sdk subpaths. findings.evidence: xy-development/typescript.md:64-78; ariestools-sdk/overview.md:22-29, conventions.md:5-8,17; toolchain packages/toolchain/src/actions/lint-init.ts:56-67.

Add one line saying the enforced barrels come from `xy lint init` (xy-toolchain eslint.md) and that @ariestools/sdk subpath guidance is owned by ariestools-sdk.

findings.title: Layer 1 mandates `.js` extensions in relative imports, but the house convention is `.ts`
findings.current: typescript.md:62 "Use `.js` extensions in relative import paths (TypeScript resolves `.ts` → `.js`)"
findings.truth: @ariestools/tsconfig sets allowImportingTsExtensions: true with noEmit, and the toolchain emits the output. The reference repos use `.ts`: toolchain packages/*/src has 1810 relative imports ending in .ts and 0 in .js; sdk-js has 1052 .ts and 29 .js. Layer 2 lists allowImportingTsExtensions (xy-toolchain/typescript.md:34) but never states the convention, and its own example uses .js (xy-toolchain/testing.md:202).
findings.evidence: toolchain packages/tsconfig/tsconfig.json:4; `grep -rhoE "from '\.{1,2}/[^']+\.ts'" packages/*/src | wc -l` in toolchain gives 1810 (.js gives 0) and in sdk-js gives 1052 (.js gives 29).
findings.recommendation: In Layer 1, say "use explicit file extensions in relative imports, matching the repository's existing convention" so it stays toolchain-agnostic. Move the house rule (.ts extensions, enabled by allowImportingTsExtensions) into xy-toolchain/typescript.md (see the separate xy-toolchain finding).

findings.title: Layer 1 prescribes `pnpm --filter <pkg> build` and `pnpm compile`, which conflicts with Layer 2's root-scoped `xy` commands
findings.current: workflow.md:27 "Use workspace-aware commands: `pnpm --filter <package> build`, not `cd packages/foo && pnpm build`"; workflow.md:18-21 maps gates to pnpm build, lint and test; workflow.md:89 "A clean `pnpm compile` does not guarantee…"
findings.truth: Layer 2 runs the root `xy` with a package argument (xy-toolchain/project-profiles.md:122-123; toolchain.md:51). In xy repos, workspace packages have no build script: sdk-js packages/sdk/package.json scripts are only {sync-sdk-layout, sync-sdk-layout:check, test}, and the sdk-js root has no build, lint or test script. `pnpm --filter @ariestools/sdk build` therefore has nothing to run there. `compile` is an xy-specific script name.
findings.evidence: node -e on sdk-js packages/sdk/package.json and the root package.json scripts; xy-toolchain/project-profiles.md:117-127; toolchain.md:49-66.
findings.recommendation: Replace workflow.md:27 with tool-neutral wording: "Use the repository's workspace-aware entry point: its root script or CLI with a package argument (for example `pnpm xy build <pkg>` in @ariestools/toolchain repos), or `pnpm --filter <pkg> <script>` when packages define that script." Add "If the repo uses @ariestools/toolchain, follow xy-toolchain." Change `pnpm compile` at :89 to "the repo's compile/build command".

findings.title: The Layer-3 Node floor (>=26) is missing; Layer 2's stated baseline is Node 22
findings.current: absent in ariestools-sdk. xy-toolchain/toolchain.md:41 says "requires Node.js 22 or newer" and :115 says "Require Node.js 22 or newer unless the consuming product imposes a newer version".
findings.truth: Every published sdk-js package declares engines.node ">=26", while the toolchain and config packages declare ">=22". A repo following Layer 2's baseline and then adding @ariestools/sdk hits an engine mismatch that neither skill mentions.
findings.evidence: sdk-js packages/*/package.json engines (sdk, crypto, crypto-auth, eth-address, express, json-rpc-engine, sdk-meta, pixel, storage-adapters, telemetry, testing and threads are all {"node":">=26"}); `npm view @ariestools/sdk@9.0.1 engines` returns { node: '>=26' }; toolchain packages/{toolchain,eslint-config-flat,tsconfig,vitest-config,lib-neutral}/package.json engines {"node":">=22"}.
findings.recommendation: Add a Requirements block to overview.md: Node >=26 for @ariestools sdk-js packages, ESM only, peers zod (optional) and @opentelemetry/api. Cross-reference it from xy-toolchain/toolchain.md:115 ("adding @ariestools/sdk raises the floor to Node 26; see ariestools-sdk").

findings.title: "Tooling status" is stale: `xy plan lint` already automates part of the check catalog, and a template cites a command that does not exist
findings.current: auditing.md:9 "There is no `xy agent` command yet. The checks below are performed by hand today"; auditing.md:11-19 describes a future `xy agent` surface; templates.md:212 `<!-- Generated. Do not edit. Run: pnpm xy agent index -->`. structure.md:24 and agents-md.md:91,130-136 recommend nested `packages/<pkg>/AGENTS.md`.
findings.truth: `xy --help` lists no `agent` command. `xy plan lint` (experimental, "prefer xyex") has shipped since v10.0.5 and checks several entry-point items automatically, with --fix: plan.root.claude-imports-agents, plan.root.agents-no-at-imports, plan.root.docs-index and plan.root.required-files. The toolchain's docs/repo-docs.md is a second normative description of the same conventions and disagrees in places: repo-docs.md:16 says "Do not add AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md inside packages". The xy-toolchain skill never mentions `xy plan` (grep finds no match).
findings.evidence: `node packages/toolchain/dist/bin/xy.mjs --help` command list; `xy.mjs plan --help`; `xy.mjs plan lint --rules`; toolchain stability.ts ('plan': 'experimental', 'plan lint': 'experimental'); toolchain docs/repo-docs.md:16,22,35-44; `grep -rn "xy plan" skills/` returns nothing.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite "Tooling status": name `xyex plan lint` as the current automated subset (experimental, monorepo-scoped, not part of `xy check`), map its rules onto the check catalog, and keep the rest manual. Replace the templates.md:212 command with "regenerate with the repository's index generator". Ownership: xy-toolchain commands.md documents the `plan lint` command and its rules; xy-agent owns the conventions and links to it. Reconcile the remaining disagreements with repo-docs.md, including nested AGENTS.md (allow it as delta-only, or drop it), so the skill and the toolchain stop being two separate sources of truth.

findings.title: xy-agent contradicts xy-toolchain on claiming work items and restates toolchain internals that do not hold at the CLI
findings.current: auditing.md:109 "there is no lease or compare-and-swap. Queue work there; do not claim work there." auditing.md:102 "Pass an explicit stable id derived from the check and the path". lifecycle.md:114 cites `WorkAnchor` and `createWorkId` internals. templates.md:23 uses `pnpm xy work list`.
findings.truth: xy-toolchain/commands.md:185-186 tells agents to run `pnpm xy work next --claim` and `claim <id>`, and the toolchain's own xy-work skill says "Claim the next item before starting implementation". A claim is only a timestamp (work/helpers.ts:60-65; schema.ts:28 claimedAt), so the no-lease caveat is accurate, but it is missing from Layer 2. `xy work add --help` has no --id flag; an explicit id is only possible programmatically (work/index.ts:171 options.id). `work` is experimental: stability.ts has 'work': 'experimental', and the help text says "(experimental — prefer xyex)".
findings.evidence: xy-toolchain/commands.md:177-190; toolchain .agents/skills/xy-work/SKILL.md "Queue And Execute" section; packages/toolchain/src/actions/work/{helpers.ts:60-65, schema.ts:17-18,28, index.ts:171}; `xy.mjs work add --help` (options list has no --id).
findings.recommendation: Move the operational `xy work` guidance into xy-toolchain's work section: claim semantics and the no-lease warning for multi-worktree use, deduplication, suppressing GitHub dual-write for machine-generated items, and the xyex channel. In xy-agent, keep a short pointer: "record findings in the repository's work tracker; in xy repos see xy-toolchain work tracking". Replace the stable-id advice with "search existing items by tag/file before adding", or file a toolchain request for `xy work add --id`.

findings.title: Layer 1 includes XYO/XL1 product-specific examples and references

findings.title: Package-manager detection in Layer 1 diverges from Layer 2's order
findings.current: workflow.md:11-15 detects the package manager from the lock file only (pnpm, yarn, npm).

findings.title: The `any` ladder ends with 'use any plus a // TODO comment', which fails the enforced no-explicit-any lint error

A TODO comment alone fails `xy lint`, and the DoD (workflow.md:73-75) requires a clean lint. The repos write an ESLint disable directive instead. CLAUDE.md:45.

findings.title: `pnpm install --resolution-only` no longer exists in pnpm 12, the version every ariestools library repo pins
findings.current: workflow.md:88 "After adding or changing dependencies, run `pnpm install --resolution-only` to force a fresh resolution check that surfaces all peer dependency warnings."
findings.truth: pnpm 12.x rejects the flag. Every ariestools library repo pins pnpm@12.4.2, and sdk-react pins pnpm@12.9.1. The replacement is `pnpm peers check`, available in pnpm 11.25+ and 12, which 'Checks for unmet or missing peer dependency issues'. Only pnpm 10/11 accept `--resolution-only`.
findings.evidence: In an empty scratch dir: `corepack pnpm@12.4.2 install --resolution-only --help` prints "error: unexpected argument '--resolution-only' found". 12.9.1 and 12.10.1 print the same error. 10.33.2 prints the install usage, and `pnpm@11.25.0 install --help` lists --resolution-only at line 162. `pnpm peers --help` on 12.4.2 shows "Checks for unmet or missing peer dependency issues"; 11.25.0 shows the `check` subcommand. Pins: ariestools/cli-kit/package.json:39 pnpm@12.4.2 (same in toolchain, sdk-js, browser-kit and actor-kit); ariestools/sdk-react/package.json:74 pnpm@12.9.1.
findings.recommendation: Replace with a version-aware instruction: "Check the pinned pnpm major (`packageManager`). On pnpm 11+ run `pnpm peers check`; on pnpm 10 run `pnpm install --resolution-only`." Keep the warning that a no-op install hides peer issues.

findings.title: `pnpm --filter <package> build` fails in XY repos and contradicts the rule to run from the repo root

findings.title: No guidance on finding the Node runtime and package-manager versions (repos pin Node 26 and pnpm 12)

findings.title: The absolute 'never rewrite history' ban contradicts workspace and repo policy
findings.current: git.md:46-62 "Git history is append-only... **Never do any of the following:** `git commit --amend` ... `git rebase` (interactive or otherwise) — merge instead ... `git push --force` or `--force-with-lease`"
findings.truth: The workspace instructions require rewriting an unpushed commit that has the wrong author email, and say to ask before force-pushing one that is already pushed. The skills repo bans rewriting only on shared branches. Gitflow repos squash-merge feature PRs as standard policy.
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md:56 "Rewrite an unpushed commit that carries the wrong email (keeping its tree, parents, message, and dates); ask before force-pushing one that is already pushed." (same at AGENTS.md:264). ariestools-skills CLAUDE.md:41 "Never rewrite git history on shared branches (no force-push to `main`/`develop`)" and :47-49 squash for feature→develop and release-please→main. XYOracleNetwork/xyo-skills/CLAUDE.md:65-74 (same merge policy and rationale).
findings.recommendation: Scope the rule: "Never rewrite pushed or shared history: no force-push to main/develop, and ask before force-pushing anything already pushed. You may amend or rebase your own unpushed local commits when repo or workspace instructions require it (for example, fixing commit identity). Platform squash merges done under the repo's merge policy are expected." Keep the revert, fix-forward and cherry-pick guidance for pushed mistakes.

findings.title: Gitflow with release/* branches is presented as the default, but most repos work on trunk/main
findings.current: git.md:66 "We follow Gitflow where possible"; :69 "`main` — production-ready code. Every commit on main is a release."; :75 "`release/<version>` — release prep..."; :82-87 the workflow; :89-90 trunk allowed only as a 'Pragmatism' exception
findings.truth: Only 9 of the 80 local clones have an origin/develop branch, and none have release/* branches. The six ariestools library repos (toolchain, sdk-js, cli-kit, browser-kit, actor-kit, sdk-react) have no develop branch on the remote. They commit straight to main, merge topic and agent branches (`claude/*`, `codex/*`, `feat/*`), run CI on push to main, and release by bumping versions with `xy deploy` plus a 'Deploy' commit. The Gitflow repos (the skill packs) release with release-please, not release/* branches.
findings.evidence: Scan of {XYOracleNetwork,xylabs,ariestools}/*: repos=80, with_develop=9, release/*=0 everywhere. `git ls-remote --heads origin`: toolchain shows feat/typescript-native-compiler, feature/eslint-flat, feature/esm-run-mode, main and prev; cli-kit shows ci/pnpm12-action-setup and main; actor-kit shows only main. Merge commits on main: toolchain "Merge branch 'claude/eloquent-wright-73114e'"; sdk-js "Merge branch 'codex/bounded-response-reads'". toolchain 3320116a4 "Deploy\n\n10.1.0"; toolchain/.github/workflows/build.yml:3-7 (push: branches: main). ariestools-skills CLAUDE.md:54 "Release-please on push to `main`... Do not bump versions by hand."
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the section as "Follow the repo's documented branching model" and describe the two models in use. (1) Trunk: main plus short-lived topic branches (including agent `claude/*` and `codex/*` worktree branches), released through `xy deploy`. (2) Gitflow: `develop` as the integration branch, release-please PRs into main. Remove `release/<version>` branches, manual tagging, and "every commit on main is a release".

findings.title: Merge-method policy is missing, including that the PR title becomes the squash commit message
findings.current: absent. git.md:83-86 only says "merge feature into develop" and "Merge the release branch into main".
findings.truth: Gitflow repos squash feature→develop and release-please→main PRs, and use merge commits for develop→main and the main→develop sync. Never squash between two long-lived branches. A squashed PR's title becomes the conventional commit that release-please reads.
findings.evidence: ariestools-skills CLAUDE.md:44-50 (merge method table). XYOracleNetwork/xyo-skills/CLAUDE.md:65-74 ("squash is fine when the source branch is throwaway... `develop ↔ main` always merge-commit"). ariestools-skills .github/workflows/lint-pr-title.yml:13-28 and :34-58 lint PR titles.
findings.recommendation: Add a short 'Merging' subsection. Squash throwaway branches (feature or fix PRs, release-please PRs) and merge-commit long-lived branch pairs (develop↔main). Because the PR title becomes the squash commit, it must be a valid conventional commit. Follow the repo's merge-method table when it has one.

findings.title: Commit-type list and rules miss perf/style/revert, breaking-change syntax, and the PR-title rules that actually enforce types
findings.current: git.md:11-19 lists only feat, fix, refactor, chore, docs, test, build, ci; git.md:21-25 rules say nothing about breaking changes; git.md:32 example "chore: update typescript to 5.x"

Breaking changes use `type!:` or a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer in practice. No commit-message hook or commitlint exists in the library repos, and `xy git lint` checks git config (autocrlf/eol/ignorecase), not messages, so the convention is enforced only through PR titles. findings.evidence: ariestools-skills .github/workflows/lint-pr-title.yml:13-28 (main: feat and fix only) and :34-54 (develop: 11 types). toolchain commit 13350616a "feat(toolchain)!: remove lintlint, republint, node-lint, gitlint aliases"; actor-kit has 2 `!:` commits and 2 BREAKING CHANGE footers since 2026-01-01. `xy.mjs git lint --rules` lists git.autocrlf, git.eol, git.ignore-toolchain-cache and git.ignorecase. No commitlint, husky or PR-title workflow in toolchain, sdk-js, cli-kit, browser-kit, actor-kit or sdk-react .github/workflows. cli-kit/package.json devDependencies "typescript":"~6.0.3".

Add breaking-change notation (`feat(scope)!:` or a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer) and explain that release tooling derives version bumps from the type. findings.title: No generic rule against overriding the configured commit identity
findings.current: absent

findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md:52-56; AGENTS.md:260-264

findings.title: 'Prefer inference; do not annotate return types' contradicts the workspace rule of explicit return types on exported functions
findings.current: typescript.md:23-31 "Let TypeScript's type inference do its job... **Do not annotate return types** unless one of these applies: public API boundary..."
findings.truth: The workspace convention is explicit return types on exported functions, and `Promise<T>` (never `Promise<Promisable<T>>`) for functions that await. ESLint does not enforce this (explicit-module-boundary-types is off; explicit-function-return-type is unset), so it is exactly the kind of rule a linter can't catch, which this file exists to cover. In practice almost all exported functions are annotated.
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md:43 "Explicit return types on exported functions"; :46 "declare the return as `Promise<T>` — never `Promise<Promisable<T>>`". toolchain/packages/eslint-config-flat/src/typescript/index.ts:101 and tiers/rule-catalog/managed-rules.ts:54 set explicit-module-boundary-types 'off'; cli-kit print-config shows explicit-function-return-type undefined. Grep of single-line `export function ... {` signatures: toolchain/packages 501 of 517 annotated, cli-kit/packages 72 of 75, sdk-js/packages 86 of 104, actor-kit 12 of 12.
findings.recommendation: Reword to: "Annotate the return type of every exported function and method (the public contract). For async functions use `Promise<T>`, never `Promise<Promisable<T>>`. Rely on inference for local helpers, callbacks and variables." Keep the type-guard and recursion cases.

findings.title: Enums are framed as 'prefer unions', but the shared tsconfig makes enums, parameter properties and runtime namespaces compile errors
findings.current: typescript.md:85 "**Prefer union types** over enums: `type Status = 'active' | 'inactive'` rather than `enum Status { Active, Inactive }`". Parameter properties and namespaces are not mentioned.
findings.truth: @ariestools/tsconfig sets `erasableSyntaxOnly: true` (since 2025-08-06). TypeScript 6.0.3 then reports TS1294 for `enum`, constructor parameter properties and runtime namespaces. ESLint also flags TSEnumDeclaration with 'Enums are disallowed'. The workspace rule is 'No `enum` (use string-literal unions or `const` objects)'.
findings.evidence: ariestools/toolchain/packages/tsconfig/tsconfig.json:8 "erasableSyntaxOnly": true (introduced in 7d4b6b5ec, 2025-08-06). A scratch file compiled with cli-kit's tsc 6.0.3 and --erasableSyntaxOnly reports "error TS1294: This syntax is not allowed when 'erasableSyntaxOnly' is enabled" at the enum (1,13), the `constructor(private readonly bar: string)` (3,15) and the `namespace NS { export const x = 1 }` (5,18). eslint-config-flat/src/typescript/index.ts:161-167 no-restricted-syntax on TSEnumDeclaration. CLAUDE.md:45.
findings.recommendation: Replace with an 'Erasable syntax only' rule: never use `enum` (it is a compile error), and use string-literal unions or `as const` objects plus a derived union type. Do not use constructor parameter properties; declare fields explicitly. Do not use runtime `namespace` or `import x = require()`.

findings.title: Relative imports are told to use `.js` extensions, but the shared tsconfig and nearly all code use `.ts`
findings.current: typescript.md:62 "Use `.js` extensions in relative import paths (TypeScript resolves `.ts` → `.js`)"
findings.truth: The base tsconfig sets allowImportingTsExtensions with NodeNext resolution, and repo source writes `.ts` on relative imports. The toolchain's own lint restriction is written in `.ts` form (`./index.ts`, `../index.ts`).
findings.evidence: toolchain/packages/tsconfig/tsconfig.json:4 "allowImportingTsExtensions": true. eslint-config-flat/src/rules/correctness.ts:5-14 restricted paths './index.ts' … '../../../../../../../index.ts'. Grep of `from './…'` in *.ts/*.tsx excluding node_modules and dist: toolchain/packages 2232 `.ts` vs 27 `.js` lines (all in spec fixtures monolithCompile.spec.ts and monolithDedupeDeclarations.spec.ts); sdk-js/packages 1052 vs 29; cli-kit 512 vs 0; browser-kit 130 vs 0; actor-kit 268 vs 0; sdk-react 891 vs 0.
findings.recommendation: Change to: "Use `.ts` extensions in relative import paths. The shared @ariestools/tsconfig enables allowImportingTsExtensions, and the toolchain's compile step emits the runtime extensions." Mention that repos not on the shared tsconfig follow their own config.

findings.title: The root-barrel section uses an XYO example and points to skills that are not in this pack
findings.current: typescript.md:66 "Import from the root barrel package of each monorepo... reach for a named sub-package only when the symbol genuinely is not on the barrel"; :70-75 `@xyo-network/sdk` / `@xyo-network/payload-model` example; :78 "See the XYO and XL1 knowledge skills for the specific root barrel packages."

The xyo-knowledge and xl1-knowledge skills ship only in XYOracleNetwork/xyo-skills, so a Layer 1 skill here should not depend on them. Read literally, 'avoid sub-packages' conflicts with Layer 3's subpath guidance.

Use `@ariestools/sdk` / `@ariestools/sdk/fetch` as the example, defer package-specific choices to the ariestools-sdk skill (Layer 3) and, for XYO, to the domain pack. State explicitly that subpath exports of the barrel package are fine.

findings.title: Enforced import restrictions are missing: no local index.ts barrels, no other package's src/, no cross-package relative imports, type-only imports
findings.current: absent. typescript.md:64-81 covers only root-barrel packages and import ordering, and its own example (typescript.md:70) imports the type `Payload` in a value import.
findings.truth: `no-restricted-imports` is an error from tier 0. It bans relative imports of `./index.ts` up to `../../../../../../../index.ts` and any `**/src/**` path into another package. At tier 3 and above, `workspaces/no-relative-imports` and `workspaces/require-dependency` are errors. `consistent-type-imports` requires a separate `import type`. The workspace rule is 'no importing from barrel `index.ts` files'.
findings.evidence: toolchain/packages/eslint-config-flat/src/rules/index.ts:5-28 and :44-56 (srcImportsConfig message "Do not import from another package's src folder"); tiers/rule-catalog/managed-rules.ts:46 (no-restricted-imports error at tier 0), :129-130 (workspaces rules error at tier 3), :84-87 (consistent-type-imports, separate-type-imports). cli-kit print-config: no-restricted-imports [2,{paths:[./index.ts…],patterns:[**/src/**…]}], workspaces/no-relative-imports [2], workspaces/require-dependency [2], consistent-type-imports [1,{fixStyle:separate-type-imports}]. CLAUDE.md:45.
findings.recommendation: Add an 'Import boundaries' block. Inside a package, import the defining file directly and never the local `index.ts` barrel. Across workspace packages, import by package name, never by relative path or `src/`, and declare the dependency. Put type-only imports in `import type { … }`. Fix the example so the type is imported with `import type`.

findings.title: Type-aware rules that change how code must be written (strict-boolean-expressions and others) are not mentioned
findings.current: typescript.md:5 says linters cover most opinions. :87 says "prefer optional chaining (`?.`) and nullish coalescing (`??`)". Truthiness checks are not mentioned.
findings.truth: The default recommendedConfig is tier 3 with type checking. At that level `@typescript-eslint/strict-boolean-expressions` and `no-deprecated` are errors, and the effective config also makes `prefer-nullish-coalescing`, `prefer-optional-chain`, `no-floating-promises` and `no-misused-promises` errors. The base tsconfig enables noImplicitOverride. So `if (maybeString)`, unawaited promises, deprecated APIs and a missing `override` all fail the lint or the compile.
findings.evidence: eslint-config-flat/src/tiers/recommendedConfig.ts:12-15 (DEFAULT: isTypeChecked true, tier 3); tiers/rule-catalog/managed-rules.ts:57-58 (strict-boolean-expressions and no-deprecated: 3 → 'error'). cli-kit print-config: strict-boolean-expressions [2], prefer-nullish-coalescing [2], prefer-optional-chain [2], no-floating-promises [2], no-misused-promises [2], no-deprecated [2]. toolchain/packages/tsconfig/tsconfig.json:19 noImplicitOverride.
findings.recommendation: Add a short 'Write it right the first time' list. Use explicit comparisons for nullable values (`!== undefined`, `.length > 0`) instead of truthiness. Use `??` and `?.` (enforced). Await or explicitly `void` every promise. Do not call @deprecated APIs. Mark overrides with `override`. Link xy-toolchain/eslint.md for the full tier catalog instead of listing rules here.

findings.title: Workspace style conventions that no linter enforces are missing
findings.current: typescript.md:86 covers only "PascalCase for types and interfaces, camelCase for variables and functions". Named exports, function style, boolean prefixes, file naming and Node built-in imports are absent.
findings.truth: The workspace requires these, and none are enforced by an ESLint rule: named exports over default; `function` declarations at top level with arrows only for callbacks; booleans prefixed is/has/should/can; camelCase module files and PascalCase component or class files; Node built-ins imported via `node:` with a default import (`import PATH from 'node:path'`); no `import * as X`. Only filename-case (camel, kebab or pascal accepted), prefer-node-protocol and import-style are lint-backed. The toolchain itself renamed its `typeChecked` option to `isTypeChecked`, applying the boolean-prefix rule to its own public API.
findings.evidence: CLAUDE.md:42-47 (also AGENTS.md:250-255). cli-kit print-config: import-x/no-default-export, func-style, @typescript-eslint/naming-convention and import-x/no-namespace all undefined; unicorn/filename-case [2,{cases:{camelCase,kebabCase,pascalCase}}]; unicorn/prefer-node-protocol [2]; unicorn/import-style [2]. eslint-config-flat/src/tiers/recommendedConfig.ts:8 `isTypeChecked` and :66-69 (legacy `typeChecked` parse). toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/releaseAgeExcludeScopes.ts:2 `import PATH from 'node:path'`.
findings.recommendation: Extend 'Other Conventions' to cover: named exports only; top-level `function` declarations with arrows for callbacks; boolean names prefixed is/has/should/can; file names camelCase for modules and PascalCase for components and classes; `node:`-prefixed built-ins with default import for path-style modules; no `import * as X`. Note which of these lint enforces and which are review-only.

findings.title: The import-ordering description is approximate; simple-import-sort enforces and autofixes the order
findings.current: typescript.md:80-81 "External packages first, then internal modules, separated by a blank line"
findings.truth: simple-import-sort/imports and simple-import-sort/exports are warnings at tier 2 and errors at tier 3, with autofix. The default groups are side-effect imports, `node:` built-ins, packages, absolute, then relative.
findings.evidence: toolchain/packages/eslint-config-flat/src/import/index.ts:27-28; tiers/rule-catalog/managed-rules.ts:131-132 (2 'warn' → 3 'error'). The repos' eslint.config.ts files order `node:url` first, then a blank line, then `@ariestools/...`.
findings.recommendation: Replace with: "Import order is enforced and autofixed (simple-import-sort): `node:` built-ins, then packages, then relative imports. Run the repo's fix command instead of ordering by hand."

findings.title: Browser-verification step names MCP tools that do not exist and is specific to Claude in a pack that is also published for Codex

findings.title: Advice to add dependencies at the 'latest published version' ignores the repos' pnpm supply-chain policy and tilde-range convention
findings.current: workflow.md:35 "always use `pnpm add <package>`... to resolve the latest published version"; :87 "Version ranges follow the repo's existing conventions"
findings.truth: pnpm-workspace.yaml sets `minimumReleaseAge: 1440`, so versions under a day old are withheld (except `@ariestools/*`), and an `allowBuilds` allowlist for install scripts. `xy packman lint` enforces both. Ranges in these repos are predominantly `~`, while `pnpm add` saves `^` by default.
findings.evidence: ariestools/cli-kit/pnpm-workspace.yaml:3-8 (sdk-js identical). toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/package-lint-pnpm.ts:148-154 (checkPnpmMinimumReleaseAge) and releaseAgeExcludeScopes.ts:6 (known exclude patterns @ariestools/*, @xylabs/*, @xyo-network/*). Range prefixes: sdk-js/packages/sdk 10 `~` vs 2 `^`; cli-kit-node 10 `~`; browser-kit-page 13 `~`. No skill mentions minimumReleaseAge or allowBuilds (grep of skills/).
findings.recommendation: Add one Layer-1 caveat: "Respect the repo's package-manager policy (minimum release age, build-script allowlist). Do not bypass it to get a just-published version. After `pnpm add`, match the repo's range prefix." Document the details in xy-toolchain (packman).

findings.title: The `.npmrc` and `.env` gitignore rule conflicts with tracked config and the toolchain's gitignore template
findings.current: workflow.md:52 "`.npmrc` — may contain npm auth tokens after `npm login`. Always add it to `.gitignore`."; :53 "`.env`, `.env.*` — ... Always gitignored."; :55 verify `.gitignore` includes `.npmrc`
findings.truth: The toolchain repo tracks a project `.npmrc` with no tokens. The toolchain's managed gitignore template ignores `.env` and `.env.*` but re-includes `.env.example`, and does not list `.npmrc`. The actual rule is never to commit secrets, not that a project `.npmrc` must be ignored.
findings.evidence: `git -C toolchain ls-files .npmrc` returns 1 (empty file, added in 9bcf6363c "switch to pnpm"). toolchain/packages/toolchain/templates/gitignore/template.gitignore:25-27 lists `.env`, `.env.*`, `!.env.example` and no .npmrc. sdk-js and cli-kit .gitignore have no .npmrc entry.
findings.recommendation: Reword: "Never commit auth tokens. A tracked project `.npmrc` may hold only non-secret settings, and tokens come from user-level config or `${NPM_TOKEN}` interpolation. Ignore `.env` and `.env.*` but keep `.env.example` tracked."

findings.title: Toolchain-specific `pnpm compile` script leaks into Layer 1

findings.title: 'Layer 2' and 'Layer 3' mean different things inside xy-development, and the DoD never maps to the xy-toolchain gates
findings.current: workflow.md:116-118 "Layer 1 — Generic DoD... Layer 2 — Domain DoD... Layer 3 — Project-specific acceptance criteria (PRD.md)". SKILL.md:25 and testing.md:3 call the XY Toolchain skill "(Layer 2)". workflow.md:73 requires zero lint warnings.

Under 'Applying the Definition of Done', add one line: "In XY toolchain repos, DoD items 1-4 are the xy-toolchain lifecycle gates (`pnpm xy build`, `pnpm xy test`, `pnpm xy check`; use `--strict` so warnings fail)."

findings.title: The skill-identity example shows a version that does not match this pack's numbering

findings.title: xyo-skills install docs use `--all`, which overwrites canonical xy-development/xy-toolchain with redirect stubs
findings.current: xyo-skills/README.md:145-147 "npx skills add ariestools/ariestools-skills --all" then "npx skills add XYOracleNetwork/xyo-skills --all"; same pattern at :158 (-g) and :166 (--copy). README.md:23 calls ariestools-skills the "Required companion".
findings.truth: xyo-skills still ships skills/xy-development and skills/xy-toolchain as REDIRECT ONLY stubs (metadata.status: redirect, v1.1.38). Skills.sh installs each skill into `.agents/skills/<name>` after `cleanAndCreateDirectory(canonicalDir)`, so running the second command replaces the canonical ariestools copies with the stubs. skills-lock.json then records source XYOracleNetwork/xyo-skills, and `xy skills lint` (part of `xy check`) fails `skills.migrated-source`. The xyo-skills marketplace renderers also copy the whole skills/ tree, so anyone with both plugins installed gets two skills each named xy-development and xy-toolchain. The toolchain's own `xy skills defaults` avoids this by using explicit `--skill` selectors for xyo-skills.
findings.evidence: xyo-skills/README.md:147,158,166; xyo-skills/skills/xy-development/SKILL.md:1-12 (status: redirect); toolchain/packages/toolchain/node_modules/skills/dist/cli.mjs:2274-2324 (installSkillForAgent -> cleanAndCreateDirectory(canonicalDir)); `xy skills --help`: "--all  Shorthand for --skill '*' --agent '*' -y"; toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/skills/lock.ts:75-92 + lint.ts:364-388 (skills.migrated-source, defaultLevel error); defaults.ts:67-74 (xyo selector = explicit XYO_STACK_SKILLS); xyo-skills/scripts/marketplace-sync/build-claude.mjs:7-8 (copies all of skills/).
findings.recommendation: In xyo-skills/README.md, replace each `XYOracleNetwork/xyo-skills --all` with explicit selectors (`--skill xyo-knowledge --skill xl1-knowledge --skill xl1-patterns --skill xl1-testing --skill xl1-dapp-kit --skill xl1-scaffold --skill xl1-build`) or with `xy skills defaults`. Also state the order rule: install ariestools-skills last. Longer term, retire the stubs. Every link into them uses an anchor that exists in canonical workflow.md (lines 63, 112, 124), so rewrite the xl1-* links to absolute ariestools-skills GitHub URLs, then delete the stubs and remove them from the stub allowlist in xyo-skills/scripts/validate-skills.mjs:70-73.

findings.title: sdk-react ships tracked legacy xylabs-* skills that describe the retired yarn toolchain and compete with xy-toolchain
findings.current: sdk-react tracks .agents/skills/xylabs-xy-cli/SKILL.md, xylabs-e2e-setup/SKILL.md, and xylabs-xy-deplint-fix/SKILL.md (git ls-files). xylabs-xy-cli/SKILL.md:4 says "Comprehensive reference for the `xy` CLI provided by `@xylabs/ts-scripts-yarn3`" and its description says "Use this skill whenever the user asks how to build, lint, test...". In the toolchain, add a `skills.legacy-installed` rule to `xy skills lint` (error, fixable by removal) that flags known retired names: `xylabs-*` skill directories and generated `.claude/rules/xylabs-*.md`. findings.title: xy-agent's repository layout contradicts the toolchain's `xy plan lint` / repo-docs contract shipped in 10.1.0
findings.current: structure.md:50 "The house convention is `<PRODUCT>_{WHITE,YELLOW,GREEN,LIGHT}_PAPER.md`". structure.md:14 and lifecycle.md:104-108: docs/README.md is a "GENERATED index — never hand-edited". The tree at structure.md:5-27 has no notes/, CONTRIBUTING.md, CHANGELOG.md, or docs/ROADMAP.md. structure.md:24 and agents-md.md:130-136 allow `packages/<pkg>/AGENTS.md` as a delta. auditing.md:32 accepts CLAUDE.md as "a symlink". structure.md:29 says an empty papers/ "is a lie". auditing.md:9 says "There is no `xy agent` command yet. The checks below are performed by hand today".
findings.truth: Toolchain 10.1.0 ships experimental `xy plan lint` (prefer `xyex plan lint`). Its rules require root AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, CHANGELOG.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, and README.md. papers/ must contain exactly README.md, WHITE-PAPER.md, and YELLOW-PAPER.md, plus an optional GREEN-PAPER.md. Any other file in papers/ is an error, and `--fix` flattens it into notes/, so `<PRODUCT>_WHITE_PAPER.md` gets moved. The rules also require docs/README.md, docs/ROADMAP.md, and notes/README.md, scaffolding them from templates. toolchain/docs/repo-docs.md:16 says "Do not add `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` inside packages". repo-docs.md:22 requires CLAUDE.md to be a regular file, not a symlink. The `plan.root.*` rules automate several of xy-agent's "by hand" checks. Both landed within a day of each other: xy-agent on 2026-09-01, plan lint on 2026-09-02.
findings.evidence: toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/plan/lint.ts:19-37 (REQUIRED_ROOT_PATHS, REQUIRED_PAPER_PATHS, OPTIONAL_PAPER_PATHS, REQUIRED_DOC_PATHS, REQUIRED_NOTES_PATHS), :478-489 (plan.papers.unexpected-files "fixes flatten other regular files into notes/"); `node packages/toolchain/dist/bin/xy.mjs plan lint --rules` (8 rules listed); toolchain/docs/repo-docs.md:16,22,33-46; toolchain/CHANGELOG.md:14-17,30; xy-agent git log: 2d8f995 2026-09-01; plan/lint.ts first commit 4e14639c5 2026-09-02.
findings.recommendation: Pick one canonical contract and record the choice as a decision. Then align xy-agent with it. Rename the papers convention to `papers/{README,WHITE-PAPER,YELLOW-PAPER,GREEN-PAPER}.md`, or get plan lint changed. Add notes/, CONTRIBUTING.md, CHANGELOG.md, and docs/ROADMAP.md to the canonical tree. Reconcile the generated docs/README.md with plan lint's template-scaffolded index. Drop nested `packages/<pkg>/AGENTS.md` and the symlinked CLAUDE.md option, or get the toolchain doc changed. In auditing.md, replace the "no command yet" paragraph with `pnpm xyex plan lint` (experimental, not part of `xy check`) and `xy repo lint` for the checks that are already automated, keeping the manual checks only for the rest. Cross-link xy-toolchain.

findings.title: Toolchain skill catalog does not know xy-agent (misrouted source, rejected in config, never version-checked)
findings.current: defaults.ts:13-17 `ARIESTOOLS_SKILLS = ['ariestools-sdk','xy-development','xy-toolchain']`. defaults.ts:84-86 sends every other name to XYOracleNetwork/xyo-skills. repo-init/skillsInstall.ts:34 hard-codes the same three names. Derive the repo-init name set from ARIESTOOLS_SKILLS instead of the literal at skillsInstall.ts:34. findings.title: Version reset (xyo-skills 1.1.x to ariestools-skills 0.1.x) means stale migrated copies and redirect stubs are reported as current
findings.current: versions.ts:59-69 `isSkillVersionOutdated` uses `semver.lt(installed, latest)`. The only migration guard is lock.ts:75-92, which reads skills-lock.json.
findings.truth: Before migration, the full xy-development/xy-toolchain in xyo-skills were at 1.1.30, and today's stubs are 1.1.38. Canonical ariestools-skills is 0.1.5. So `isSkillVersionOutdated('1.1.30','0.1.5')` and `('1.1.38','0.1.5')` both return false. A stale full copy or a stub installed without a matching skills-lock entry passes `skills.required-current`. That covers manual or marketplace copies, and repos whose lock was regenerated. The skill's own identity example (xy-development/SKILL.md:14 'v1.1.19') reinforces the old numbering.
findings.evidence: node import of versions.ts: 'installed 1.1.30 ... outdated? false', 'installed 1.1.38 ... outdated? false'; xyo-skills: `git show <pre-stub>:skills/xy-development/SKILL.md` -> version 1.1.30; xyo-skills/skills/xy-development/SKILL.md:9 version 1.1.38; ariestools-skills skills/*/SKILL.md:5 version 0.1.5.
findings.recommendation: In `xy skills lint`, flag any installed SKILL.md whose frontmatter has `metadata.status: redirect` or `canonical:` as an error, fixable by reinstalling from ARIESTOOLS_SKILLS_SOURCE. Independently, consider a release-please `release-as: 2.0.0` in ariestools-skills so canonical versions sort above every xyo-skills 1.1.x copy.

findings.title: Layer-1 links to ../xy-agent dangle in every consumer, because no install path puts xy-agent beside xy-development
findings.current: SKILL.md:33 "**[xy-agent](../xy-agent/SKILL.md)** — *recommended, not required.*"; workflow.md:47 "The [xy-agent skill](../xy-agent/SKILL.md) describes the house pattern..."
findings.truth: Consumers install by name: `xy skills lint --fix` (lint.ts:91-95) and `xy repo init` (skillsInstall.ts:24-52) install only tier-required skills, and xy-agent is never required. None of toolchain, sdk-js, sdk-react, actor-kit, browser-kit, or cli-kit has .agents/skills/xy-agent, and neither does ~/.claude/skills. All of them carry the 0.1.5 xy-development that contains these relative links.
findings.evidence: `ls -d */.agents/skills/xy-agent` under ariestools/ -> no matches; `grep -c xy-agent sdk-js/.agents/skills/xy-development/SKILL.md cli-kit/.agents/skills/xy-development/workflow.md toolchain/.agents/skills/xy-development/SKILL.md` -> 1 each; diff -rq of consumer xy-development vs source -> identical.
findings.recommendation: Keep Layer 1 self-contained. Make the xy-agent mentions absolute (https://github.com/ariestools/ariestools-skills/tree/main/skills/xy-agent) and add the install hint `npx skills add ariestools/ariestools-skills --skill xy-agent`. Alternatively, after the toolchain catalog fix, have `xy skills lint` print xy-agent as an optional, info-level skill so the relative link resolves in repos that opt in.

findings.title: Telling agents to prefer `@ariestools/sdk/<module>` subpaths creates duplicate class types when the code also uses actor-kit or sdk-react
findings.current: conventions.md:6 "Prefer **subpath imports** for clarity..."; conventions.md:17 "Prefer subpaths in libraries"; conventions.md:56 "Prefer `@ariestools/sdk` + subpath for neutral helpers"; overview.md:22 "subpaths are clearer and tree-shaking-friendly"; modules.md:3 "Prefer subpaths when the import set is small"; overview.md:40 says `zod` is an optional peer, needed only for zod helpers
findings.truth: In sdk 9.0.1 the root export resolves by platform (`node` -> dist/node/index.d.ts and a bundled dist/node/index.mjs), but every subpath resolves unconditionally to dist/neutral. The house tsconfig uses NodeNext, so the `node` condition is active. Mixing root and subpath imports therefore loads two separate declarations and two separate runtime copies of classes with private members. AbstractCreatable has `private _status`. actor-kit switched to root imports for exactly this reason. The rest of the ecosystem imports from the root: actor-kit 18 root / 0 subpath, sdk-react 115/0, browser-kit 1/0, ariestools 38/4. The root bundle also statically imports `zod/mini` and `zod/v4/core`, so root importers need zod installed even though peerDependenciesMeta marks it optional.
findings.evidence: sdk-js/packages/sdk/package.json exports: '.' has node/browser/types/default conditions; './assert' and './creatable' have only types/default pointing at ./dist/neutral/*. Separate files exist at dist/node/modules/creatable/AbstractCreatable.d.ts and dist/neutral/modules/creatable/AbstractCreatable.d.ts (line 19 `private _status;`). toolchain/packages/tsconfig/tsconfig.json: "moduleResolution": "NodeNext". actor-kit commit 5299634 "fix: import @ariestools/sdk from the root barrel, not subpaths": "a program mixing an actor-kit package (subpath imports) with a root-importing consumer ... sees two nominally-incompatible AbstractCreatable declarations". `grep -oE 'from "zod[^"]*"' dist/node/index.mjs` returns zod/mini and zod/v4/core. peerDependenciesMeta: {zod:{optional:true}}. Import counts came from grep over each repo's packages/ directory, excluding node_modules and dist.
findings.recommendation: Reverse the guidance. Default to the root barrel `@ariestools/sdk`, which is the ecosystem norm and is required whenever a value or type crosses into actor-kit, cli-kit, browser-kit or sdk-react: AbstractCreatable, BaseEmitter, Creatable params, loggers. Never mix root and subpath imports in one program. Allow subpaths only in isolated leaf bundles that share no SDK class with other packages, and explain why: subpaths are neutral-only while the root is per-platform. In overview.md, say that a root import needs `zod` (^4.6) installed. Add a short 'Class identity' section to modules.md next to `creatable`.

findings.title: Add a Layer-3 skill, `ariestools-sdk-react`, for @ariestools/sdk-react 12.x; React UI work has no skill coverage today
findings.current: absent. No skill mentions @ariestools/sdk-react. In skills/, grep for react/MUI/Storybook finds only toolchain profile, eslint and tsconfig mentions (project-profiles.md:47,51; eslint.md:14,70; typescript.md:9).
findings.truth: sdk-react 12.0.1 publishes 11 packages: the umbrella @ariestools/sdk-react (about 32 subpaths), sdk-react-foundation, -ui, -app, -analytics, -crypto, -identicon, -json-viewer, -motion and -number-status, plus the npm-deprecated compatibility facade sdk-react-core. Peers are react ^19.3, @mui/material ^9.4, react-router ^8.4, ethers ^6.17 (crypto), and the sdk-js packages @ariestools/pixel ^9.0 (analytics) and @ariestools/eth-address ^9.0 (crypto). 16 other workspace repos depend on it. The repo's own AGENTS.md is stale: it describes `@xylabs/react-*` names, yarn, and `cd packages/<name> && yarn xy compile`. The authoritative ownership map lives in packages/sdk/README.md.
findings.evidence: Package manifests: names, versions, peers and export counts come from a node dump of sdk-react/packages/*/package.json. `npm view @ariestools/sdk-react-core deprecated` returns "Use @ariestools/sdk-react-foundation, @ariestools/sdk-react-ui, or a focused feature package...". sdk-react/packages/sdk/README.md has the 'install the smallest owning package' rule and the package ownership list. sdk-react/AGENTS.md:10,15-26,32 contain the stale @xylabs/react-* names and yarn. Dependent repos (grep over workspace package.json files): sdk-xyo-react-js, xyo-chain, xl1-edge-node-api, web-xylabs.com-react, web-elisetrouw.com-react, ariestools, xyo-cash, xl1-protocol, web-xyo.network-react, wallet-xl1-chrome, sdk-os-js, lifehash, crypto-cards, app-portal, app-node, app-explore. 68 *.stories.tsx files are colocated with components.
findings.recommendation: Create `skills/ariestools-sdk-react/` at Layer 3, as a sibling of ariestools-sdk. It builds on xy-toolchain (React profile, eslint-config-react-flat, tsconfig-react) and on ariestools-sdk (root-barrel imports, plus the pixel and eth-address peers). Files: (1) SKILL.md router. (2) overview.md: umbrella vs focused packages (apps may use the umbrella and its subpaths; libraries install the smallest owning package), the peer matrix, Node and React versions. (3) packages.md: the ownership table from packages/sdk/README.md and the subpath catalog. (4) patterns.md: Context.ts + Provider.tsx + useX hook, MUI prop intersection types, useAsyncEffect/usePromise from foundation, ErrorBoundary/ErrorReporter, colocated Storybook stories. (5) migration.md: the @xylabs/react-* and @xylabs/sdk-react to @ariestools/sdk-react-* mapping, and the sdk-react-core deprecation. Add the skill to release-please-config.json extra-files and to the README layer table. Upstream, fix sdk-react/AGENTS.md so it stops contradicting the skill; xy-agent tells agents that a repo's own AGENTS.md wins.

findings.title: Add one Layer-3 skill, `ariestools-actor`, covering actor-kit and its two host kits, cli-kit and browser-kit
findings.current: absent. Nothing in skills/ mentions @ariestools/actor*, provider*, cli-kit or browser-kit. In xyo-skills, only xl1-knowledge/gateway-browser.md:37-42,221 mentions the browser-kit realm adapters, and only in an XL1 context.
findings.truth: actor-kit 2.0.0 publishes actor, actor-model, actor-engine (the single host-agnostic engine), provider and provider-model, plus actor-system, a deprecated alias of actor-engine that maps every ActorSystem* name to ActorEngine*. cli-kit 2.1.0 (cli-kit, -node, -yargs, -daemon) and browser-kit 2.0.0 (browser-kit, -page, -worker, -service-worker, -plugin) are host adapters over that engine. Both still import and peer on the deprecated @ariestools/actor-system: 20 imports, with peers `^1.3 || ^2.0` in browser-kit and `^2.0` in cli-kit. @ariestools/actor-cli is retired and npm-deprecated. ARCHITECTURE.md says runActorOnce, runActorsService and buildCatalogActors 'move to cli-kit', but none of them exists in cli-kit 2.1.0. Usage across the workspace: 24 repos use the actor family, 15 use cli-kit, 6 use browser-kit (dapp-kit, crypto-cards, webble, lifehash, event-kit, xyo-chain and others).
findings.evidence: actor-kit/README.md:3-6 (one Actor base class serves CLI commands via cli-kit, browser webapps, workers, service workers and plugins), :8-10 (the engine is host-agnostic; host kits adapt it and never re-implement it), :21 (actor-system deprecated), :43-46 (actor-cli retired). actor-kit/packages/actor-system/src/index.ts:1-9. actor-kit/ARCHITECTURE.md:267-289. `npm view @ariestools/actor-cli deprecated` returns a deprecation message. `grep -rhoE "from '@ariestools/actor[a-z-]*'" cli-kit/packages browser-kit/packages` returns 20 imports of '@ariestools/actor-system'. Peer ranges are in browser-kit/packages/browser-kit/package.json:73 and cli-kit/packages/cli-kit/package.json:65. Exported APIs confirmed by grep: launchCliSystem, launchCompiledCliSystem, runCliSystemUntilInterrupt, runProcessApplication, runCatalogApplication, configureCliSurface, createSysExitFailureMapper, compileBrowserSystem, launchCompiledBrowserSystem, bindPageLifecycle, bindWorkerShutdown; abstract classes Actor, ProviderActor, AccountProviderActor. Grep for runActorOnce|runActorsService|buildCatalogActors in cli-kit/packages finds nothing. Neither repo declares xy.skills, and actor-kit has no AGENTS.md.
findings.recommendation: Create a single `skills/ariestools-actor/` skill at Layer 3. It depends on ariestools-sdk (AbstractCreatable lifecycle; root-barrel imports are mandatory, see the sdk finding) and xy-toolchain. One skill rather than three, because both host kits are thin facades over actor-engine and would otherwise repeat the engine concepts. Files: (1) SKILL.md router; its description must trigger on actors, providers, CLI process shells/yargs/daemons, and browser page/worker/service-worker/extension realms. (2) overview.md: the package map and dependency edges, SDK 8.1/8.3/9.0 peer qualification, Node 26. (3) actors.md: Actor lifecycle, registerTimer firstRun, readiness, ProviderActor/AccountProviderActor, the locator tiers. (4) providers.md: provider-model/provider, required vs optional dependencies, the deterministic resolver. (5) engine.md: compileActorEngine, launchCompiledActorEngine, launchActorEngine, launchActors, parallel/sequential supervision, boot diagnostics. (6) cli.md: cli-kit core/node/yargs/daemon, the application-shell pattern, the SYS_EXITS ladder, lifehash-indexer as the reference. (7) browser.md: browser-kit and its four realm adapters, compileBrowserSystem/launchCompiledBrowserSystem, keeping security-sensitive extension providers in the background realm. (8) migration.md: actor-system to actor-engine renames; that host kits 2.x still need actor-system as a peer; the actor-cli retirement table, noting its cli-kit replacements are not shipped yet. Keep XL1 specializations (@xyo-network/chain-actor-model, xl1-browser-system) in xyo-skills, and link xl1-knowledge/gateway-browser.md to the new skill. If cli.md grows past about 150 lines, split it into `ariestools-cli`.

findings.title: The toolchain's managed skill catalog leaves out xy-agent, so it cannot be required, declared without a source, or version-checked, and its source is resolved to xyo-skills
findings.current: skills/xy-agent/SKILL.md presents xy-agent as a first-class skill of this pack (released in 0.1.5 and listed in release-please extra-files), but the toolchain catalog does not know it
findings.truth: ARIESTOOLS_SKILLS = ['ariestools-sdk','xy-development','xy-toolchain'] (defaults.ts:13-17). XYO_SKILL_NAMES is built from that list (skillRules.ts:24). As a result: (a) `commands.skillsLint.additionalSkills: ['xy-agent']` throws 'Unknown skills ...' (skillRules.ts:80-96); (b) a package.json `xy.skills: [{name:'xy-agent'}]` is reported as 'needs a source because it is outside the managed catalog' (packageSkills.ts:134-141); (c) xy-agent is never checked for being outdated; (d) skillSourceForName('xy-agent') returns XYOracleNetwork/xyo-skills (defaults.ts:84-86), which has no xy-agent, so versions.ts:8-10 would fetch a URL that does not exist. Only `xy skills defaults` (`--all`) installs it. None of sdk-js, sdk-react, actor-kit, browser-kit, cli-kit or toolchain has xy-agent in skills-lock.json.
findings.evidence: toolchain defaults.ts:3-17, 84-86; skillRules.ts:24, 80-96, 126-128; packageSkills.ts:115-150; versions.ts:8-10. `ls XYOracleNetwork/xyo-skills/skills` shows no xy-agent. The skills-lock.json files in the six repos list only ariestools-sdk, xy-development and xy-toolchain. The unreleased commits on toolchain main (e8bd980d1, 7eb43c3c2) do not touch actions/skills.
findings.recommendation: Add 'xy-agent' to ARIESTOOLS_SKILLS and update the doc comment at defaults.ts:3-5. Add it to SKILL_ORDER after xy-toolchain. Keep it out of TIER_REQUIRED_SKILLS, because it is 'recommended, not required' (xy-agent/SKILL.md:18), but let repos opt in through additionalSkills. Do the same for any new Layer-3 skills (ariestools-sdk-react, ariestools-actor). Pair each with a detection set like ARIESTOOLS_SDK_JS_PACKAGES (detectProfile.ts:26-40) or with xy.skills declarations; otherwise catalog skills get flagged as unnecessary.

findings.title: Skills are not reliably installed in the repos that need them: nothing uses the package.json `xy.skills` declaration, and the skill does not document it
findings.current: commands.md:163 `xy skills lint` | Required project skills, versions...; commands.md:171 "Use `xy skills lint --fix` to install missing profile-required skills". No mention of tier detection, `commands.skillsLint.additionalSkills`, or package.json `xy.skills`.
findings.truth: Since toolchain 10.0.8 (881eede39, 2026-09-25), packages can recommend skills to their consumers through `xy.skills` in package.json. The `skills.package-recommended` rule reads it from workspace packages and direct dependencies, and `--fix` installs what is missing. A skill outside the catalog needs a `source`. Recommended skills are exempt from 'unnecessary' warnings. The only other ways a skill reaches a consumer are tier detection (xy/xyo/xl1) and a hard-coded sdk-js package set. No producing package declares xy.skills: every sdk-js, sdk-react, actor-kit, browser-kit, cli-kit and toolchain manifest shows `xy: undefined`.
findings.evidence: toolchain/docs/xy-config.md (Skills lint section) documents additionalSkills and xy.skills. toolchain packageSkills.ts:295-305; lint.ts:476-495 (recommendedNames are excluded from unnecessary). Running `git tag --contains 881eede39` lists v10.0.8, v10.0.9 and v10.1.0. A node dump of each repo's packages/*/package.json shows `xy: undefined` everywhere. detectProfile.ts:26-40 lists sdk-js packages only.
findings.recommendation: Add a 'How skills reach a repo' subsection to commands.md#skills-and-work-tracking. Cover tier detection, the sdk-js and dapp-kit triggers, `commands.skillsLint.additionalSkills`, and `xy.skills` with its source rule, using the JSON example from xy-config.md. Use this as the waterfall mechanism for Layer 3: each producing package declares its skill. @ariestools/sdk* declares ariestools-sdk; @ariestools/sdk-react* declares ariestools-sdk-react; actor-kit, cli-kit and browser-kit packages declare ariestools-actor with `source: 'ariestools/ariestools-skills'` until the skill is in the toolchain catalog. Then consumers get the right skill from `xy skills lint --fix` with no tier logic needed.

findings.title: xy-agent's repository layout contradicts the toolchain's repo-docs contract and its `xy plan lint` rules, and never mentions `xy plan`
findings.current: structure.md:24 `packages/<pkg>/AGENTS.md delta only`; agents-md.md:91,130-136 recommend nested package AGENTS.md; agents-md.md:110-114 "A symlink works equally well ... ln -s AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md"; auditing.md:32 allows CLAUDE.md to be "an @AGENTS.md import, a symlink, or absent"; structure.md:46 paper names `<PRODUCT>_{WHITE,YELLOW,GREEN,LIGHT}_PAPER.md`; the tree in structure.md:5-27 has no notes/, docs/ROADMAP.md or .xy/plan.json; auditing.md:9 says the checks are "performed by hand today"
findings.truth: The toolchain is the stated reference implementation. Its contract says: (1) "Do not add AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md inside packages". (2) CLAUDE.md must be a regular file containing `@AGENTS.md`; plan lint uses lstat and rejects symlinks. (3) Root CHANGELOG.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and README.md are required. (4) papers/ may contain only README.md, WHITE-PAPER.md, YELLOW-PAPER.md and an optional GREEN-PAPER.md; `--fix` moves every other file, including `<PRODUCT>_WHITE_PAPER.md` and LIGHT papers, into notes/. (5) docs/ROADMAP.md and notes/README.md are required. (6) `.xy/plan.json` is the plan manifest that routes to papers, docs and `xy work`. `xy plan lint`/`init` exist in 10.1.0 (experimental; prefer xyex). `xy repo lint` (stable, part of `xy check`) enforces package READMEs. The `xy agent` command the skill predicts is still only an open work item (XYW-20260901-263436), and `xy plan` (2026-09-08) has since shipped an overlapping layout.
findings.evidence: toolchain/docs/repo-docs.md:16, 22, 37-44; toolchain/docs/plan-manifest.md:89-94, 105; actions/plan/lint.ts:88-90 (`stat.isFile() && !stat.isSymbolicLink()`). `node xy.mjs plan lint --rules` lists 8 rules including plan.papers.unexpected-files and plan.root.claude-imports-agents. `xy.mjs --stability --json` reports plan/plan init/plan lint as experimental and repo as stable. `xy.mjs --help` has no `agent` command. toolchain/.xy/work/items/XYW-20260901-263436.json is still open.
findings.recommendation: Make the toolchain's repo-docs.md and plan-manifest.md the mechanical authority, and have xy-agent defer to them. Drop the symlink and 'absent' options for CLAUDE.md. Either drop nested packages/*/AGENTS.md or state the conflict explicitly and prefer .claude/rules. Adopt the WHITE-PAPER.md / YELLOW-PAPER.md / GREEN-PAPER.md names, and move LIGHT papers and other irregular material to notes/. Add docs/ROADMAP.md, notes/ and .xy/plan.json to the canonical tree. Rewrite auditing.md 'Tooling status' to list what `xyex plan lint` and `xy repo lint` already automate. The xy-agent skill should own guidance on how to use `xy plan`, and xy-toolchain's command catalog should list `plan` with a pointer to xy-agent. Upstream, update XYW-20260901-263436 so the future `xy agent` extends `xy plan` instead of introducing a second layout.

findings.title: `xy work` guidance is split across three places that disagree on whether agents should claim work items
findings.current: xy-toolchain commands.md:185-186 shows `pnpm xy work next --claim` and `pnpm xy work claim <id>` with no caveat. xy-agent auditing.md:109 says ".xy/work/ is a durable backlog, not a live coordination plane ... Queue work there; do not claim work there." toolchain/.agents/skills/xy-work/SKILL.md:22,146-149 says to claim the next item before starting implementation. xy-agent auditing.md:102-103 tells agents to pass an explicit stable id and to suppress the GitHub dual-write per item.
findings.truth: claimItem is a plain overwrite of the item JSON with no lock, lease or compare-and-swap (helpers.ts:56-69), so xy-agent's warning is correct for concurrent worktrees. The CLI has no `--id` or per-item GitHub opt-out on `xy work add`; only the programmatic API takes `id` (work/index.ts:104,171), and dual-write is controlled only by `stores.github.enabled`. `xy work` is experimental: help says "(experimental — prefer xyex)" and the stability catalog reports {name:'work',stability:'experimental'}.
findings.evidence: toolchain/packages/toolchain/src/actions/work/helpers.ts:56-69; work/index.ts:104,171; `node xy.mjs work add --help` shows no --id or --no-github option; `node xy.mjs work --help`; `xy.mjs --stability --json` reports work as experimental. Skill lines are as quoted.
findings.recommendation: Make xy-toolchain commands.md#skills-and-work-tracking the single owner of xy work usage rules. Add the experimental status (`xyex work`), and a concurrency caveat: claim is non-atomic, so use it only in single-agent or single-worktree flows and queue rather than claim across worktrees. Move xy-agent's machine-generated-item rules there, rewritten to match the CLI: use config `stores.github.enabled:false` or the programmatic API for stable ids, since there is no `--id` flag. Then replace auditing.md:100-109 in xy-agent with a short link plus the documentation-specific batching advice.

findings.title: Retire the toolchain repo's unpublished local xy-work skill; keep xy work as a section of xy-toolchain
findings.current: toolchain/.agents/skills/xy-work/SKILL.md (173 lines, metadata.version 0.1.0) is tracked in git but not in skills-lock.json and not symlinked into .claude/skills. Its description says "Use when a user asks Codex...". It does not mention experimental status or xyex.
findings.truth: xy-toolchain already documents xy work in full: commands.md:169-249 and toolchain.md:64. The local file is a fork last edited 2026-07-23 (4ab4fbe3a). It conflicts with xy-agent on claiming and omits the experimental status. Its only unique content is the item-type guidance (lines 165-173) and the core capture rules (lines 12-22).
findings.evidence: `git -C toolchain ls-files .agents/skills/xy-work` returns the SKILL.md. `ls -la toolchain/.claude/skills` shows only the xy-development and xy-toolchain symlinks. toolchain/skills-lock.json has no xy-work. `git log -- .agents/skills/xy-work` shows the latest commit is 4ab4fbe3a (2026-07-23). `node xy.mjs work --help` prints "(experimental — prefer xyex)".
findings.recommendation: Decision for xy work tracking: keep it as a section of xy-toolchain (Layer 2), not a new skill. Fold the item-type guidance and the 'prefer a work item over free-form TODO markdown' rule into commands.md#skills-and-work-tracking, then delete the toolchain-local skill or reduce it to a redirect stub. Revisit a separate `xy-work` Layer-2 skill only if the xy-toolchain description budget (see the separate finding) forces a split.

findings.title: xy-toolchain's description is 958 characters, close to the 1024-character Agent Skills limit, and the validator does not check length
findings.current: SKILL.md:3 description is 958 characters and lists features in detail ("with optional GitHub Issues dual-write/sync and multi-folder workspace scope, and configurable clean (including --full hygiene)").
findings.truth: The pending xy-toolchain additions (xy vs xyex stability per toolchain/docs/SKILLS-FOLLOWUP.md, plus `xy plan` and the xy.skills distribution) will push it past the limit. scripts/validate-skills.mjs checks only that `name` and `description` exist.
findings.evidence: A node measurement of each SKILL.md `description:` line gives xy-toolchain 958, xy-agent 681, ariestools-sdk 545, xy-development 198. scripts/validate-skills.mjs:11 has `REQUIRED_FIELDS = ['name', 'description']` and no length check.
findings.recommendation: Trim the description to trigger terms only: xy CLI, build/lint/test, configs, deplint, publint, policy, skills, work. Move feature detail into the router body. Add a `description.length <= 1024` error (and perhaps a warning at 900) to validate-skills.mjs.

findings.title: "Layer N" means two different things across the pack, and the Definition of Done never points to the xy-toolchain gates
findings.current: workflow.md:116-118 defines DoD layers: 1 generic, 2 domain, 3 PRD. SKILL.md:25 and testing.md:3 call xy-toolchain "Layer 2". README.md:9-13 and CLAUDE.md:29-33 number the skill stack 1/2/3. workflow.md:68,73,81 give `pnpm build` / `pnpm lint` / `pnpm test` as the gates.
findings.truth: Downstream xyo-skills relies on the DoD meaning: xl1-build/SKILL.md:157 "### Layer 2 — Domain DoD" and xl1-scaffold/SKILL.md:245. In XY repos the generic gates are actually `pnpm xy build` (compile, publint, deplint, lint) and `pnpm xy test`, plus `xy check` where CI requires it (xy-toolchain commands.md:31-42). The DoD does not link there.
findings.evidence: grep -n 'Layer [0-9]' across skills/, README.md and CLAUDE.md; xyo-skills/skills/xl1-build/SKILL.md:152-157; xl1-scaffold/SKILL.md:243-245. The anchors xyo-skills links into (#applying-the-definition-of-done, #definition-of-done, #writing-project-specific-acceptance-criteria) all resolve today.
findings.recommendation: Keep the DoD 'Layer 1/2/3' wording, since xyo-skills depends on it and its anchors must stay stable. Rename the skill-stack levels to 'Tier 1/2/3' or 'base/toolchain/library' in the README, CLAUDE.md, SKILL.md:25 and testing.md:3. In DoD Layer 1, add one line: 'In @ariestools/toolchain repos these gates are xy-toolchain's lifecycle gates', linking to ../xy-toolchain/commands.md#lifecycle-gates.

findings.title: Keep the name `ariestools-sdk`, but state its scope (sdk-js only) and point to the React and actor skills
findings.current: SKILL.md:3 "utility libraries from the sdk-js monorepo". It has no 'not covered' statement, no Related-skills section, and no Authority line, unlike the other three skills. packages.md:3 says "(or closely related Aries Tools packages)".
findings.truth: The name is wired into the toolchain: lint.ts:108-110 gives the reason 'repo uses packages from ariestools/sdk-js'; detectProfile.ts:21-40 defines ARIESTOOLS_SDK_JS_PACKAGES; skillRules.ts:28-39 has SKILL_ORDER. The skills-lock.json files of sdk-js, sdk-react, actor-kit and browser-kit pin it. Renaming it to sdk-js would break all of those. sdk-react gets ariestools-sdk installed because it depends on @ariestools/sdk, but that skill says nothing about @ariestools/sdk-react*. No sdk-js package moved to actor-kit or cli-kit, and the skill mentions none.
findings.evidence: toolchain lint.ts:108-110; detectProfile.ts:26-40; sdk-react/skills-lock.json contains "ariestools-sdk"; grep for 'actor|cli-kit|browser-kit|react' in skills/ariestools-sdk returns only `creatable` (modules.md:29); `ls sdk-js/packages` shows 13 packages, all still present.
findings.recommendation: Keep the skill name. Add a scope line to the description and body: 'sdk-js packages only; for @ariestools/sdk-react* use ariestools-sdk-react; for actor/provider/cli-kit/browser-kit use ariestools-actor'. Add a Related-skills section and the standard Authority line. Remove the vague "closely related Aries Tools packages" from packages.md:3.

findings.title: The peer-pin example pins MUI 7, two majors behind what the house React SDK requires
findings.current: workflow.md:35 "(e.g., `pnpm add @mui/material@~7.3.9`)"
findings.truth: @mui/material latest is 9.4.0, and every MUI-dependent @ariestools/sdk-react-* 12.0.1 package declares the peer `@mui/material: ^9.4`. An agent copying the example into an sdk-react consumer creates a peer conflict.
findings.evidence: `npm view @mui/material dist-tags` shows latest 9.4.0 and latest-v7 7.3.11. The sdk-react peers dump shows '@mui/material':'^9.4' for analytics, app, crypto, foundation, motion, number-status and ui.
findings.recommendation: Use a version-neutral example (`pnpm add <peer>@<range from the dependency's peerDependencies>`), or update it to `@mui/material@^9.4`.
